# Zivogift — Setup & Deployment Guide (v8, current architecture)

Stack: static frontend (no build step) + Netlify Functions backend + Supabase
(DB/auth) + Cashfree (payments) + Resend (email) + Meta WhatsApp Cloud API
(messaging) + Cloudflare R2 (generated images/videos) + Google Gemini API (AI
generation, content moderation, safety guardrails — switched from Anthropic
in Jul 2026, see section 6). Follow this in order — each step unlocks the
next.

> This replaces the older SendGrid/AiSensy instructions from earlier builds.
> The codebase migrated to Resend + Meta WhatsApp Cloud API directly.

---

## 0. Before you touch anything: rotate exposed keys

If you ever had real credentials sitting in `.env.example` or committed to a
repo, rotate them now (Supabase service role key, Resend key, Cashfree keys,
Gemini key). `.env.example` should only ever contain placeholder text —
real values live in Netlify's environment variables UI, never in a file that
gets committed.

---

## 1. Supabase (database + auth)

1. Create a project at supabase.com.
2. **SQL Editor → New query** — run these files **in this exact order**
   (each is idempotent, safe to re-run):
   1. `supabase/schema.sql` (base schema — tables, RLS policies, seed catalog)
   2. `supabase/schema-group2.sql`
   3. `supabase/schema-group3.sql`
   4. `supabase/schema-group4.sql`
   5. `supabase/schema-group4-part2.sql`
   6. `supabase/schema-group5.sql`
   7. `supabase/schema-sender-otp-msg91.sql` — sender SMS OTP verification (required for every digital order, text or media). Supersedes `schema-sender-otp.sql` — don't run that one.
   8. `supabase/schema-share-clip.sql` — Share Clip video jobs + `recipient_photo_url` column
   9. `supabase/schema-care-package.sql` — Care Package feature (New Parent pack) + its product catalog entry
   10. `supabase/schema-scheduler-hardening.sql` — retry-attempts tracking for `gift-scheduler.js`
   11. `supabase/schema-webhook-replay-protection.sql` — Cashfree webhook replay-dedup table
   12. `supabase/schema-fix-track-order-leak.sql` — closes a `sender_phone`/`sender_name` leak in the `track_order()` RPC (was reachable via the public anon key — see file comment for detail)
   13. `supabase/schema-fix-orders-ref-column.sql` — adds the `orders.ref` column that `create-cashfree-order.js` writes to on every order. Run this even if you already ran files 1–12 on an older deploy; the earlier version of `schema.sql` had a comment about this column but never actually created it, which breaks every checkout with a Postgres "schema cache" error until this runs.

   **13 files total.** If you're re-running this on an environment that
   already had files 1–6 applied from an earlier build, you only need 7–13 —
   but running the full sequence is always safe (every file is idempotent).
3. **Project Settings → API** → copy:
   - `Project URL` → `js/config.js` as `SUPABASE_URL`, and Netlify env as `SUPABASE_URL`
   - `anon public` key → `js/config.js` as `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, and Netlify env as `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
   - `service_role` key (**secret**) → Netlify env only, as `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — never in `config.js`, never committed
4. **Authentication → Providers** → confirm Email is enabled. You can turn off
   email confirmation in Authentication → Settings for faster testing.
5. **Authentication → URL Configuration** → set:
   - **Site URL** to `https://zivogift.com` (not the `localhost:3000` default —
     leaving this unchanged is why signup-confirmation and password-reset
     emails land on a "localhost refused to connect" page instead of your
     real site).
   - **Redirect URLs** → add `https://zivogift.com/reset-password.html`
     (needed for the Forgot Password flow — `auth.resetPasswordForEmail()`
     in `js/auth.js` sends people here, and Supabase will silently reject
     the redirect if it isn't on this allow-list).
6. Edit `js/config.js` and fill in the real `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`.

### Make yourself an admin
1. Sign up on your live site (or via Supabase Auth UI) with your own email.
2. In Supabase SQL Editor:
   ```sql
   update public.profiles set is_admin = true
   where id = (select id from auth.users where email = 'you@example.com');
   ```
3. Log in and visit `/admin.html`.

## 2. Cashfree (payments)

1. Sign up at cashfree.com → Payment Gateway. Start in **sandbox** mode.
2. **Developers → API Keys** → copy `App ID` / `Secret Key` → Netlify env as
   `CASHFREE_APP_ID` / `CASHFREE_SECRET_KEY`.
3. Netlify env: `CASHFREE_ENV=sandbox` while testing → `production` when live.
4. **Developers → Webhooks** → add:
   `https://YOUR-SITE.netlify.app/.netlify/functions/cashfree-webhook`
   Subscribe to `PAYMENT_SUCCESS_WEBHOOK` and `PAYMENT_FAILED_WEBHOOK`.
   Copy the **Webhook Secret** → Netlify env as `CASHFREE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
   (This secret backs a real HMAC-SHA256 signature check in
   `cashfree-webhook.js` — every webhook is verified before it's trusted,
   and already-processed orders are never double-processed on a retry.)
5. Sandbox test card/UPI details are in Cashfree's docs.

## 3. Resend (order + notification emails)

1. Sign up at resend.com (free tier: 3,000 emails/month).
2. **Domains** → verify your sending domain (or use a Resend test address
   while developing).
3. **API Keys → Create API Key** → Netlify env as `RESEND_API_KEY`.
4. Netlify env: `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` (verified sender), `RESEND_FROM_NAME`,
   and `ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL` (your own inbox). This address receives:
   - New-order alerts
   - **Gift delivery failure alerts** — if a WhatsApp/email send fails
     repeatedly (`gift-scheduler.js` retries up to 4 times before giving
     up), you get emailed once, with the recipient/sender/order details,
     so a stuck gift doesn't silently vanish. Don't skip setting this.

## 4. Meta WhatsApp Cloud API (gift delivery, reminders, OTP, care packages)

No AiSensy middleman — this goes direct to Meta. ~20 minutes for setup, plus
however long Meta takes to approve your templates (see below — budget real
time for this, it's not instant and not guaranteed).

1. developers.facebook.com → My Apps → Create App → **Business** type.
2. Add the **WhatsApp** product to the app.
3. WhatsApp → Getting Started → note the test Phone Number ID (fine for dev).
   For production: WhatsApp → Phone Numbers → Add a Production Number.
4. Generate a permanent System User token:
   business.facebook.com → Settings → System Users → Add → Admin role →
   Generate Token → select your WhatsApp app → permissions:
   `whatsapp_business_messaging`, `whatsapp_business_management`.
   → Netlify env: `WHATSAPP_TOKEN`
5. Netlify env: `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID` = your Phone Number ID (numbers only).
6. **Approve twelve message templates** in Meta Business Manager → WhatsApp
   Manager → Message Templates. Use category **UTILITY** where possible
   (cheaper, faster approval, ~₹0.145/msg, no monthly fee) — AUTHENTICATION
   category for the OTP template specifically usually approves fastest but
   only allows the fixed code+button format, not custom wording.

   | Netlify env var | Template name | Configurable? |
   |---|---|---|
   | `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_NAME` | `zivogift_birthday_surprise` | env var |
   | — | `gift_delivered_sender_notify` | ⚠️ hardcoded in `gift-scheduler.js` |
   | `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_OPENED` | `gift_opened_sender_notify` | env var |
   | `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_REPLY_RECEIVED` | `gift_reply_received` | env var |
   | `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_REACTION_INVITE` | `squad_reaction_invite` | env var |
   | `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_OCCASION_NUDGE` | `zg_occasion_nudge` | env var |
   | — | `zg_birthday_reminder` | ⚠️ hardcoded in `reminder-scheduler.js` |
   | — | `zg_anniversary_nudge` | ⚠️ hardcoded in `reminder-scheduler.js` |
   | — | `zg_condition_gift_instructions` | ⚠️ hardcoded in `_lib/digitalSendsHelper.js` |
   | `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_CARE_DAILY` | `zg_care_package_daily` | env var |
   | `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_CARE_COMPLETE` | `zg_care_package_complete` | env var |

   The four marked ⚠️ are hardcoded template names, not read from an env
   var — renaming any of those later needs a code change, not just an env
   var edit. Not a launch blocker (Meta approval works the same either way),
   just worth knowing before you assume changing one is a config-only change.

   `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_CARE_DAILY` uses a single large free-text body
   variable — Meta sometimes rejects templates that are almost entirely one
   free-text placeholder as a way to dodge content review. **Submit this
   one first and don't assume approval** — if it gets rejected, Care
   Package delivery is blocked until you resolve it.

   Meta approval typically takes 1–2 business days — submit these early
   so they're ready by the time you're testing end-to-end.

   Sender phone verification is **not** sent via WhatsApp — new WABAs
   can't get an AUTHENTICATION-category template approved (Meta requires
   1,000+ business-initiated conversations/day on the number first), and
   OTP content submitted under UTILITY gets auto-rejected as a category
   mismatch. See the MSG91 setup section below instead.

## MSG91 SMS OTP setup (sender phone verification)

**Second correction to this section — the first one was also wrong.**
An earlier version said MSG91's raw SendOTP API has a free default
template usable without DLT. MSG91's own support team clarified that's
not quite right: that default template still requires your DLT Entity ID
to be mapped in the MSG91 panel. If you don't have that yet, the raw
SendOTP API genuinely won't work for you.

**What actually works pre-DLT/pre-GST: the MSG91 OTP Widget** — a
different product, with its own default template that has no such
requirement. This is confirmed working (tested end-to-end, real OTP
delivered) and is what `verify-sender-otp.js` / `_lib/msg91.js` /
`checkout.html` / `js/checkout.js` are wired for now. The Widget runs
almost entirely client-side (MSG91 handles OTP generation, sending, and
first-pass verification in the browser); the server only independently
re-confirms the resulting access-token with MSG91 before trusting it —
never the raw OTP code itself.

**Setup:**
1. Sign up at msg91.com — no GST required.
2. Dashboard → **OTP → Widgets** → **Create New Widget**. Name it, choose
   Mobile Number as the contact point, SMS as the primary channel, pick an
   OTP length. On the template step, MSG91 auto-assigns its default
   template — no DLT/documents needed. Save through to the end.
3. Dashboard → **OTP → Widgets → your widget → Integration** tab. Under
   **"1. Client Side Integration"**, the `widgetId` is in the URL/page and
   the `tokenAuth` comes from the **Select Token** dropdown (Tokens →
   Create New Token if you don't have one yet — this is a widget-scoped
   token, not your main Authkey, and is safe to expose in browser code by
   design). Put both into `js/config.js`:
   `MSG91_WIDGET_ID` and `MSG91_WIDGET_TOKEN_AUTH`.
4. Dashboard → **API/Authkey** (top-right or username dropdown) → copy
   your account Authkey → Netlify env: `MSG91_AUTH_KEY`. This one *is* a
   real secret, server-side only — it's what `verify-sender-otp.js` uses
   to independently confirm a widget access-token with MSG91 before
   issuing our own verification token.
5. **Test the full loop before trusting it for real orders**: open
   checkout, send yourself a code, verify it, confirm the order actually
   goes through. Test against a couple of different carriers if you can
   (Jio/Airtel/Vi) — a shared/default-template route can behave
   differently carrier to carrier.

**Confirmed:** the `verifyAccessToken()` endpoint, payload shape, and
headers in `_lib/msg91.js` are verified directly against the actual
"2. Server Side Integration" tab for this widget — `POST
https://control.msg91.com/api/v5/widget/verifyAccessToken` with
`{authkey, "access-token"}` and `Content-Type`/`Accept: application/json`
headers. The one thing that wasn't shown in that snippet is the exact
response *body* shape on success/failure — `_lib/msg91.js` assumes
MSG91's usual `{type: 'success'|'error', ...}` convention. If real
verification attempts unexpectedly fail, check the logged response body
first before assuming the OTP itself is wrong.

Tradeoffs worth knowing: the SMS is unbranded (MSG91's generic wording,
not "Zivogift"), and deliverability on a shared/default template is
generally a notch below a fully DLT-registered branded one.

**Once you've registered the business (GST + DLT) later**, you can
either keep using the Widget (create a custom template inside the same
widget, now DLT-backed) or switch to the raw SendOTP API path
(`_lib/msg91.js`'s `sendOtp`/`verifyOtp` — currently unused, kept for
this purpose) for a fully branded flow. Either way nothing else in the
codebase needs to change.

Cost: pay-per-SMS (~₹0.15–0.25/SMS on MSG91's standard transactional
rate), no subscription.

Run `supabase/schema-sender-otp-msg91.sql` in the Supabase SQL editor (it
creates `sender_phone_otp_sends`, `sender_phone_otp_verify_attempts`, and
`sender_verification_tokens`, and drops the old WhatsApp-era
`sender_phone_otps` table). This replaces the older
`supabase/schema-sender-otp.sql` — don't run that one anymore.
7. Once you have a production number, register the inbound webhook:
   Meta Developer Console → WhatsApp → Configuration → Webhook →
   `https://YOUR-SITE.netlify.app/.netlify/functions/whatsapp-webhook`
   (this powers Condition-Based Delivery keyword replies, and Care Package
   PAUSE/RESUME — a recipient texting either keyword pauses/resumes their
   own message sequence).
8. Meta Developer Console → App Dashboard → Settings → Basic → copy
   **App Secret** → Netlify env `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET`. Required: without
   it, `whatsapp-webhook.js` rejects every inbound POST outright rather
   than trusting an unverified sender, since Meta signs every webhook
   request with this secret and there's no other way to confirm a POST to
   that URL actually came from Meta and not from anyone who found it.

---

## 5. Cloudflare R2 (generated card images, share-clip videos, uploaded media)

1. Cloudflare Dashboard → R2 → create a bucket (e.g. `zivogift-cards`).
2. Bucket → Settings → enable **Public Access**, copy the public URL →
   Netlify env `R2_PUBLIC_URL`.
3. R2 → Manage API Tokens → create a token with read/write **and delete**
   permissions on the bucket → Netlify env `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` /
   `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. (Delete permission matters: oversized uploads
   that fail server-side size validation get actually deleted from R2, not
   just rejected — see `_lib/mediaSizeGuard.js`.)
4. Netlify env: `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `R2_BUCKET_NAME`.
5. **Optional but recommended** — malware scanning for uploaded media:
   virustotal.com → sign up (free) → API Key → Netlify env
   `VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY`. Without this set, `_lib/mediaSizeGuard.js` still
   runs magic-byte content validation and, for images, a full decode/
   re-encode via `sharp` on every upload — those two don't need the key —
   but the virus-scan step is skipped (and logged as skipped, not silently
   treated as clean) until you add it. Free tier is rate-limited but fine
   at low order volume.

---

## 6. Gemini API (AI generation, content moderation, safety checks)

Switched from Anthropic to Google Gemini in Jul 2026 — the Anthropic account
this project used ran out of billing credit and wasn't topped up, so
`_lib/anthropicHelper.js` now calls Gemini instead (filename kept as-is so
every file that `require()`s it didn't need to change). Gemini's free tier
covers this comfortably: no card required, ~1,500 requests/day on
gemini-2.5-flash as of writing.

No longer optional-only — still gracefully degrades for the original two
features, but now also backs real safety enforcement.

1. aistudio.google.com/apikey → sign in with a Google account → Create API key.
2. Netlify env: `GEMINI_API_KEY`. (Remove `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` if it's still
   set from before — it's no longer read by anything.)
3. What breaks without it:
   - Note Story Card + Numerology features fall back to a static template
     (safe to launch without, same as before).
   - **Message content moderation** (`_lib/moderateMessage.js`) fails OPEN
     without a key — messages go through unchecked rather than blocking
     checkout. Fine for availability, but means the abuse filter isn't
     actually protecting anything until this key is set.
   - **Care Package generation** cannot run at all without this key — no
     fallback, orders will sit stuck in `pending_generation`.
   - **Care Package content guardrail** fails CLOSED without a key —
     content gets flagged for manual review rather than silently sent, so
     this direction is safe, just means nothing sends until the key exists.

---

## 7. Deploy to Netlify

1. Push the project to a GitHub/GitLab repo. **Double-check `.env.example`
   has no real secrets in it before this push** — it's a template only.
2. Netlify → **Add new site → Import an existing project** → pick the repo.
   Build command and publish directory are already set in `netlify.toml`.
3. **Site configuration → Environment variables** → add every variable from
   `.env.example` with your real values, plus `SITE_URL` set to your final
   domain (e.g. `https://zivogift.com`).
4. Trigger a deploy. Netlify installs function dependencies automatically
   from `package.json`: `@supabase/supabase-js`, `@aws-sdk/client-s3`,
   `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner`, `sharp`, `ffmpeg-static`, `pdfkit`.
5. Confirm all **seven** scheduled functions are running in **Netlify →
   Functions** logs — a missing one here means a whole feature silently
   doesn't work, not just a slow one:
   - `gift-scheduler` — every 2 min (fires pending digital gift sends; now
     retries a failed send up to 4 times before giving up and emailing
     `ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL`)
   - `clip-scheduler` — every 2 min (renders + sends Share Clip videos)
   - `care-package-generator` — every 2 min (generates the message sequence
     for newly-paid Care Package orders)
   - `care-package-guardrail` — every 2 min (safety-checks generated Care
     Package content — deliberately separate tick from generation)
   - `care-package-scheduler` — every 2 min (sends due Care Package
     messages; skips paused sequences; notifies sender on completion)
   - `reminder-scheduler` — daily at 07:30 IST / 02:00 UTC (birthdays,
     anniversaries)
   - `occasion-scheduler` — daily at 08:00 IST / 02:30 UTC (college-calendar
     nudges)

---

## 8. Point your Hostinger domain at Netlify

1. Netlify → **Domain management → Add a domain** → enter your Hostinger-owned domain.
2. Netlify gives you DNS records (usually an `A` record + `CNAME` for `www`).
3. Hostinger → **Domains → DNS / Name Servers → DNS Zone Editor** → add/edit
   those records.
4. DNS can take up to 24–48 hours to propagate (often faster). Netlify
   auto-provisions free SSL once the domain resolves.
5. Once live, update the Cashfree webhook URL and any sender-domain settings
   in Resend to use your real domain instead of `.netlify.app`.
6. Set `WHATSAPP_NUMBER` in `js/config.js` to your real business number.

## 9. Go-live checklist

**Original core flow:**
- [ ] Full test order in Cashfree **sandbox**: order lands in Supabase
      `orders` as `paid`, confirmation email arrives via Resend, admin
      notification email arrives, order shows on `/account.html` and
      `/order-status.html`.
- [ ] Digital gift with "send right now" completes and the WhatsApp message
      arrives within ~2 minutes (confirms `gift-scheduler` + WhatsApp
      templates are wired correctly).
- [ ] Log into `/admin.html`, change an order's status, confirm the
      customer status-update email sends.
- [ ] Edit a price in `/admin.html` → Catalog tab, confirm it updates live
      on the homepage.
- [ ] Toggle a product's **Active** checkbox off in `/admin.html` → Catalog,
      confirm its card actually disappears from the digital-studio type
      picker (not just blocked at checkout — the picker now checks this live).

**Security/hardening added since the original build:**
- [ ] Try placing a digital gift order without completing WhatsApp OTP
      verification — confirm it's rejected server-side (not just hidden
      in the UI).
- [ ] Try submitting an obviously abusive message on a digital gift —
      confirm it's rejected with `MESSAGE_BLOCKED` (requires
      `GEMINI_API_KEY` to be set — see section 6).
- [ ] Try uploading an oversized photo directly via the presigned URL
      (bypassing the client's 8MB check) — confirm the order is rejected
      with `MEDIA_TOO_LARGE` and the file is actually deleted from R2.
- [ ] Confirm all **twelve** WhatsApp templates show **Approved** in Meta
      Business Manager — especially `zg_sender_otp_verification` and
      `zg_care_package_daily`, which carry real rejection risk (see
      section 4).

**Newer features:**
- [ ] Full Share Clip test: complete a digital gift, tap "Download & Share"
      on the recipient's `gift.html` page, confirm the video generates and
      plays.
- [ ] Full Care Package test: order the New Parent pack with the
      `ZIVOTEST100` (or equivalent 100%-off) promo code, confirm
      `care-package-generator` produces 14 messages, `care-package-guardrail`
      checks them, and the first message sends on schedule. Text `PAUSE`
      from the recipient number, confirm the sequence stops; text `RESUME`,
      confirm it starts again.
- [ ] Force a WhatsApp send failure (e.g. temporarily break
      `WHATSAPP_TOKEN`) and confirm `ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL` receives the
      failure alert after `gift-scheduler` gives up retrying.

**Final production switchover:**
- [ ] Switch `CASHFREE_ENV` to `production` with live keys, update the
      Cashfree webhook URL to the production endpoint.
- [ ] Switch WhatsApp to your production phone number if you started on the
      test number.
- [ ] Re-test one real, small order end-to-end with a real card/UPI.
- [ ] Review `privacy-policy.html` and `refund-policy.html` — solid drafts,
      not a substitute for actual legal review once handling real money at
      scale. There is currently no separate Terms of Use / Acceptable Use
      Policy page — worth a real lawyer's input given user-generated content
      and the abuse-prevention work already in place.
- [ ] Confirm R2 bucket is publicly readable (generated card images and
      share-clip videos load).

  _lib/mediaValidation.js         Magic-byte signatures, sharp re-encode, VirusTotal hook — used by mediaSizeGuard.js
  _lib/msg91.js                   MSG91 SMS OTP send/verify — used by send-sender-otp.js / verify-sender-otp.js
  _lib/clipFrames.js              Share Clip frame rendering + ffmpeg MP4 encoding
  _lib/phoneUtil.js               Phone number normalization (shared by OTP + Care Package)
  _lib/                       Shared Supabase/Cashfree/Resend/WhatsApp/R2 helpers

supabase/
  schema.sql                       Base schema, RLS policies, seed catalog
  schema-group2.sql … group5.sql   Sequential additive migrations — run in order
  schema-sender-otp.sql            SUPERSEDED — do not run, see schema-sender-otp-msg91.sql
  schema-sender-otp-msg91.sql      Sender SMS (MSG91) OTP verification

/* ============================================================================
   ZIVOGIFT · REVEAL PLUS — reveal-plus.css   (v2)
   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Purely-additive visual upgrade for gift.html. Loaded AFTER the inline
   <style>, so these rules win. No markup changes required.

   v2 focus (from live feedback):
     • THE PERSONAL MESSAGE IS THE HERO. In the live build it was rendering as
       tiny text squeezed between the sealed hint and the Skip dots. It is now
       forced into a large, centred, glowing quote card that sits above
       everything else — impossible to miss.
     • MEME GIFTS GET PERSONALITY. A "fun" layer (driven by reveal-plus.js)
       drops tilted sticky-note memes + emoji around the message, all tinted
       with the vibe accent the sender chose.
     • Everything disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
   ============================================================================ */

/* ── MOBILE ── */
/* BUGFIX: this used to be TWO separate @media (max-width: 860px) blocks for
   #studio-preview — one setting display:none, a second (added later) setting
   display:flex right after it. CSS cascade always resolves to the LAST rule
   for equal specificity, so the display:none never actually applied; the
   preview panel (a phone-mockup, with an animated confetti/particle layer)
   was rendering on every mobile screen, nested inside an already-phone-sized
   viewport. That's the flicker + stray dots reported on mobile — the
   particle animation kicking in on load for a panel that was supposed to be
   hidden. Consolidated into one block, correctly hidden on mobile: a
   phone-frame preview of a phone doesn't add anything when you're already
   looking at your phone, and hiding it removes the wasted vertical space
   and the animation-driven layout shift. */
@media (max-width: 860px) {
  #studio-wrap {
    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
    max-width: 100vw;
  }
  #studio-preview {
    display: none;
  }
  #studio-builder {
    max-height: none;
    position: static;
    padding: 28px 20px 80px;
  }
  #studio-progress {
    right: 0;
    padding: 0 20px;
  }
}



/* ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   (A) MOBILE ACTION-BUTTON VISIBILITY / OVERFLOW
   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   On phones the studio's Next / Add-to-Cart buttons could sit below the fold
   or get clipped by tight bottom padding. These rules guarantee every step's
   primary action stays reachable: generous safe-area bottom padding on the
   scroll container, full-width tap-friendly buttons, and no clipping.
   ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
@media (max-width: 860px) {
  #studio-builder{
    /* Room so the last button clears the phone's home-indicator / nav bar. */
    padding-bottom: calc(96px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
    overflow-x: hidden;               /* stop side-scroll from wide rows */
  }
  .studio-step{ overflow: visible; }  /* never clip an action button */
  .studio-next-btn, .studio-add-btn{
    min-height: 54px;
    font-size: 16px;
    margin-top: 20px;
    margin-bottom: 8px;
    width: 100%;
  }
  /* Two-button rows (e.g. Re-record / Use) keep buttons full-height & wrap
     cleanly instead of squeezing off-screen. */
  .studio-next-btn{ box-sizing: border-box; }
}

/* Extra-small phones: make sure long button labels wrap rather than overflow. */
@media (max-width: 400px) {
  .studio-next-btn, .studio-add-btn{
    white-space: normal;
    line-height: 1.25;
    padding: 15px 14px;
  }
}

# Campaign Center · Emergency Console · Export Center · Festival Automation

**Deploy guide — ZivoGift**

---

## 0. The one thing to do first (it is not code)

Submit a **MARKETING** WhatsApp template to Meta. Approval takes hours to days and
is entirely outside my control and yours. Email campaigns work without it.

**Meta Business Manager → WhatsApp → Message Templates → Create**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `zg_promo_broadcast` |
| Category | **Marketing** (not Utility — Meta rejects promos on Utility) |
| Language | English |

**Body:**

```
Hey {{1}} 👋
{{2}}
Tap below to see what's new on Zivogift.
```

**Footer:** `Reply STOP to opt out`
**Button:** Visit website → `https://zivogift.com`

The code reads your live template list from Meta on every page load, so the
moment it is approved it appears in the Campaigns dropdown — **no redeploy.**

Any approved MARKETING template with exactly **2 body variables**
(`{{1}}` = first name, `{{2}}` = message) works unchanged.

---

## 1. Run the migration

Supabase Dashboard → SQL Editor → New query → paste the whole file → Run.

```
supabase/consolidated/60_campaigns_and_admin_ops.sql
```

Additive and idempotent — safe to re-run. Creates:

| Object | What it is |
|---|---|
| `v_customers` | View. Your deduped customer list, derived from `orders` |
| `marketing_optouts` | The suppression list |
| `campaigns` | One row per broadcast |
| `campaign_recipients` | One row per individual message + delivery receipt |
| `admin_settings` | Kill switches (DB-backed, no deploy to flip) |
| `festival_schedules` | 7 festivals, seeded **inactive** |

Verify:

```sql
select count(*) as customers,
       count(*) filter (where paid_orders_count > 0) as paying,
       count(*) filter (where email is not null and not opted_out) as emailable
from public.v_customers;
```

If `customers` is 0 but you have orders, `contact_email` and `contact_phone`
are both empty on those rows — tell me and I will adjust the view.

---

## 2. Set two environment variables

Netlify → Site configuration → Environment variables.

| Variable | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET` | any long random string | Signs unsubscribe links. **Never change it** once live — old links would break |
| `ADMIN_EMAILS` | your admin email | Some functions already require it and **fail closed** without it |

`ADMIN_EMAILS` is belt-and-braces: the new `_lib/adminAuth.js` also accepts
`profiles.is_admin = true`, so you are not locked out if you forget. If you do
get a 403, it now tells you exactly why instead of saying `forbidden`.

---

## 3. Deploy the files

Drop the ZIP contents into your repo at the same paths and deploy.

### New files (13)

```
supabase/consolidated/60_campaigns_and_admin_ops.sql
netlify/functions/_lib/adminAuth.js
netlify/functions/_lib/audience.js
netlify/functions/_lib/adminSettings.js
netlify/functions/_lib/unsubToken.js
netlify/functions/_lib/campaignEmail.js
netlify/functions/admin-campaigns.js
netlify/functions/campaign-sender.js
netlify/functions/admin-ops.js
netlify/functions/admin-export.js
netlify/functions/festival-scheduler.js
netlify/functions/unsubscribe.js
js/admin-campaigns.js
js/admin-ops.js
```

### Modified files (4) — overwrite

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `admin.html` | Two new tabs + panels + script tags |
| `netlify.toml` | Two new cron entries |
| `netlify/functions/_lib/resend.js` | `sendEmail()` gained an **optional** `headers` param. Every existing caller is unaffected |
| `netlify/functions/whatsapp-webhook.js` | Campaign delivery receipts + `STOP` records a marketing opt-out |

### Verification scripts (optional, not deployed)

```
scripts/verify-campaigns.js    → node scripts/verify-campaigns.js
scripts/verify-sender.js       → node scripts/verify-sender.js
```

No new npm dependencies. `package.json` is unchanged.

---

## 4. First run — in this order

1. **Admin → 🚨 Emergency.** Everything should be green. Red rows under
   *Database objects* mean the migration did not run.
2. Tap **Test email**. Check inbox *and* spam.
3. Tap **Test WhatsApp** with your own number.
4. **Admin → 📢 Campaigns.** Pick *Paid customers only* → **Preview audience**.
   Confirm the count looks like your real customer base.
5. Write a short message → **Send test to me**. Read it on your phone.
6. Only then → **Launch**. You must type `SEND`.

---

## 5. How sending actually works

Launch **queues**; it does not send. `campaign-sender` drains the queue.

- Every **5 minutes**, **20 messages** per run = **240/hour**
- A 1,000-person campaign takes about **4 hours**

The slow ramp is deliberate. Your domain has only ever sent transactional
mail; a sudden 1,000-message spike is the classic trigger for Gmail
throttling.

**To stop a campaign mid-flight:** Emergency tab → *Pause marketing campaigns*.
Takes effect on the next tick. Do **not** comment out the cron — that needs a
deploy.

---

## 6. Credit cost

| Function | Schedule | Invocations/day |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign-sender` | `*/5 * * * *` | 288 |
| `festival-scheduler` | `0 3 * * *` | 1 |

`campaign-sender` early-exits on a single indexed query when nothing is
queued — the normal state. Having this installed costs close to nothing when
you are not running a campaign.

---

## 7. Festival automation

Seeded **inactive**. Nothing auto-sends until you switch one on.

⚠️ **Holi, Raksha Bandhan and Diwali follow the lunar calendar and move every
year.** The seeded dates are placeholders. Correct them each year — it is two
number fields, editable from your phone.

Each festival fires once per year (`last_fired_year` guard), creates a normal
campaign row, and is visible and cancellable in the Campaigns tab before
`campaign-sender` reaches it.

---

## 8. Compliance — read this once

Your codebase previously had **no unsubscribe concept anywhere**. It does now:

- Every marketing email carries a visible unsubscribe link **and**
  `List-Unsubscribe` / `List-Unsubscribe-Post` headers (Gmail and Yahoo
  require these for bulk senders)
- `STOP` / `UNSUBSCRIBE` on WhatsApp records an opt-out automatically
- Opt-outs are filtered inside `_lib/audience.js` — the single choke point
  every send path goes through
- Unsubscribing drops any **already-queued** messages immediately

**Opt-outs only suppress marketing.** Order confirmations, delivery updates
and gift notifications keep working — they are transactional.

---

## 9. What I verified vs. what needs your live services

### ✅ Verified on this machine

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `node --check` on all 15 JS files | pass |
| SQL against the **real PostgreSQL parser** (`libpg_query`) | pass — 32 statements |
| All `require()` paths resolve | pass — 7 functions load |
| `scripts/verify-campaigns.js` | **39/39 pass** |
| `scripts/verify-sender.js` | **7/7 pass** |

Covered by those tests: opt-out filtering, de-duplication, invalid-email
rejection, segment filter chains, HMAC token forgery rejection, HTML escaping
of admin input, per-recipient unsubscribe tokens, CSV injection neutralisation,
CSV column-union, kill-switch fail-open, send/retry/terminal-failure state
machine, festival date validity, and cross-file wiring.

### ⚠️ Cannot be verified without your live services

| Unknown | How you check it |
|---|---|
| Does `zg_promo_broadcast` get approved? | Meta's decision, days |
| Is your Resend domain OK for bulk? | Emergency → Test email |
| Real customer counts | Campaigns → Preview audience |
| Are the env vars set? | Emergency tab shows each one |
| Does the migration apply cleanly? | Run it; Emergency shows red if not |

### Two bugs the tooling caught during this build

Being specific so you know the verification was real:

1. **Missing comma between CTEs** in `v_customers` — the real Postgres parser
   caught it. The migration would have failed on paste.
2. **Wrong env var names** in the health check — I had assumed `R2_BUCKET`,
   `R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` and `WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN`. Grepping your actual code
   showed they are `R2_BUCKET_NAME`, `R2_PUBLIC_URL` and
   `WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN`. The console would have reported healthy
   variables as missing.

Also corrected mid-build: a contradictory `.is()`/`.or()` filter in the
festival atomic claim, a double tab-hook that would have fired every load
twice, and `describeTemplates()` field names (`bodyParamCount`, not
`bodyVariables`).

---

## 10. Known limitations — stated plainly

- **`v_customers` only contains people who have ordered.** `profiles` has no
  email column, so there is no other reachable source. Browsers/newsletter
  signups are not in it because nothing in your schema captures them.
- **WhatsApp campaigns need Meta approval.** No code can work around this.
- **Email-only is a complete, working feature today.** WhatsApp is additive.
- **Unsubscribe links never expire.** Deliberate — an expired unsubscribe link
  is a spam complaint.
- **Lunar festival dates need manual correction each year.**
- **Exports cap at 40,000 rows** and say `TRUNCATED` in the filename if hit.

---

## 11. Preview

`docs/CAMPAIGN_EMAIL_PREVIEW.html` is a real rendered campaign email
(generated by the actual code, not mocked up). Open it in a browser to see
exactly what customers receive.

# Deploy Guide — Voice Gift · Video Gift · Group Video Tribute (+ Part 1 vibe clarity)

_One-shot deploy checklist. Built to avoid multiple Netlify redeploys._

---

## 0) What's in this release

**Part 1 (vibe clarity):**
- "Choose your vibe" now has a one-line explanation + examples.
- New universal **Motivation 🚀** vibe (works for graduation, promotion, new job, work anniversary, exam).

**Part 2 (three new products):**
- 🎙️ **Voice Gift** (₹79) → delivers as `media_audio`
- 🎬 **Video Gift** (₹99) → delivers as `media_video`
- 👥 **Group Video Tribute** (₹149) → delivers as `squad_drop`
- Each captures **occasion + title + message + media** (upload OR record).

---

## 1) RUN THE SQL FIRST  ⚠️ required

In Supabase → SQL Editor, run:

```
supabase/schema-voice-video-tribute.sql
```

It is 100% additive and idempotent (safe to run once or twice). It:
1. Inserts the 3 products (`digital_voice`, `digital_video`, `digital_tribute`).
2. Adds nullable column `digital_sends.gift_title`.

**If you skip this:** the 3 type-cards stay hidden and checkout would reject the
products. (Code degrades gracefully for the title column, but the product rows
are mandatory.)

**Verify (optional):**
```sql
select id, name, price, active from public.products
  where id in ('digital_voice','digital_video','digital_tribute');
select column_name from information_schema.columns
  where table_name='digital_sends' and column_name='gift_title';
```
Expect 3 product rows (active=true) and 1 column row.

---

## 2) Files to overwrite (exact repo paths)

From the ZIP, drop these in at the same paths and commit:

```
digital-studio.html
digital-gifts.html
gift.html
css/studio.css
js/studio.js
js/vibe-tokens.js
js/studio-group2.js
netlify/functions/get-gift.js
netlify/functions/get-media-upload-url.js
netlify/functions/_lib/digitalSendsHelper.js
supabase/schema-voice-video-tribute.sql   (new file — also run it, step 1)
docs/WhatsApp_Templates_VoiceVideoTribute.md   (reference only, no deploy impact)
docs/DEPLOY_VoiceVideoTribute.md                (this file)
```

> These `studio.js` / `digital-studio.html` / `css/studio.css` **already include
> Part 1**, so they supersede the earlier Part 1 ZIP. Don't apply both.

---

## 3) Env vars — nothing new required

- ✅ Uses existing `get-media-upload-url` (R2) — already configured.
- ✅ Recipient delivery uses existing `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_NAME` default.
- ✅ Tribute invites use existing `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_REACTION_INVITE` default.
- ⛔ No new WhatsApp templates needed to launch (see WhatsApp doc).

---

## 4) Post-deploy smoke test (5 min, ~₹80 of test spend or a test coupon)

Do a **live** check because the parts I can't verify are all in your services
(R2 PUT from a real browser, Cashfree, WhatsApp send, camera/mic permissions).

**Voice Gift**
1. Studio → **Voice Gift** → pick occasion **Graduation** → title + message.
2. **Upload** an MP3/M4A (and separately test **Record**). Confirm "media is ready ✅".
3. Fill recipient + your details → Add to cart → pay.
4. Confirm the recipient WhatsApp lands, gift page plays audio, and the
   **title** shows above the name on the keepsake.

**Video Gift** — same, choose **Upload** an MP4 and once **Record**; confirm the
video plays on reveal.

**Group Video Tribute**
1. Studio → **Group Video Tribute** → occasion **Farewell** → title + message.
2. Add 1–2 friend numbers → pay.
3. Confirm each friend gets the invite WhatsApp with the contribution link.
4. Have a friend add a video; confirm it appears on the recipient's tribute wall.

**Part 1** — open any Birthday Digital Gift → confirm the vibe helper line shows
and **Motivation** appears as a vibe with the trophy card art.

---

## 5) Rollback

Pure front-end + additive back-end. To roll back, redeploy the previous commit.
The SQL is additive — nothing needs undoing (leaving the 3 products + column in
place is harmless; set `active=false` on the products to hide them if needed):
```sql
update public.products set active=false
 where id in ('digital_voice','digital_video','digital_tribute');
```

---

## 6) What I verified vs. what depends on your live services

**Verified locally (ran the code):**
- `node --check` clean on all changed JS.
- Ran the real `studio-group2.js` Voice + Tribute flows through a DOM shim →
  correct `addToCart` payloads (product id, gift_type, occasion, gift_title,
  media_url, contributors) and redirect to checkout.
- Traced `gift_title` across all 6 hops (studio → checkout → order fn →
  digitalSendsHelper → get-gift → gift.html).
- JSON-LD on `digital-gifts.html` parses; 3 cards + FAQ mirror present.

**Depends on your live services (not testable here):**
- Real R2 upload from a browser, Cashfree charge, WhatsApp/email send, and
  on-device camera/mic recording. Do the step-4 smoke test once after deploy.

# Order Pipeline Audit — Fixes

**ZivoGift · deploy guide**

Fixes audit findings **#2–#10**. (#1 `ZIVOSURI01` you are handling yourself; order
updates stay **email-only** as you asked — no WhatsApp status messages added.)

---

## 1. Run the migration

Supabase → SQL Editor → paste → Run:

```
supabase/consolidated/70_pipeline_fixes.sql
```

Additive and idempotent. Adds:

| Object | Closes |
|---|---|
| `digital_sends.buyer_notified_at` | #3 |
| `orders.tracking_number` / `courier_name` / `tracking_url` | #6 |
| `orders.recovery_email_sent_at` | #8 |
| `v_abandoned_checkouts` (view) | #8 |
| `products.stock_qty` + `decrement_stock()` + `set_stock()` | #10 |

Verify:

```sql
select count(*) from public.v_abandoned_checkouts;
select id, name, type, stock_qty from public.products order by type, sort_order;
```

⚠️ **`stock_qty` is NULL = unlimited for every product.** Nothing changes until
you deliberately set a number. A `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` would have taken your
whole catalogue offline the moment the migration ran.

---

## 2. Deploy the files

### New (3)

```
netlify/functions/_lib/suppression.js
netlify/functions/abandoned-cart-scheduler.js
supabase/consolidated/70_pipeline_fixes.sql
```

### Modified (11) — overwrite

| File | Change | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| `_lib/adminSettings.js` | `guardSchedulers()` added | #2 |
| `reminder-scheduler.js` | opt-out on all 3 send paths + kill switch | #2 |
| `occasion-scheduler.js` | opt-out + kill switch | #2 |
| `gift-scheduler.js` | emails the **buyer** on permanent failure | #3 |
| `_lib/digitalSendsHelper.js` | fallback email on WhatsApp-only rows | #4 |
| `js/studio.js` | optional backup email in WhatsApp mode | #4 |
| `digital-studio.html` | label styling for the above | #4 |
| `js/order-status.js` | real post-payment confirming state | #5 |
| `_lib/resend.js` | 2 new templates + tracking block | #3 #6 #8 |
| `js/admin.js` | tracking editor, stock column, row cap | #6 #9 #10 |
| `create-cashfree-order.js` | stock pre-check + atomic reservation | #10 |
| `netlify/functions/admin-ops.js` + `js/admin-ops.js` | Pipeline Health panel | — |
| `netlify/functions/admin-export.js` | abandoned-checkout CSV | #8 |
| `netlify.toml` | hourly abandoned-cart cron | #8 |

No new npm dependencies.

---

## 3. What each fix does

### #2 — Nudge schedulers now honour unsubscribes

`reminder-scheduler` and `occasion-scheduler` sent promotional nudges on a daily
cron and **ignored `marketing_optouts` entirely**. They also had no knowledge of
the settings table, so the Emergency tab's *Pause EVERYTHING* button did not
actually stop them.

That was a hole in what I shipped last turn — the opt-out system existed but
only covered the campaign path. All 3 send sites in `reminder-scheduler` and the
1 in `occasion-scheduler` are now guarded, and both respect the kill switch.

Suppression **fails open**: if the opt-out table can't be read, reminders still
go out rather than one DB blip silencing everything. The read failure is logged.

### #3 — The buyer is finally told when their gift fails

Previously: 4 failed attempts → email to `ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL` → and if that env
var was unset, **nowhere at all**. The person who paid for a midnight birthday
surprise was never told.

Now they get an apologetic email naming the recipient and the order, saying the
gift **is not lost**, and asking for corrected contact details. The raw
technical error is deliberately not shown. `buyer_notified_at` prevents
duplicates on retry.

### #4 — The WhatsApp email fallback actually works now

`50_whatsapp_delivery.sql` built a rescue path: Meta reports a terminal failure
→ requeue as email. But it was gated on `if (row.recipient_email)`, and
WhatsApp rows were inserted **without one** — so for WhatsApp-only gifts the
rescue could never fire.

Digging further, the root cause was upstream: in WhatsApp mode the studio set
`state.recipientEmail = ''` and hid the field. So there was no address to carry.

**Two-part fix.** The studio now keeps the field visible in WhatsApp mode,
relabelled *"optional — backup if WhatsApp fails"*; blank is fine, malformed is
rejected. And `digitalSendsHelper` attaches it to the WhatsApp row.

**Critically, `delivery_mode: 'both'` is excluded** — an email row already
exists for those, so a fallback would deliver the same gift twice.

### #5 — No more "Waiting for payment" after paying

Polling went 8 × 2s = 16s, then rendered whatever it had. A customer whose money
had left their account could see *"Waiting for payment"*.

Now: an explicit **"Confirming your payment"** state, an 80-second window, and
if it still hasn't cleared, honest copy — *"if the amount has left your account,
your order is safe"* — with a re-check button. A network blip no longer ends the
wait early.

### #6 — Courier tracking

Three new columns, an editor in the expandable order row (**physical orders
only**), and a tracking block that appears in the status email automatically
when present. Emails without tracking are byte-identical to before.

### #8 — Abandoned checkout recovery

Hourly cron over `v_abandoned_checkouts`. **One email per order, ever.**

- **1-hour floor** — never interrupt someone mid-payment or on a slow bank OTP page
- **7-day ceiling** — also stops the first deploy mailing years of history in one burst, which every mailbox provider would read as a spam run
- **Re-checks status immediately before sending** — telling a paying customer "you didn't finish" is worse than sending nothing
- Honours opt-outs, carries `List-Unsubscribe`
- If `RESEND_API_KEY` is missing it does **not** stamp — the order keeps its one allowed email

### #9 — Admin row cap

Was a hard `.limit(100)`; older orders silently vanished with no indication.
Now 500 by default, an exact total count, *"showing the newest N of M"*, and a
**Load more** button.

### #10 — Stock control

**Two layers, because one isn't enough.** A read-only pre-check rejects the
order before the payment page. Then `decrement_stock()` — a single conditional
`UPDATE ... WHERE stock_qty >= qty` — settles the race when two people buy the
last unit simultaneously. The loser's order is auto-cancelled and they're told
**they have not been charged**.

Stock is reserved at order creation, not payment success, so an abandoned
checkout does hold a unit. Acceptable at your volume, and correctable by hand.

---

## 4. What I verified vs. what needs your live services

### ✅ Verified on this machine

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `node --check`, all changed JS | pass |
| SQL vs. real PostgreSQL parser (`libpg_query`) | pass — both migrations |
| All `require()` paths resolve | 7 functions load |
| `scripts/verify-pipeline-fixes.js` | **32/32 pass** |
| Regression: `verify-campaigns.js` | **39/39 still pass** |
| Regression: `verify-sender.js` | **7/7 still pass** |

### ⚠️ Needs your live services

Actual email delivery, Meta receipts, real abandoned-order counts, and whether
the migration applies cleanly to your live DB. The Emergency tab's new
**Pipeline Health** panel reports all of these from your phone.

### Issues the tooling caught during this build

1. **`delivery_mode: 'both'` would have double-sent gifts.** My first fallback patch attached `recipient_email` to every WhatsApp row — including `'both'`, which already has its own email row. Caught while reasoning through the rescue path; now explicitly excluded and covered by a test.
2. **The #4 fix was incomplete on its own.** Grepping `studio.js` showed WhatsApp mode never captured a recipient email at all, so the helper patch would have had nothing to attach. That's why the studio change exists.
3. **`pipelinePanel` was silently never written.** A build script asserted after a partial edit and aborted before saving. The verification suite caught it as a failing test — exactly what it's for.
4. Two test assertions were themselves too broad (slicing fixed character counts, and matching a function name inside a comment). The code was correct; the tests were tightened.

---

## 5. Known limitations

- **Stock is held by abandoned checkouts** until you correct it manually.
- **One recovery email per order.** A 3-email sequence converts slightly better and annoys people considerably more — the wrong trade with no laptop to watch complaint rates.
- **`v_abandoned_checkouts` needs `contact_email`.** Orders without one can't be recovered.
- **Tracking is manual paste.** No courier API integration.
- **Nudge suppression fails open** by design — a DB error won't silence reminders.

---

## 6. First run

1. Run the migration.
2. Deploy.
3. **Emergency tab → Pipeline Health.** Check abandoned count looks sane.
4. Place a test order, abandon it at payment, wait an hour, confirm one recovery email arrives.
5. Set `stock_qty` on one note, buy it down to 0, confirm checkout blocks.
6. Add a tracking number to an order, change status, confirm it appears in the email.

Run the tests yourself any time:

```
node scripts/verify-pipeline-fixes.js
```

# Customer Messages (WhatsApp Inbox) — deploy & number migration runbook

Everything below is in dependency order. Steps 1–4 are safe to do now; **step 5 (the number migration) is the point of no return**, so do the prep first.

---

## What this adds

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Text messages | Stored UPPER-CASED in `whatsapp_inbound_log` | Stored with original casing in `wa_messages` |
| Images, voice notes, PDFs, locations, stickers, button taps | **Silently discarded** | Stored, with media retrievable |
| Unknown / future message types | **Silently discarded** | Stored as `unsupported` + raw payload |
| Outbound automation (gifts, campaigns) | Invisible | Mirrored into the customer's thread |
| Replying | WhatsApp Business mobile app only | Admin panel, from anywhere |
| Knowing a message arrived | Nothing | Free email alert (+ optional WhatsApp relay) |

The root cause of the old data loss was two lines in `whatsapp-webhook.js`:

```js
const body = (msg.text?.body || '').trim().toUpperCase();
if (!fromPhone || !body) return;          // <- everything non-text died here
```

The webhook is now **capture-first**: the message is written to `wa_messages` *before* any keyword/condition logic runs.

---

## 1. Apply the migration

Supabase → SQL Editor → run:

```
supabase/consolidated/80_whatsapp_inbox.sql
```

Additive and idempotent. It creates `wa_contacts`, `wa_messages`, `wa_webhook_failures`, `wa_relay_map`, seeds two kill switches, and backfills existing `whatsapp_inbound_log` history so the tab isn't empty on day one.

**It does not alter `whatsapp_inbound_log`** — that table is the dedupe key for gift unlocking and care-package pause/resume, and is deliberately left exactly as-is.

Verify:

```sql
select count(*) from public.wa_contacts;
select count(*) from public.wa_messages;
select key, value from public.admin_settings where key like 'pause_wa%';
-- expect: pause_wa_alerts = false (alerts ON), pause_wa_relay = true (relay OFF)
```

---

## 2. Netlify environment variables

**Required — the inbox cannot receive anything without these:**

| Var | Where to find it |
|---|---|
| `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` | Meta App Dashboard → Settings → Basic → App Secret |
| `WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN` | Any secret string you choose; must match Meta's console |
| `WHATSAPP_TOKEN` | Already set (outbound) |
| `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID` | Already set (outbound) |

> ⚠️ **`WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` fails closed.** If it is unset, `verifyMetaSignature()` rejects **every** inbound POST with a 401 and **no customer message is ever stored**. This is the single most likely cause of an empty inbox. The Emergency tab now reports it explicitly.

**Recommended (free alerting):**

| Var | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL` | Where the free "customer messaged you" alert goes. Costs ₹0. |

**Only if you enable the paid relay (step 7):**

| Var | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER` | Your personal number |
| `WHATSAPP_RELAY_TEMPLATE` | Approved template used when the relay's own 24h window has lapsed |

---

## 3. Deploy

Push to GitHub → Netlify builds. No `netlify.toml` change is needed: `whatsapp-webhook` is HTTP-triggered and `admin-inbox` is a plain function. **No new cron jobs were added**, so this costs no extra scheduled invocations.

---

## 4. Point Meta at the webhook

Meta Developer Console → **WhatsApp → Configuration → Webhook**

- **Callback URL:** `https://zivogift.com/.netlify/functions/whatsapp-webhook`
- **Verify token:** the value of `WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN`
- **Subscribe to field:** `messages` ← **required.** Without this, Meta delivers nothing and there is no error anywhere to tell you.

Then open **Admin → 🚨 Emergency → Re-check**. Under `inbox` you should see `webhook_can_receive: true` and the three `wa_*` tables reporting `ok`.

---

## 5. Migrate the published number — read this before starting

This is the irreversible step.

**Before you begin:**

1. **Export your chat history** from the WhatsApp Business app. Existing conversations **do not** migrate to the Cloud API. Once migrated they are gone from your side.
2. **Submit a re-engagement template now** (see step 6) — approval takes time, and you'll want it on day one.
3. Have your **2-step verification PIN** ready; registration requires it.

**What happens:**

- The WhatsApp **Business App stops working** on that number. It becomes API-only.
- Inbound messages start arriving at the webhook instead of the phone.
- Outbound automation (gift/order templates) continues unchanged.

Meta's own migration flow (Business App → Cloud API) is the supported path — follow it in WhatsApp Manager rather than deleting the number first.

**Immediately after migration, send a test message to the number from another phone.** Within seconds you should see: an email alert, and the conversation in **Admin → 💬 Messages**.

---

## 6. Templates

Submit at least one **utility** template for re-engagement, used when a customer's 24h window has closed.

Suggested body (one variable):

```
Hi {{1}}, following up on your message to ZivoGift. Reply here and we'll continue the conversation.
```

Once approved it appears automatically in the Messages tab composer when a window is closed — the picker reads your live approved templates via introspection, so nothing is hardcoded.

If you enable the relay, submit a second utility template with **two** variables (customer name, message preview) and set `WHATSAPP_RELAY_TEMPLATE` to its name.

---

## 7. The personal-number relay — optional, and OFF

Ships disabled (`pause_wa_relay = true`). Everything works without it.

**Turn it on** (no redeploy, no build credits):

```sql
update public.admin_settings set value = false where key = 'pause_wa_relay';
```

Then set `ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER`.

**How you use it:** a customer messages ZivoGift → you get a WhatsApp on your personal number → you reply → the reply goes back out **from the ZivoGift number**. Your personal number is never exposed.

Replying works three ways:

1. **Long-press the notification → Reply.** Resolved via `wa_relay_map`. Most reliable.
2. **Number prefix:** `9876543210 Sure, we can do 50 boxes`
3. **Implicit** — only when exactly one conversation was relayed in the last 90 minutes.

If two or more conversations are active and you reply without quoting or prefixing, **the relay refuses to guess** and asks you which one. Sending a reply to the wrong customer is worse than one extra tap.

Commands: `LIST`, `CLOSE 9876543210`, `HELP`.

**Cost:** the first forward after a quiet spell is a billable utility template (~₹0.12–0.15). Once you reply, a 24h window opens with your number and further forwards that day are free. Alerts are throttled to one per contact per hour regardless.

---

## 8. Daily use

**Admin → 💬 Messages.** Conversation list on the left (unread first, searchable by name/phone/order), thread on the right.

- 🟢 **Window open** → free-text composer + countdown. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends.
- 🔴 **Window closed** → composer switches to the approved-template picker automatically.
- 📎 **Media** loads on demand (Meta → R2, cached permanently after first view).
- 🤖 marks messages sent automatically by ZivoGift; `you` marks your replies.
- Ticks are real: ✓ sent, ✓✓ delivered, green ✓✓ read, ⚠ failed with the reason.
- The nav button shows an unread badge, polled once a minute even from other tabs.

---

## Rollback

Restore the previous `netlify/functions/whatsapp-webhook.js` and `netlify/functions/_lib/whatsapp.js` and redeploy. The new tables are additive and harmless if left in place — nothing else reads them.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| Inbox stays empty | `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` unset (webhook 401s everything), or the `messages` field is not subscribed in Meta |
| "relation does not exist" | `80_whatsapp_inbox.sql` not applied |
| Reply fails with "window closed" | More than 24h since the customer wrote — use a template |
| Media won't load | Meta expires media after ~30 days; the message text and metadata remain |
| `unprocessed_failures > 0` in Emergency | A payload shape this code didn't expect. **Not data loss** — the raw JSON is in `wa_webhook_failures` |
| No email alerts | `ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL` unset, or `pause_wa_alerts = true` |

# ZivoGift — WhatsApp Templates for Voice Gift / Video Gift / Group Video Tribute

_Last updated: 2026-09-04 · For Meta WhatsApp Cloud API (Business Manager → WhatsApp Manager → Message templates)_

---

## TL;DR — Do you need to submit anything?

**No new templates are required to ship these 3 products.** They reuse delivery
paths that already send through your **existing, approved** templates:

| What happens | Template used | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Recipient gets their Voice/Video/Tribute gift | `zivogift_birthday_surprise` (default via `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_NAME`) | ✅ already approved & live |
| Tribute invites each friend to add a video | `squad_reaction_invite` (via `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_REACTION_INVITE`) | ✅ already approved & live |
| Sender gets "delivered" confirmation | `gift_delivered_sender_notify` | ✅ already approved & live |

So you can **deploy without touching Meta at all.** The section below is only for
if/when you want *cleaner, product-specific* copy later. It is written to pass as
**UTILITY**, since that's been the sticking point.

---

## Why templates kept getting flagged as MARKETING (and how to avoid it)

Meta's classifier looks at **intent and wording**, not the category you pick. A
template is **MARKETING** (higher cost, opt-out required) the moment it reads as
promotion. It stays **UTILITY** when it is a *transactional follow-up to a
specific action the user took* (here: someone paid for and sent a gift).

**Keep UTILITY — do:**
- Refer to a **specific transaction/event**: "your gift", "you sent", "just delivered".
- Be **factual and personal**: names, what happened, a link to the thing they paid for.
- Keep it a **notification**, not an invitation to buy.

**Turns it MARKETING — avoid:**
- Promotional adjectives / hype: "amazing deals", "special offer", "cheapest", "don't miss".
- Generic CTAs unrelated to a transaction: "Shop now", "Explore our range", "Sign up".
- Emojis-as-advertising, discount codes, prices, "limited time".
- Talking to someone who **didn't** trigger an action. (A recipient who never
  interacted with you is the classic MARKETING trigger — this is fine for gift
  delivery because it's a user-initiated notification, but keep the copy purely
  about the delivery, never a pitch.)

> Rule of thumb: if you removed the person's name and the specific event and the
> message still makes sense as an ad, it's MARKETING. If it becomes nonsense
> without them, it's UTILITY.

---

## Optional product-specific templates (submit ONLY if you want them)

All three are drafted as **UTILITY**, English (`en`). Variables are positional
(`{{1}}`, `{{2}}`…). Match the `bodyVariables` order in code exactly.

> ⚠️ If you submit these, wire them in via the env vars noted, otherwise the code
> keeps using the working defaults. **Nothing breaks if you skip this.**

---

### 1. `zg_voice_gift_delivered` — Voice Gift → recipient

- **Category:** UTILITY
- **Language:** English (`en`)
- **Header:** Image (optional — the sealed card). Can be omitted; code auto-retries headerless.
- **Body:**
  ```
  Hi {{1}}, {{2}} sent you a voice gift on ZivoGift 🎙️
  Tap to listen and see who it's from: {{3}}
  ```
- **Footer:** `ZivoGift`
- **Variables:** `{{1}}`=recipient name · `{{2}}`=sender name · `{{3}}`=gift link
- **Sample:** `Hi Rahul, Suresh sent you a voice gift on ZivoGift 🎙️ Tap to listen and see who it's from: https://zivogift.com/gift.html?id=abc123`
- **Wire-up:** set env `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_NAME` per-type is not currently split;
  to use this, pass `templateName` into `sendGiftMessage()` for `media_audio`
  (small change in `gift-scheduler.js`). Ask me and I'll wire it.

  function field(id, type, label, placeholder) {
    return '<div class="field-group"><label>' + label + '</label><input type="' + type + '" id="' + id + '"' +
      (placeholder ? ' placeholder="' + placeholder + '"' : '') + '></div>';

  function wireForm() {

    var cancelBtn = $('friends-cancel-btn');
    var addBtn    = $('friends-add-special');
    if (saveBtn)   saveBtn.addEventListener('click', handleSave);

  // ── Special Days repeater ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

  function occasionOptionsHtml(selected) {

  // Adds one editable special-day row. `data` pre-fills it when editing.

    // Toggle the custom-label box when "Other…" is chosen.

    var lbl = row.querySelector('.g3-sp-label');
    sel.addEventListener('change', function () {

  function collectSpecialDates() {
    var out = [];
    var rows = document.querySelectorAll('#friends-special-list .g3-special-row');
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(rows, function (row) {
      var date = row.querySelector('.g3-sp-date').value;
      if (!date) return; // a day with no date is meaningless — skip silently
      var type = row.querySelector('.g3-sp-type').value;
      var label = row.querySelector('.g3-sp-label').value.trim();
      out.push({
        occasion_type: type,
        label: type === 'custom' ? (label || 'Special Day') : null,
        event_date: date,
        reminders_enabled: row.querySelector('.g3-sp-remind').checked,
        remind_before_days: 3,
      });
    });
    return out;
  }

  function clearSpecialRows() {
    var list = $('friends-special-list');
    if (list) list.innerHTML = '';
  }

  // ── Load + render friends list ─────────────────────────────────────────────

  function loadFriends() {
    if (!token) return;
    fetch('/.netlify/functions/friends-api?action=list', {
      headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + token },
    }).then(function (r) { return r.json(); })
      .then(function (data) { renderFriendsList(data.friends || []); })
      .catch(function () { setMsg('Could not load friends.', true); });
  }

  function renderFriendsList(friends) {
    var el = $('friends-list');
    if (!el) return;
    if (!friends.length) {
      el.innerHTML = '<div style="font-size:13px;color:#777;padding:14px 0;">No saved friends yet — add the first one below! 👇</div>';
      return;
    }
    el.innerHTML = friends.map(function (f) {
      var bday  = f.birthday_date ? '🎂 ' + formatDate(f.birthday_date) : '';
      var anni  = f.friendship_start_date ? '🤝 Since ' + formatDate(f.friendship_start_date) : '';
      var college = f.college ? '🎓 ' + f.college : '';
      var meta  = [f.relationship_type, college, bday, anni].filter(Boolean).join(' · ');

      // Special-day chips — each occasion's emoji + name + date (+ bell if it
      // has a reminder). Every dynamic part is esc()'d before it goes in.
      var specialsHtml = (f.special_dates || []).map(function (d) {
        var o = occasionLabel(d.occasion_type);
        var name = d.occasion_type === 'custom' ? (d.label || 'Special day') : o.label;
        var bell = d.reminders_enabled === false ? '' : ' \uD83D\uDD14';
        return '<span style="display:inline-block;background:rgba(168,85,247,.12);border:1px solid rgba(168,85,247,.28);' +
          'color:#C084FC;font-size:11px;padding:3px 9px;border-radius:20px;margin:4px 5px 0 0;">' +
          o.emoji + ' ' + esc(name) + ' \u00b7 ' + formatDate(d.event_date) + bell + '</span>';
      }).join('');

      return [
        '<div class="card-panel" style="margin-bottom:12px;padding:14px 16px;">',
          '<div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:flex-start;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;">',
            '<div>',
              '<div style="font-weight:700;font-size:15px;">' + esc(f.name) + '</div>',
              meta ? '<div style="font-size:12px;color:#888;margin-top:3px;">' + esc(meta) + '</div>' : '',
              f.context_notes ? '<div style="font-size:12px;color:#A855F7;margin-top:4px;">🧠 ' + esc(f.context_notes.slice(0, 70)) + (f.context_notes.length > 70 ? '…' : '') + '</div>' : '',
              specialsHtml ? '<div style="margin-top:6px;">' + specialsHtml + '</div>' : '',
            '</div>',
            '<div style="display:flex;gap:8px;">',
              '<button class="g3-edit-btn" data-id="' + f.id + '" style="font-size:12px;background:rgba(168,85,247,.15);border:1px solid rgba(168,85,247,.3);color:#A855F7;padding:5px 12px;border-radius:7px;cursor:pointer;">Edit</button>',
              '<button class="g3-del-btn"  data-id="' + f.id + '" style="font-size:12px;background:rgba(255,77,46,.1);border:1px solid rgba(255,77,46,.25);color:#FF4D2E;padding:5px 12px;border-radius:7px;cursor:pointer;">Delete</button>',
            '</div>',
          '</div>',
          '<div style="display:flex;gap:16px;margin-top:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;">',
            toggle('bday',  f.id, f.birthday_reminders_enabled,    '🎂 Birthday alerts'),
            toggle('anni',  f.id, f.anniversary_reminders_enabled, '🤝 Anniversary alerts'),
          '</div>',
        '</div>',
      ].join('');
    }).join('');

    // Wire edit/delete/toggle buttons
    el.querySelectorAll('.g3-edit-btn').forEach(function (btn) {
      btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
        var friend = friends.find(function (f) { return f.id === btn.dataset.id; });
        if (friend) startEdit(friend);
      });
    });
    el.querySelectorAll('.g3-del-btn').forEach(function (btn) {
      btn.addEventListener('click', function () { deleteFriend(btn.dataset.id); });
    });
    el.querySelectorAll('.g3-toggle').forEach(function (chk) {
      chk.addEventListener('change', function () {
        toggleReminder(chk.dataset.fid, chk.dataset.type, chk.checked);
      });
    });
  }

  function toggle(type, fid, enabled, label) {
    return '<label style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;font-size:12px;color:#aaa;cursor:pointer;">' +
      '<input type="checkbox" class="g3-toggle" data-fid="' + fid + '" data-type="' + type + '" ' +
      (enabled ? 'checked' : '') + ' style="width:auto;accent-color:#A855F7;">' +
      label + '</label>';
  }

  // ── CRUD handlers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  function handleSave() {
    var name   = ($('friends-name')   || {}).value || '';
    if (!name.trim()) { setMsg('Name is required', true); return; }

    var body = {
      id:                           editingId || undefined,
      name:                         name.trim(),
      phone:                        ($('friends-phone') || {}).value || '',
      relationship_type:            ($('friends-rel')   || {}).value || '',
      college:                      ($('friends-college') || {}).value || null,
      context_notes:                ($('friends-notes') || {}).value || '',
      birthday_date:                ($('friends-bday')  || {}).value || null,
      friendship_start_date:        ($('friends-anni')  || {}).value || null,
      remind_before_days:           parseInt(($('friends-remind-days') || {}).value || '3', 10),
      birthday_reminders_enabled:   !!($('friends-bday-on')  || {}).checked,
      anniversary_reminders_enabled:!!($('friends-anni-on')  || {}).checked,
      special_dates:                collectSpecialDates(),
    };
    if (!editingId) delete body.id;

    fetch('/.netlify/functions/friends-api?action=save', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: 'Bearer ' + token },
      body: JSON.stringify(body),
    }).then(function (r) { return r.json(); })
      .then(function (data) {
        if (data.error) { setMsg(data.error, true); return; }
        setMsg(editingId ? 'Friend updated ✓' : 'Friend saved ✓', false);
        resetForm();
        loadFriends();
      }).catch(function () { setMsg('Save failed', true); });
  }

  function startEdit(friend) {
    editingId = friend.id;
    setValue('friends-name',  friend.name);
    setValue('friends-phone', friend.phone || '');
    setValue('friends-rel',   friend.relationship_type || '');
    setValue('friends-college', friend.college || '');
    setValue('friends-notes', friend.context_notes || '');
    setValue('friends-bday',  friend.birthday_date || '');
    setValue('friends-anni',  friend.friendship_start_date || '');
    setChecked('friends-bday-on',   friend.birthday_reminders_enabled !== false);
    setChecked('friends-anni-on',   friend.anniversary_reminders_enabled !== false);
    setValue('friends-remind-days', String(friend.remind_before_days || 3));

    // Rebuild the special-day rows from this friend's saved set.
    clearSpecialRows();
    (friend.special_dates || []).forEach(function (d) { addSpecialRow(d); });

    var title = $('friends-form-title');
    if (title) title.textContent = 'EDIT FRIEND';
    var cancelBtn = $('friends-cancel-btn');
    if (cancelBtn) cancelBtn.style.display = 'inline-block';

    var formEl = $('friends-save-btn');
    if (formEl) formEl.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'nearest' });
  }

  function resetForm() {
    editingId = null;
    ['friends-name','friends-phone','friends-rel','friends-notes','friends-bday','friends-anni'].forEach(function (id) {
      setValue(id, '');
    });
    setChecked('friends-bday-on', true);
    setChecked('friends-anni-on', true);
    setValue('friends-remind-days', '3');
    clearSpecialRows();
    var title = $('friends-form-title');
    if (title) title.textContent = 'ADD A FRIEND';
    var cancelBtn = $('friends-cancel-btn');
    if (cancelBtn) cancelBtn.style.display = 'none';
    setMsg('', false);
  }

  function deleteFriend(id) {
    if (!confirm('Remove this friend? Reminders for them will stop.')) return;
    fetch('/.netlify/functions/friends-api?action=delete', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: 'Bearer ' + token },
      body: JSON.stringify({ id: id }),
    }).then(function () { loadFriends(); })
      .catch(function () { setMsg('Delete failed', true); });
  }

  function toggleReminder(fid, type, enabled) {
    fetch('/.netlify/functions/friends-api?action=toggle_reminder', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: 'Bearer ' + token },
      body: JSON.stringify({ id: fid, type: type, enabled: enabled }),
    }).catch(function () {});
  }

  // ── Tab switching (mirrors account.js pattern) ─────────────────────────────

  function switchTab(tab) {
    document.querySelectorAll('.account-panel').forEach(function (p) { p.style.display = 'none'; });
    var panel = $('panel-' + tab);
    if (panel) panel.style.display = 'block';
    document.querySelectorAll('[data-tab]').forEach(function (b) {
      b.classList.toggle('active', b.dataset.tab === tab);
    });
  }

  // ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  function setValue(id, val) { var el = $(id); if (el) el.value = val || ''; }
  function setChecked(id, on) { var el = $(id); if (el) el.checked = !!on; }
  function setMsg(msg, isErr) {
    var el = $('friends-msg');
    if (!el) return;
    el.textContent = msg;
    el.style.color = isErr ? '#FF4D2E' : '#A855F7';
  }
  function esc(s) {
    return String(s).replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;').replace(/>/g,'&gt;').replace(/"/g,'&quot;');
  }
  function formatDate(d) {
    if (!d) return '';
    var parts = d.split('-'); // YYYY-MM-DD
    var months = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec'];
    return months[parseInt(parts[1],10)-1] + ' ' + parseInt(parts[2],10);
  }

  // ── Init ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
    // Wait for account.js to load session
    var attempts = 0;
    var poll = setInterval(function () {
      attempts++;
      if (attempts > 30) { clearInterval(poll); return; }

      if (window.ZGAuth) {
        clearInterval(poll);
        window.ZGAuth.getSession().then(function (session) {
          if (!session) return; // not logged in — friends tab is login-required
          token = session.access_token;
          injectFriendsTab();
        }).catch(function () {});
      }
    }, 200);
  });

})();
