FILE: netlify\functions\unsubscribe.js
=====================================================

// netlify/functions/unsubscribe.js
//
// PUBLIC endpoint. No auth by design — an unsubscribe link has to work from
// an email client with no login, which is the whole point. The signed token
// (_lib/unsubToken.js) is what stops it being "anyone can unsubscribe anyone".
//
// Handles three callers:
//   GET  ?t=<token>  -> a human clicked the footer link. Renders an HTML page.
//   POST ?t=<token>  -> Gmail/Yahoo one-click (List-Unsubscribe-Post). Returns
//                       200 with no body; these providers never render HTML.
//   GET  ?t=..&undo=1-> the "I did not mean to do that" path.
//
// RFC 8058 one-click requires that a POST unsubscribes IMMEDIATELY with no
// confirmation step. Gmail tests this. A confirmation page on POST is treated
// as a non-functioning unsubscribe and costs deliverability, so the POST
// branch deliberately does not ask.

const { getSupabaseAdmin } = require('./_lib/supabaseAdmin');
const { readToken, makeToken } = require('./_lib/unsubToken');

const HTML_HEADERS = { 'Content-Type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8', 'Cache-Control': 'no-store' };

exports.handler = async (event) => {
  const qs = event.queryStringParameters || {};
  const token = qs.t || '';
  const isPost = event.httpMethod === 'POST';

  const parsed = readToken(token);

  if (!parsed.valid) {
    if (isPost) return { statusCode: 400, body: '' };
    return page(400, 'That link is not valid',
      'This unsubscribe link could not be verified. It may have been altered by your email client. ' +
      'Email <a href="mailto:hello@zivogift.com" style="color:#f5c842;">hello@zivogift.com</a> and we will remove you by hand.');
  }

  const supabase = getSupabaseAdmin();
  const email = parsed.email ? String(parsed.email).toLowerCase() : null;
  const phone10 = parsed.phone10 || null;

  // ── UNDO ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (!isPost && qs.undo === '1') {
    try {
      if (email) await supabase.from('marketing_optouts').delete().eq('email', email);
      if (phone10) await supabase.from('marketing_optouts').delete().eq('phone10', phone10);
      return page(200, 'You are back on the list',
        'You will receive Zivogift offers again. You can unsubscribe at any time from any email.');
    } catch (e) {
      console.error('unsubscribe: undo failed:', (e && e.message) || e);
      return page(500, 'Something went wrong', 'Please email hello@zivogift.com and we will sort it out.');
    }
  }

  // ── UNSUBSCRIBE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  try {
    // Upsert per identifier. Two separate writes rather than one row with both
    // columns, because the partial unique indexes are per-column -- and
    // because a person who unsubscribes by email should also stop receiving
    // WhatsApp campaigns tied to the same order.
    if (email) {
      await supabase.from('marketing_optouts')
        .upsert({ email, source: 'link', campaign_id: parsed.campaignId || null }, { onConflict: 'email' });
    }
    if (phone10) {
      await supabase.from('marketing_optouts')
        .upsert({ phone10, source: 'link', campaign_id: parsed.campaignId || null }, { onConflict: 'phone10' });
    }

    // Also drop any still-queued campaign sends for this person, so an
    // unsubscribe during an in-flight campaign takes effect immediately
    // rather than at the end of the drain.
    if (email) {
      await supabase.from('campaign_recipients')
        .update({ status: 'skipped', error_message: 'Recipient unsubscribed' })
        .eq('email', email).eq('status', 'queued');
    }
    if (phone10) {
      await supabase.from('campaign_recipients')
        .update({ status: 'skipped', error_message: 'Recipient unsubscribed' })
        .eq('phone10', phone10).eq('status', 'queued');
    }
  } catch (e) {
    console.error('unsubscribe: write failed:', (e && e.message) || e);
    if (isPost) return { statusCode: 500, body: '' };
    return page(500, 'Something went wrong',
      'We could not record that. Please email <a href="mailto:hello@zivogift.com" style="color:#f5c842;">hello@zivogift.com</a> and we will remove you by hand.');
  }

  // One-click: succeed silently, no HTML.
  if (isPost) return { statusCode: 200, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain' }, body: 'OK' };

  const undoLink = `?t=${encodeURIComponent(makeToken({ email, phone10, campaignId: parsed.campaignId }))}&undo=1`;
  return page(200, 'You are unsubscribed',
    'You will not receive Zivogift offers again.<br /><br />' +
    '<strong>You will still receive order confirmations, delivery updates and gift notifications</strong> — ' +
    'those are part of the service, not marketing.<br /><br />' +
    `<a href="${undoLink}" style="color:#f5c842;">I did not mean to do that — put me back</a>`);
};

// Self-contained HTML. Deliberately not loading css/style.css: this page is
// opened from inside an email client on an unpredictable network, and a
// stylesheet that fails to load would leave it unreadable.
function page(statusCode, heading, bodyHtml) {
  return {
    statusCode,
    headers: HTML_HEADERS,
    body: `<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en"><head>
<meta charset="utf-8" /><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1" />
<meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow" />
<title>${escape(heading)} — Zivogift</title>
</head>
<body style="margin:0;background:#08080a;color:#f5f5f0;font-family:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Arial,sans-serif;">
  <div style="max-width:520px;margin:0 auto;padding:64px 24px;text-align:center;">
    <div style="font-size:26px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.5px;margin-bottom:26px;">
      <span style="color:#f5c842;">Zivo</span><span style="color:#ff4d2e;">gift</span>
    </div>
    <div style="background:#12100c;border:1px solid #2a2925;border-radius:18px;padding:34px 26px;">
      <h1 style="margin:0 0 16px;font-size:21px;line-height:29px;color:#f5f5f0;">${escape(heading)}</h1>
      <p style="margin:0;font-size:15px;line-height:24px;color:#b5aea4;">${bodyHtml}</p>
    </div>
    <p style="margin-top:26px;font-size:13px;color:#6f6a63;">
      <a href="https://zivogift.com" style="color:#8a847b;">zivogift.com</a>
      &middot; <a href="mailto:hello@zivogift.com" style="color:#8a847b;">hello@zivogift.com</a>
    </p>
  </div>
</body></html>`,
  };
}

function escape(s) {
  return String(s == null ? '' : s).replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) =>
    ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;', "'": '&#39;' }[c]));
}

FILE: netlify\functions\verify-sender-otp.js

// POST /.netlify/functions/verify-sender-otp
//
// MSG91 OTP WIDGET flow (not the raw SendOTP API — see _lib/msg91.js for
// why the widget is what actually works pre-DLT/pre-GST). The browser
// sends and verifies the OTP itself via MSG91's widget script, then hands
// this endpoint the resulting access-token. We never see the OTP code —
// we only ever get an opaque token, which we independently confirm with
// MSG91's own server before trusting it (never trust a client-reported
// "success" alone; anyone can fake calling a JS callback).
//
// CHANGED (per the "OTP every order" fix): verification is no longer a
// 30-minute per-order token. This endpoint is now called ONLY from the
// "Verify Mobile Number" block in My Account (js/account-phone-verify.js),
// requires a logged-in session, and on success writes a PERMANENT
// phone_verified=true flag onto that user's profiles row for their saved
// phone number. create-cashfree-order.js checks that flag, not a token —
// so once verified, digital-gift checkout never asks for OTP again for
// that account. A sender_verification_tokens row is still written too,
// kept only as a secondary audit trail / defense-in-depth signal — it is
// not what gates order creation anymore.

const crypto = require('crypto');
const { getSupabaseAdmin } = require('./_lib/supabaseAdmin');
const { verifyAccessToken } = require('./_lib/msg91');
const { normalizePhone } = require('./_lib/phoneUtil');

const MAX_WRONG_ATTEMPTS = 5;
const ATTEMPT_WINDOW_MINUTES = 10;
const TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES = 30;

exports.handler = async (event) => {
  if (event.httpMethod !== 'POST') {
    return { statusCode: 405, body: 'Method Not Allowed' };
  }

  // Must be logged in — verification is now tied to the account's profile
  // row, not a bare phone number, so there's no anonymous path here anymore.
  const supabase = getSupabaseAdmin();
  const authHeader = event.headers.authorization || event.headers.Authorization;
  if (!authHeader || !authHeader.startsWith('Bearer ')) {
    return { statusCode: 401, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Please log in to verify your mobile number' }) };
  }
  const { data: userData, error: userErr } = await supabase.auth.getUser(authHeader.slice(7));
  if (userErr || !userData || !userData.user) {
    return { statusCode: 401, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Your session has expired — please log in again' }) };
  }
  const userId = userData.user.id;

  let body;
  try {
    body = JSON.parse(event.body || '{}');
  } catch {
    return { statusCode: 400, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Invalid JSON body' }) };
  }

  const phone = normalizePhone(body.phone);
  const accessToken = String(body.accessToken || '').trim();
  if (!phone || !accessToken) {
    return { statusCode: 400, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Missing phone or verification token' }) };
  }

  // The phone being verified must match what's actually saved on the
  // account — otherwise someone could verify a number that isn't the one
  // create-cashfree-order.js will end up trusting for this account anyway
  // (it reads profiles.phone), or worse, verify a number that isn't theirs.
  const { data: profileRow, error: profileErr } = await supabase
    .from('profiles')
    .select('phone')
    .eq('id', userId)
    .maybeSingle();
  if (profileErr || !profileRow) {
    return { statusCode: 500, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Could not load your account — please try again' }) };
  }
  const accountPhone = normalizePhone(profileRow.phone);
  if (!accountPhone || accountPhone !== phone) {
    return { statusCode: 400, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'This doesn\'t match the mobile number saved on your account. Update it in My Account first, then verify.' }) };
  }

  // Guard against brute-forcing this endpoint with junk tokens for a given
  // number (the actual OTP brute-forcing is MSG91's problem now, since
  // they own send+verify — this protects our own verify-access-token
  // round-trips to MSG91 from being hammered).
  const windowStart = new Date(Date.now() - ATTEMPT_WINDOW_MINUTES * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
  const { count: attemptCount, error: attemptCountErr } = await supabase
    .from('sender_phone_otp_verify_attempts')
    .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
    .eq('phone', phone)
    .gte('created_at', windowStart);

  if (attemptCountErr) {
    console.error('verify-sender-otp: attempt check failed:', attemptCountErr.message);
    return { statusCode: 500, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Something went wrong, please try again' }) };
  }
  if ((attemptCount || 0) >= MAX_WRONG_ATTEMPTS) {
    return { statusCode: 429, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Too many attempts — please start over' }) };
  }

  let verified;
  try {
    verified = await verifyAccessToken(accessToken);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('verify-sender-otp: MSG91 verifyAccessToken call failed:', err.message);
    return { statusCode: 502, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Something went wrong, please try again' }) };
  }

  if (!verified) {
    await supabase.from('sender_phone_otp_verify_attempts').insert({ phone });
    return { statusCode: 400, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Verification failed or expired — please try again' }) };
  }

  // This is the actual fix: persist verification on the account itself
  // instead of a 30-min token, so it never has to be redone for future
  // orders. create-cashfree-order.js reads these two columns directly.
  const { error: profileUpdateErr } = await supabase
    .from('profiles')
    .update({ phone_verified: true, phone_verified_at: new Date().toISOString() })
    .eq('id', userId);

  if (profileUpdateErr) {
    console.error('verify-sender-otp: profile update failed:', profileUpdateErr.message);
    return { statusCode: 500, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Verified, but could not save it to your account — please try again' }) };
  }

  // Kept only as a secondary audit trail — not read by create-cashfree-order.js
  // anymore, so a failure here doesn't need to fail the whole request.
  const verificationToken = crypto.randomBytes(24).toString('hex');
  const tokenExpiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
  try {
    await supabase
      .from('sender_verification_tokens')
      .insert({ phone, verification_token: verificationToken, token_expires_at: tokenExpiresAt });
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn('verify-sender-otp: audit token insert failed (non-fatal):', err && err.message);
  }

  return {
    statusCode: 200,
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ verified: true, phone: phone }),
  };
};



=====================================================
FILE: netlify\functions\whatsapp-webhook.js
=====================================================


// netlify/functions/whatsapp-webhook.js
//
// Meta WhatsApp Cloud API — Inbound Webhook
//
// ============================================================================
// WHAT CHANGED IN THIS VERSION AND WHY
// ============================================================================
//
// The previous version was built for ONE job: spotting a keyword so that
// Condition-Based Delivery (#23) could unlock a gift. That job it did well.
// But as a receiver of CUSTOMER messages it lost almost everything:
//
//   1. `const body = (msg.text?.body || '').trim().toUpperCase();`
//      followed by `if (!fromPhone || !body) return;`
//      -> ANY non-text message was discarded before a single row was written.
//         A photo of a bulk-order requirement list, a voice note asking about
//         delivery, a PDF purchase order, a shared location — all of them hit
//         that early return and vanished. No row, no log, no trace.
//
//   2. The text that WAS stored had been .toUpperCase()'d first, so
//      whatsapp_inbound_log.body held shouting instead of a transcript.
//      Fine for keyword matching, useless as customer support history.
//
//   3. There was no outbound side and no thread, so "show me my conversation
//      with this customer" was not answerable from the data at all.
//
// THIS VERSION IS RESTRUCTURED AS: CAPTURE FIRST, INTERPRET SECOND.
//
// Every inbound message is written to wa_messages (with Meta's raw payload
// attached) BEFORE any keyword, opt-out, care-package or condition logic
// runs. That ordering is the whole guarantee: a bug in the interpretation
// step can no longer cost you the message, because the message was already
// safe on disk before interpretation began.
//
// Anything that still manages to throw is spooled into wa_webhook_failures
// with the raw body, so the worst possible outcome is "stored but not yet
// processed" — never "gone".
//
// NOTHING EXISTING WAS REMOVED. Delivery receipts, the digital_sends email
// fallback, campaign receipts, marketing opt-out, care-package pause/resume
// and condition-keyword unlocking all behave exactly as before. The two
// inline raw fetch() replies now route through _lib/whatsappSession.js so
// they get retries and are recorded in the thread.
//
// ── SETUP (one-time in Meta Developer Console) ──────────────────────────────
//   1. App Dashboard → WhatsApp → Configuration → Webhook
//   2. Callback URL: https://zivogift.com/.netlify/functions/whatsapp-webhook
//   3. Verify token: WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN
//   4. Subscribe to: messages     <-- REQUIRED. Without this field subscribed,
//                                     Meta delivers nothing and the inbox
//                                     stays empty with no error anywhere.
//
// ── REQUIRED ENV VARS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//   WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN — matches Meta's console
//   WHATSAPP_TOKEN                — same token used for outbound
//   WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID      — your WABA phone number id
//   WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET           — App Dashboard → Settings → Basic
//
//   ⚠ WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET IS NOT OPTIONAL. verifyMetaSignature() fails CLOSED:
//     if the secret is unset, every inbound POST is rejected with 401 and no
//     customer message is ever stored. This is the single most likely cause
//     of "the inbox is empty" — check it first.
//
// Requires: supabase/consolidated/80_whatsapp_inbox.sql

const crypto = require('crypto');
const { getSupabaseAdmin } = require('./_lib/supabaseAdmin');
const {
  recordInbound,
  recordOutbound,
  applyStatusToThread,
  spoolFailure,
  previewFor,
} = require('./_lib/waInbox');
const { sendWhatsAppText } = require('./_lib/whatsappSession');
const { notifyNewMessage } = require('./_lib/waNotify');
const { handleAdminRelayMessage } = require('./_lib/waRelay');

// Meta signs the raw POST body with HMAC-SHA256 using your App Secret and
// sends it as `X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex digest>`. Verifying this is
// the only thing standing between this endpoint and anyone on the internet
// being able to forge inbound WhatsApp messages against your webhook — spot
// a request with no valid signature, and it's not really from Meta.
function verifyMetaSignature(rawBody, signatureHeader) {
  const appSecret = process.env.WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET;
  if (!appSecret) {
    console.error('whatsapp-webhook: WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET not set — cannot verify inbound signature. Rejecting for safety.');
    return false;
  }
  if (!signatureHeader || !signatureHeader.startsWith('sha256=')) return false;

  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac('sha256', appSecret)
    .update(rawBody, 'utf8')
    .digest('hex');

  const providedHex = signatureHeader.slice('sha256='.length);
  const expectedBuf = Buffer.from(expected, 'hex');
  const providedBuf = Buffer.from(providedHex, 'hex');

  // Buffer.from(..., 'hex') silently truncates on malformed hex rather than
  // throwing — an empty/garbled header produces a shorter buffer, which
  // the length check below catches before timingSafeEqual would throw on
  // mismatched lengths.
  return expectedBuf.length === providedBuf.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(expectedBuf, providedBuf);
}

exports.handler = async (event) => {
  // ── GET: Meta verification handshake ──────────────────────────────────────
  if (event.httpMethod === 'GET') {
    const params        = event.queryStringParameters || {};
    const mode          = params['hub.mode'];
    const token         = params['hub.verify_token'];
    const challenge     = params['hub.challenge'];

    if (mode === 'subscribe' && token === process.env.WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN) {
      console.log('whatsapp-webhook: Meta verification handshake passed');
      return { statusCode: 200, body: challenge };
    }
    console.warn('whatsapp-webhook: verification failed — token mismatch');
    return { statusCode: 403, body: 'Forbidden' };
  }

  // ── POST: Inbound message from Meta ───────────────────────────────────────
  if (event.httpMethod !== 'POST') {
    return { statusCode: 405, body: 'Method Not Allowed' };
  }

  const rawBody = event.body || '';
  const signatureHeader = event.headers['x-hub-signature-256'] || event.headers['X-Hub-Signature-256'];

  if (!verifyMetaSignature(rawBody, signatureHeader)) {
    console.warn('whatsapp-webhook: invalid or missing X-Hub-Signature-256 — rejecting.');
    // Meta itself will never hit this path with a bad signature, so there's
    // no retry-storm concern in returning non-200 here (unlike the JSON
    // parse-error case below, which intentionally returns 200 to avoid
    // Meta retrying a payload that will never parse).
    return { statusCode: 401, body: 'Invalid signature' };
  }

  const supabase = getSupabaseAdmin();

  let payload;
  try {
    payload = JSON.parse(rawBody || '{}');
  } catch (parseErr) {
    // A payload that cannot parse will never parse, so returning non-200 here
    // would just make Meta retry it forever. Spool the raw text instead, so
    // even an unparseable body is recoverable by hand.
    await spoolFailure(supabase, {
      stage: 'parse',
      error: `JSON parse failed: ${parseErr.message}`,
      rawPayload: { raw: String(rawBody).slice(0, 8000) },
    });
    return { statusCode: 200, body: 'OK' };
  }

  try {
    // Navigate the Meta Cloud API nested structure
    // payload.entry[].changes[].value.messages[]
    const entries = payload.entry || [];
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const changes = entry.changes || [];
      for (const change of changes) {
        const value    = change.value || {};
        const messages = value.messages || [];
        const statuses = value.statuses || [];

        for (const msg of messages) {
          // Each message is isolated. One malformed message in a batch must
          // never prevent the others from being stored.
          try {
            await handleInbound(supabase, msg, value);
          } catch (msgErr) {
            console.error('whatsapp-webhook: message handling threw:', msgErr.message);
            await spoolFailure(supabase, {
              stage: 'message',
              waMessageId: msg && msg.id,
              fromPhone: msg && msg.from,
              error: (msgErr && msgErr.stack) || String(msgErr),
              rawPayload: msg,
            });
          }
        }

        // Delivery receipts. Meta sends these on the SAME webhook as inbound
        // messages, under `value.statuses[]` -- this handler used to ignore
        // them entirely, which is why a WhatsApp gift could be marked 'sent'
        // in digital_sends while Meta had actually failed to deliver it. The
        // row said delivered; the recipient's phone never buzzed.
        for (const st of statuses) {
          try {
            await processStatusUpdate(supabase, st);
            // Mirror the same receipt onto the conversation thread so the
            // dashboard shows real ticks rather than optimistic ones.
            await applyStatusToThread(supabase, st);
          } catch (stErr) {
            console.error('whatsapp-webhook: status handling threw:', stErr.message);
            await spoolFailure(supabase, {
              stage: 'status',
              waMessageId: st && st.id,
              error: (stErr && stErr.stack) || String(stErr),
              rawPayload: st,
            });
          }
        }
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    // Log but always return 200 — Meta retries on non-200 which would flood us
    console.error('whatsapp-webhook: processing error:', err.message);
    await spoolFailure(supabase, {
      stage: 'envelope',
      error: (err && err.stack) || String(err),
      rawPayload: payload,
    });
  }

  return { statusCode: 200, body: 'OK' };
};

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// INBOUND — CAPTURE FIRST, INTERPRET SECOND
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * STEP 1 (always): store the message, whatever it is.
 * STEP 2 (best effort): interpret it for keywords/automation.
 *
 * Step 2 failing can never undo step 1.
 */
async function handleInbound(supabase, msg, value) {
  if (!msg || !msg.from) return;

  // ── STEP 0: IS THIS ME? ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // A reply typed on the admin's own personal phone arrives here exactly like
  // a customer message would, because it was sent TO the ZivoGift number.
  // It must be routed onward to the customer, NOT filed as a new customer
  // conversation — otherwise the inbox would fill with your own replies
  // addressed to yourself.
  //
  // Returns true only when it genuinely handled the message. With
  // ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER unset (the default) this is a cheap no-op.
  try {
    if (await handleAdminRelayMessage(supabase, msg)) return;
  } catch (relayErr) {
    console.error('whatsapp-webhook: relay handling threw:', relayErr.message);
    await spoolFailure(supabase, {
      stage: 'relay',
      waMessageId: msg.id,
      fromPhone: msg.from,
      error: (relayErr && relayErr.stack) || String(relayErr),
      rawPayload: msg,
    });
    // Fall through to normal capture: an admin message stored as a
    // conversation is recoverable, a dropped one is not.
  }

  // Meta puts the sender's WhatsApp display name in a parallel contacts[]
  // array, keyed by wa_id — not on the message itself.
  const contactsArr = (value && value.contacts) || [];
  const profile = contactsArr.find((c) => c && c.wa_id === msg.from);
  const profileName = (profile && profile.profile && profile.profile.name) || null;

  // ── STEP 1: CAPTURE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  const stored = await recordInbound(supabase, { msg, profileName, rawPayload: msg });

  if (!stored.ok) {
    // Could not store it. Spool the raw message so it is still recoverable,
    // then continue to interpretation anyway — a gift unlock should not be
    // blocked by an inbox bookkeeping failure.
    await spoolFailure(supabase, {
      stage: 'capture',
      waMessageId: msg.id,
      fromPhone: msg.from,
      error: stored.error,
      rawPayload: msg,
    });
  }

  // A duplicate means Meta retried a webhook we already handled. Re-running
  // interpretation would be harmless for keywords but would re-send the
  // confirmation reply, so stop here.
  if (stored.duplicate) return;

  // ── STEP 1b: ALERT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Free email by default; paid WhatsApp relay only if explicitly enabled.
  // Never throws (see waNotify), so it cannot affect the 200 we owe Meta.
  if (stored.ok && stored.contact) {
    const preview = previewFor(stored.parsed || {});
    await notifyNewMessage(supabase, {
      contact: stored.contact,
      preview,
      isDuplicate: false,
      // Lets the relay quote the customer's own message back when you reply.
      sourceWaId: msg.id,
    });
  }

  // ── STEP 2: INTERPRET ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  await interpretInboundMessage(supabase, msg);
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// DELIVERY RECEIPTS (value.statuses[])
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Meta reports the real fate of every template message here, keyed by the
// message id we stored in digital_sends.provider_message_id at send time.
//
// Status lifecycle: sent -> delivered -> read. A terminal 'failed' carries an
// `errors[]` array explaining why (recipient not on WhatsApp, template paused,
// user blocked the business, and so on).
//
// We record this on digital_sends so:
//   - the admin delivery-health view reflects reality, not optimism
//   - a 'failed' WhatsApp gift can be rescued by the email fallback in
//     gift-scheduler.js instead of silently vanishing
//
// Requires supabase/consolidated/50_whatsapp_delivery.sql. Every write below
// is wrapped so that a missing column degrades to a warning rather than
// breaking the webhook (which would make Meta retry and flood us).

const WA_STATUS_RANK = { sent: 1, delivered: 2, read: 3, failed: 4 };

async function processStatusUpdate(supabase, st) {
  const messageId = st.id;
  const status    = String(st.status || '').toLowerCase();
  if (!messageId || !status) return;

  // Find the send this receipt belongs to. No match is normal and not an
  // error: session replies, care-package messages and reaction invites all
  // produce receipts too.
  const { data: rows, error: findErr } = await supabase
    .from('digital_sends')
    .select('id, wa_status, status, recipient_email, channel')
    .eq('provider_message_id', messageId)
    .limit(1);

  if (findErr) {
    console.warn('whatsapp-webhook: status lookup failed:', findErr.message);
    return;
  }

  // Not a gift send -- it may be a marketing campaign message. Campaign
  // receipts are recorded on campaign_recipients, which deliberately uses the
  // same column names (wa_status / wa_status_at / wa_error_code) so the
  // handling below reads identically.
  //
  // Crucially, there is NO email fallback for campaigns: a promotional
  // WhatsApp that Meta refused to deliver must not be silently re-sent down
  // another channel the customer did not choose.
  if (!rows || !rows.length) {
    await processCampaignStatusUpdate(supabase, st, messageId, status);
    return;
  }

  const row = rows[0];

  // Receipts can arrive out of order. Never let a late 'sent' overwrite an
  // already-recorded 'read'.
  const incomingRank = WA_STATUS_RANK[status] || 0;
  const currentRank  = WA_STATUS_RANK[row.wa_status] || 0;
  if (incomingRank && currentRank && incomingRank < currentRank && status !== 'failed') return;

  const patch = { wa_status: status, wa_status_at: new Date().toISOString() };

  if (status === 'failed') {
    const errs = Array.isArray(st.errors) ? st.errors : [];
    const first = errs[0] || {};
    const detail = first.error_data && first.error_data.details ? first.error_data.details : (first.title || 'unknown');
    patch.wa_error_code = first.code || null;
    patch.error_message = `WhatsApp delivery failed: ${detail}${first.code ? ` (code ${first.code})` : ''}`;

    // The gift never reached the recipient. If we have an email address, hand
    // the row back to gift-scheduler as a pending EMAIL send so the gift still
    // lands. This is the whole point of tracking receipts.
    if (row.recipient_email) {
      patch.status  = 'pending';
      patch.channel = 'email';
      patch.sent_at = null;
      patch.provider_message_id = null;
      patch.attempts = 0;
      patch.fallback_reason = 'whatsapp_delivery_failed';
      console.warn(`whatsapp-webhook: send ${row.id} failed on WhatsApp -- requeued for email fallback`);
    } else {
      patch.status = 'failed';
      console.error(`whatsapp-webhook: send ${row.id} failed on WhatsApp and has no email fallback: ${detail}`);
    }
  }

  const { error: updErr } = await supabase.from('digital_sends').update(patch).eq('id', row.id);
  if (updErr) {
    // Almost always "column does not exist" -- i.e. the migration has not been
    // run yet. Retry with just the columns that have always existed so a
    // failed delivery is still not lost.
    console.warn(`whatsapp-webhook: status update failed for ${row.id} (${updErr.message}) -- run 50_whatsapp_delivery.sql`);
    if (status === 'failed') {
      const minimal = row.recipient_email
        ? { status: 'pending', channel: 'email', sent_at: null, provider_message_id: null, attempts: 0, error_message: patch.error_message }
        : { status: 'failed', error_message: patch.error_message };
      await supabase.from('digital_sends').update(minimal).eq('id', row.id);
    }
    return;
  }

  console.log(`whatsapp-webhook: send ${row.id} -> wa_status=${status}`);
}

// ── CAMPAIGN DELIVERY RECEIPTS ──────────────────────────────────────────────
// Same receipt stream, different table. Added alongside the Campaign Center
// (supabase/consolidated/60_campaigns_and_admin_ops.sql).
//
// A 'failed' receipt on a MARKETING message is materially more important than
// on a gift: repeated failures are what drop a WhatsApp Business number's
// quality rating, and a downgraded number eventually stops delivering the
// TRANSACTIONAL gift templates too. Recording them is how the Emergency
// Console can warn you before that happens.
async function processCampaignStatusUpdate(supabase, st, messageId, status) {
  let row;
  try {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('campaign_recipients')
      .select('id, wa_status, campaign_id, phone10')
      .eq('provider_message_id', messageId)
      .limit(1);
    // Missing table = migration not applied yet. Not an error worth shouting
    // about on every unrelated receipt.
    if (error) return;
    if (!data || !data.length) return;
    row = data[0];
  } catch (e) {
    return;
  }

  const incomingRank = WA_STATUS_RANK[status] || 0;
  const currentRank  = WA_STATUS_RANK[row.wa_status] || 0;
  if (incomingRank && currentRank && incomingRank < currentRank && status !== 'failed') return;

  const patch = { wa_status: status, wa_status_at: new Date().toISOString() };

  if (status === 'failed') {
    const errs = Array.isArray(st.errors) ? st.errors : [];
    const first = errs[0] || {};
    const detail = first.error_data && first.error_data.details ? first.error_data.details : (first.title || 'unknown');
    patch.wa_error_code = first.code || null;
    patch.status = 'failed';
    patch.error_message = `WhatsApp delivery failed: ${detail}${first.code ? ` (code ${first.code})` : ''}`;
    console.warn(`whatsapp-webhook: campaign recipient ${row.id} failed: ${detail}`);
  }

  const { error: updErr } = await supabase.from('campaign_recipients').update(patch).eq('id', row.id);
  if (updErr) console.warn(`whatsapp-webhook: campaign receipt update failed for ${row.id}: ${updErr.message}`);
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// INTERPRETATION — keywords, opt-out, care package, condition unlock
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// This is the ORIGINAL logic, unchanged in behaviour. It now runs only AFTER
// the message has been stored, and it operates on a separate upper-cased copy
// so the stored transcript keeps its real casing.

async function interpretInboundMessage(supabase, msg) {
  const waMessageId = msg.id;
  const fromPhone   = msg.from; // E.164 without '+': '919876543210'

  // Keyword matching needs an upper-cased form. The STORED body keeps its
  // original casing -- this normalisation is local to this function only.
  const body = ((msg.text && msg.text.body) || '').trim().toUpperCase();

  // Non-text messages have no keyword to match. They are already safely
  // stored by handleInbound() above, so returning here loses nothing --
  // unlike the original code, where this same condition dropped the message
  // entirely.
  if (!fromPhone || !body) return;

  // ── Deduplicate via whatsapp_inbound_log ──────────────────────────────────
  // Insert with wa_message_id UNIQUE — if it exists already, skip processing.
  // Kept exactly as it was: this table is the dedupe key for gift unlocking
  // and care-package pause/resume, and rewriting it would risk double-firing
  // a gift.
  const { error: logInsertErr } = await supabase
    .from('whatsapp_inbound_log')
    .insert({ wa_message_id: waMessageId, from_phone: fromPhone, body });

  if (logInsertErr) {
    // 23505 = unique_violation — already processed, skip silently
    if (logInsertErr.code === '23505') return;
    console.error('whatsapp-webhook: log insert error:', logInsertErr.message);
    return;
  }

  // ── Feature #23: Condition-Based Delivery — keyword matching ─────────────
  // A sender texted a keyword. Find any digital_sends where:
  //   - condition_type  = 'sender_confirm'
  //   - condition_met   = false
  //   - condition_keyword (normalised upper) matches the incoming body text
  //   - sender_phone matches the from number (stripped to 10 digits)
  //
  // We match by sender_phone to ensure only the original buyer can unlock the
  // gift, not a random person who guesses the keyword.

  const fromPhone10 = fromPhone.replace(/^91/, '').slice(-10);

  // ── MARKETING OPT-OUT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Added with the Campaign Center. Meta requires that a business honour an
  // opt-out request, and "STOP" is the word people actually send.
  //
  // This runs BEFORE, and INDEPENDENTLY OF, the care-package branch below --
  // deliberately, because those two mean different things and both must
  // happen. STOP from a care-package recipient should pause their daily
  // messages AND suppress them from future marketing; the original code only
  // did the first.
  //
  // It only ever suppresses MARKETING. Order confirmations, delivery updates
  // and gift notifications are transactional and keep working, which is both
  // correct and what the customer actually wants.
  const OPTOUT_KEYWORDS = ['STOP', 'UNSUBSCRIBE', 'OPTOUT', 'OPT-OUT', 'OPT OUT'];
  if (OPTOUT_KEYWORDS.includes(body)) {
    try {
      const phone10 = fromPhone10;
      await supabase.from('marketing_optouts')
        .upsert({ phone10, source: 'whatsapp_stop' }, { onConflict: 'phone10' });
      // Drop anything still queued for them so the opt-out is immediate
      // rather than taking effect after the current campaign drains.
      await supabase.from('campaign_recipients')
        .update({ status: 'skipped', error_message: 'Recipient sent STOP on WhatsApp' })
        .eq('phone10', phone10).eq('status', 'queued');
      console.log(`whatsapp-webhook: ${phone10} opted out of marketing`);
    } catch (e) {
      // Missing table = migration not applied. Never let this break the
      // care-package pause handling that follows.
      console.warn('whatsapp-webhook: opt-out write failed:', (e && e.message) || e);
    }
  }

  // ── Care Package pause/resume — by RECIPIENT phone ───────────────────────
  // Unlike the condition-keyword feature (matched by SENDER phone, since the
  // sender is the one confirming), this matches by RECIPIENT phone — the new
  // parent receiving the daily messages is the one who needs to be able to
  // stop them.
  const PAUSE_KEYWORDS = ['STOP', 'PAUSE', 'MUTE'];
  const RESUME_KEYWORDS = ['RESUME', 'START', 'CONTINUE', 'UNMUTE'];

  if (PAUSE_KEYWORDS.includes(body) || RESUME_KEYWORDS.includes(body)) {
    const handled = await handleCarePackagePauseResume(supabase, fromPhone, fromPhone10, body, waMessageId);
    if (handled) return;
    // Falls through to condition-keyword matching below if no care package
    // matched this phone — e.g. someone's actual gift condition_keyword
    // happens to be the word "START".
  }

  const { data: pending, error: fetchErr } = await supabase
    .from('digital_sends')
    .select('id, condition_keyword, recipient_name, sender_name, sender_phone, status')
    .eq('condition_type', 'sender_confirm')
    .eq('condition_met', false)
    .eq('status', 'pending');

  if (fetchErr) {
    console.error('whatsapp-webhook: pending fetch error:', fetchErr.message);
    return;
  }

  const matched = (pending || []).find((row) => {
    const kw              = (row.condition_keyword || '').toUpperCase().trim();
    const rowPhone10      = (row.sender_phone || '').replace(/\D/g, '').replace(/^91/, '').slice(-10);
    return kw && kw === body && rowPhone10 === fromPhone10;
  });

  if (!matched) {
    // Not a condition keyword. Previously this was the end of the line and
    // the message was effectively discarded -- it is now already stored as a
    // customer conversation by handleInbound(), which is exactly the support
    // enquiry case this feature was built for.
    console.log(`whatsapp-webhook: no condition match for from=${fromPhone} — kept as a customer message`);
    return;
  }

  // ── Unlock the gift — flip condition_met = true ───────────────────────────
  const { error: updateErr } = await supabase
    .from('digital_sends')
    .update({ condition_met: true })
    .eq('id', matched.id);

  if (updateErr) {
    console.error(`whatsapp-webhook: failed to unlock send ${matched.id}:`, updateErr.message);
    return;
  }

  // Update the log row with the match details
  await supabase
    .from('whatsapp_inbound_log')
    .update({ matched_keyword: matched.condition_keyword, matched_send_id: matched.id, processed: true })
    .eq('wa_message_id', waMessageId);

  console.log(`whatsapp-webhook: condition unlocked for send ${matched.id} by ${fromPhone}`);

  // ── Send confirmation back to sender ─────────────────────────────────────
  // A short free-text reply confirming the gift will now be sent.
  // Meta allows 24-hour session messages (free text) only when the user
  // messaged you first within the last 24h — which is exactly the case here.
  //
  // Now routed through _lib/whatsappSession.js instead of a raw inline
  // fetch(): it gets a retry on transient Meta errors, and the reply is
  // recorded in the conversation thread so the dashboard shows what the
  // system said on your behalf.
  await sendAndRecordReply(supabase, {
    to: fromPhone,
    text: `✅ Got it! Your gift for *${matched.recipient_name}* is now unlocked and will be delivered shortly. — Zivogift`,
    contextMessageId: waMessageId,
    label: 'condition-unlock confirmation',
  });
}

// ── Care Package pause/resume handler ───────────────────────────────────
// Returns true if this phone matched an active/paused care package order
// (regardless of which keyword), false if no match — so the caller knows
// whether to fall through to condition-keyword matching instead.
async function handleCarePackagePauseResume(supabase, fromPhone, fromPhone10, body, waMessageId) {
  const isPause = ['STOP', 'PAUSE', 'MUTE'].includes(body);

  const { data: orders, error: fetchErr } = await supabase
    .from('care_package_orders')
    .select('id, recipient_phone, sender_name, status')
    .in('status', isPause ? ['active'] : ['paused']);

  if (fetchErr) {
    console.error('whatsapp-webhook: care package fetch error:', fetchErr.message);
    return false;
  }

  const matched = (orders || []).find((o) => {
    const orderPhone10 = (o.recipient_phone || '').replace(/\D/g, '').replace(/^91/, '').slice(-10);
    return orderPhone10 === fromPhone10;
  });

  if (!matched) return false;

  const newStatus = isPause ? 'paused' : 'active';
  const { error: updateErr } = await supabase
    .from('care_package_orders')
    .update({ status: newStatus, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() })
    .eq('id', matched.id);

  if (updateErr) {
    console.error(`whatsapp-webhook: failed to ${isPause ? 'pause' : 'resume'} care package ${matched.id}:`, updateErr.message);
    return false;
  }

  await supabase
    .from('whatsapp_inbound_log')
    .update({ matched_send_id: matched.id, processed: true })
    .eq('wa_message_id', waMessageId);

  console.log(`whatsapp-webhook: care package ${matched.id} ${isPause ? 'paused' : 'resumed'} by ${fromPhone}`);

  // Free-text confirmation — allowed here for the same reason as the
  // condition-keyword confirmation above: this is a reply WITHIN the 24h
  // session window opened by the recipient's own inbound message.
  const replyText = isPause
    ? `Okay, pausing the care messages from ${matched.sender_name} for now. Text RESUME anytime you'd like them back. 💛`
    : `Welcome back! Resuming the care messages from ${matched.sender_name}. — Zivogift`;

  await sendAndRecordReply(supabase, {
    to: fromPhone,
    text: replyText,
    contextMessageId: waMessageId,
    label: `care-package ${isPause ? 'pause' : 'resume'} confirmation`,
  });

  return true;
}

/**
 * Sends an automated free-text reply and mirrors it into the thread.
 *
 * Non-fatal by design: an automated courtesy reply failing must never stop
 * the webhook from returning 200, and must never undo the gift unlock or
 * care-package state change that has already been committed.
 */
async function sendAndRecordReply(supabase, { to, text, contextMessageId, label }) {
  try {
    const res = await sendWhatsAppText({ to, text, contextMessageId });

    await recordOutbound(supabase, {
      phone: to,
      waMessageId: res.ok ? res.messageId : null,
      msgType: 'text',
      body: text,
      status: res.ok ? 'sent' : 'failed',
      source: 'automation',
      sentByAdmin: null,
      contextWaId: contextMessageId || null,
      errorCode: res.ok ? null : String((res.error && res.error.code) || ''),
      errorMessage: res.ok ? null : (res.error && res.error.message) || null,
    });

    if (!res.ok) {
      console.warn(`whatsapp-webhook: ${label} failed:`, (res.error && res.error.message) || 'unknown');
    }
  } catch (replyErr) {
    console.warn(`whatsapp-webhook: ${label} threw:`, (replyErr && replyErr.message) || replyErr);
  }
}

FILE: netlify\functions\_lib\adminAuth.js

// netlify/functions/_lib/adminAuth.js
//
// ONE admin verifier for every admin function.
//
// WHY THIS EXISTS
// ---------------
// This codebase had TWO different, incompatible definitions of "admin":
//
//   1. js/admin.js (the browser)   -> SELECT is_admin FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid()
//   2. admin-analytics.js and
//      admin-whatsapp-diagnostics  -> an ADMIN_EMAILS comma-separated env allowlist,
//                                     which FAILS CLOSED when the env var is unset.
//
// So it is entirely possible to be logged into the admin panel, see Orders and
// Catalog fine, and get a bare 403 from the analytics tab -- with no message
// explaining that the cause is an unset Netlify env var. Debugging that needs
// a laptop.
//
// verifyAdmin() below accepts EITHER proof, and returns a structured reason on
// failure so the UI can say "ADMIN_EMAILS is not set and your profile row does
// not have is_admin = true" instead of "forbidden".
//
// Order of checks is deliberate: profiles.is_admin first, because it is the
// one you can change from a phone via the Supabase dashboard. ADMIN_EMAILS
// needs a redeploy.

const { createClient } = require('@supabase/supabase-js');
const { getSupabaseAdmin } = require('./supabaseAdmin');

function adminEmails() {
  return String(process.env.ADMIN_EMAILS || '')
    .split(',')
    .map((s) => s.trim().toLowerCase())
    .filter(Boolean);
}

/**
 * @param {string} authHeader  raw Authorization header ("Bearer <token>")
 * @returns {Promise<{ok:true, email:string, userId:string, via:string}
 *                 | {ok:false, reason:string, detail:string}>}
 */
async function verifyAdmin(authHeader) {
  const token = String(authHeader || '').replace(/^Bearer\s+/i, '').trim();
  if (!token) {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'no_token', detail: 'No Authorization header was sent. Log out and back in.' };
  }

  const url = process.env.SUPABASE_URL;
  const anon = process.env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY;
  if (!url || !anon) {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'server_misconfigured', detail: 'SUPABASE_URL or SUPABASE_ANON_KEY is not set on this deploy.' };
  }

  let user;
  try {
    const anonClient = createClient(url, anon);
    const { data, error } = await anonClient.auth.getUser(token);
    if (error || !data || !data.user) {
      return { ok: false, reason: 'bad_token', detail: 'Your session has expired. Log out and back in.' };
    }
    user = data.user;
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'auth_error', detail: String((e && e.message) || e) };
  }

  const email = String(user.email || '').toLowerCase();

  // ── Proof 1: profiles.is_admin ──────────────────────────────────────────
  // Read with the SERVICE ROLE key on purpose. Reading profiles with the
  // caller's own token would be subject to RLS, and a policy that hides other
  // rows can also hide your own is_admin flag depending on how it is written.
  try {
    const { data: prof } = await getSupabaseAdmin()
      .from('profiles').select('is_admin').eq('id', user.id).single();
    if (prof && prof.is_admin === true) {
      return { ok: true, email, userId: user.id, via: 'profiles.is_admin' };
    }
  } catch (e) {
    // Fall through to the env allowlist -- a profiles read failure must not
    // lock you out if ADMIN_EMAILS would have let you in.
    console.warn('adminAuth: profiles lookup failed:', (e && e.message) || e);
  }

  // ── Proof 2: ADMIN_EMAILS allowlist ─────────────────────────────────────
  const allow = adminEmails();
  if (allow.length && allow.indexOf(email) !== -1) {
    return { ok: true, email, userId: user.id, via: 'ADMIN_EMAILS' };
  }

  return {
    ok: false,
    reason: 'not_admin',
    detail: allow.length
      ? `${email} is not in ADMIN_EMAILS and profiles.is_admin is not true for this account.`
      : `ADMIN_EMAILS is not set on this deploy, and profiles.is_admin is not true for ${email}. ` +
        `Fix with: update public.profiles set is_admin = true where id = '${user.id}';`,
  };
}

/** Standard JSON headers for every admin endpoint. */
const JSON_HEADERS = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Cache-Control': 'no-store' };

function json(statusCode, body) {
  return { statusCode, headers: JSON_HEADERS, body: JSON.stringify(body) };
}

/**
 * Wraps a handler so every admin function gets identical auth, identical
 * error shape, and a CORS preflight answer, without copy-paste drift.
 *
 * @param {(event, ctx:{admin:object, supabase:object}) => Promise<object>} fn
 */
function withAdmin(fn) {
  return async function (event) {
    if (event.httpMethod === 'OPTIONS') {
      return { statusCode: 204, headers: { ...JSON_HEADERS, 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'Content-Type, Authorization' }, body: '' };
    }
    try {
      const admin = await verifyAdmin(event.headers.authorization || event.headers.Authorization);
      if (!admin.ok) return json(403, { error: admin.reason, detail: admin.detail });
      return await fn(event, { admin, supabase: getSupabaseAdmin() });
    } catch (e) {
      console.error('admin function fatal:', (e && e.stack) || e);
      return json(500, { error: 'server_error', detail: String((e && e.message) || e) });
    }
  };
}

/** Safe JSON body parse -- returns {} rather than throwing on empty/invalid. */
function parseBody(event) {
  try { return JSON.parse(event.body || '{}'); } catch (e) { return {}; }
}

module.exports = { verifyAdmin, withAdmin, json, parseBody, JSON_HEADERS, adminEmails };

// netlify/functions/_lib/adminSettings.js
//
// DB-backed kill switches.
//
// WHY NOT ENV VARS
// ----------------
// A Netlify env var change requires a redeploy. A redeploy requires a laptop
// and burns build credits -- and the whole reason these switches exist is for
// the situation where you have neither. A row in public.admin_settings can be
// flipped from the admin panel on a phone and takes effect on the very next
// cron tick with no deploy.
//
// FAIL-OPEN, DELIBERATELY
// -----------------------
// isPaused() returns FALSE when the settings table cannot be read (migration
// not applied, transient DB error). That means a database problem does NOT
// silently stop your real gift deliveries -- gift-scheduler keeps running.
// The switches are a manual brake, not a safety interlock, and treating them
// as an interlock would make a DB blip look like a total outage.
//
// The one exception is guardCampaigns(), used only by campaign-sender and
// festival-scheduler: marketing is the thing you would rather have stop by
// accident than send by accident, but even there a read failure logs loudly.

const { getSupabaseAdmin } = require('./supabaseAdmin');

const DEFAULTS = {
  pause_campaigns: false,
  pause_all_schedulers: false,
  pause_festivals: false,

  // ── CUSTOMER MESSAGES (WhatsApp Inbox) ────────────────────────────────────
  // Added with supabase/consolidated/80_whatsapp_inbox.sql.
  //
  // NOTE ON DIRECTION: these are PAUSE flags, so false = feature ON. That
  // reads backwards for the relay, which is why its seeded row is `true`.
  //
  // pause_wa_alerts — stops the free email alert sent to ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL
  //   when a customer messages the WhatsApp number. Defaults to false (alerts
  //   ON) because the alert costs nothing and an unseen bulk-order enquiry is
  //   a lost order.
  //
  // pause_wa_relay — stops the WhatsApp relay to ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER. This
  //   is the only part of the inbox that costs money per message (a
  //   business-initiated template when the 24h window with you has lapsed),
  //   so 80_whatsapp_inbox.sql SEEDS THIS ROW AS true = relay OFF.
  //
  //   The DEFAULT here is also true, deliberately. getSettings() merges the
  //   database rows OVER these defaults, so if 80_whatsapp_inbox.sql has not
  //   been applied yet there is no row and the default is what applies. A
  //   default of false would mean "migration not run" silently equals "start
  //   spending money", which is the wrong way for a billing flag to fail.
  pause_wa_alerts: false,
  pause_wa_relay: true,
};

async function getSettings(supabase) {
  const db = supabase || getSupabaseAdmin();
  const out = { ...DEFAULTS, _readable: true };
  try {
    const { data, error } = await db.from('admin_settings').select('key, value, updated_at');
    if (error) throw new Error(error.message);
    for (const row of data || []) {
      out[row.key] = row.value === true || row.value === 'true';
      out[`${row.key}_updated_at`] = row.updated_at;
    }
  } catch (e) {
    console.warn('adminSettings: read failed, using defaults (run 60_campaigns_and_admin_ops.sql):', (e && e.message) || e);
    out._readable = false;
    out._error = String((e && e.message) || e);
  }
  return out;
}

async function isPaused(key, supabase) {
  const s = await getSettings(supabase);
  return s[key] === true;
}

async function setSetting(key, value, supabase, userId) {
  if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(DEFAULTS, key)) {
    throw new Error(`Unknown setting "${key}". Valid: ${Object.keys(DEFAULTS).join(', ')}`);
  }
  const db = supabase || getSupabaseAdmin();
  const { error } = await db
    .from('admin_settings')
    .upsert({ key, value: !!value, updated_at: new Date().toISOString(), updated_by: userId || null }, { onConflict: 'key' });
  if (error) throw new Error(error.message);
  return { key, value: !!value };
}

/**
 * Called at the TOP of every scheduler that sends marketing. Returns a
 * short-circuit response object when paused, or null to continue.
 */
async function guardCampaigns(supabase, label) {
  const s = await getSettings(supabase);
  if (s.pause_all_schedulers) {
    console.log(`${label}: halted -- pause_all_schedulers is ON`);
    return { statusCode: 200, body: JSON.stringify({ skipped: 'pause_all_schedulers' }) };
  }
  if (s.pause_campaigns) {
    console.log(`${label}: halted -- pause_campaigns is ON`);
    return { statusCode: 200, body: JSON.stringify({ skipped: 'pause_campaigns' }) };
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * Called at the TOP of the NUDGE schedulers (reminder-scheduler,
 * occasion-scheduler) and any other non-campaign automation.
 *
 * Separate from guardCampaigns() on purpose: a nudge scheduler must respect
 * the global "pause everything" brake, but must NOT be stopped by
 * `pause_campaigns`, which is specifically about broadcast campaigns. Before
 * this existed, the Emergency tab's "Pause EVERYTHING" button did not
 * actually stop the daily reminder and occasion crons -- they had no
 * knowledge of the settings table at all.
 */
async function guardSchedulers(supabase, label) {
  const s = await getSettings(supabase);
  if (s.pause_all_schedulers) {
    console.log(`${label}: halted -- pause_all_schedulers is ON`);
    return { statusCode: 200, body: JSON.stringify({ skipped: 'pause_all_schedulers' }) };
  }
  return null;
}

module.exports = { DEFAULTS, getSettings, isPaused, setSetting, guardCampaigns, guardSchedulers };

FILE: netlify\functions\_lib\analytics-core.js

/* ============================================================================
   ZIVOGIFT · analytics-core.js  (Run 6 — Admin BI, pure core)
   Aggregates rows already fetched from the DB. No Supabase/I/O → unit-testable.
   Uses ONLY columns seen in the codebase. Order REVENUE is defensive
   (detectAmountColumn) because the orders schema wasn't provided — if no numeric
   amount-like column is found, revenue is reported as null with a reason, never
   a fabricated number.
   ============================================================================ */
'use strict';

function inc(map, key) { key = key || 'unknown'; map[key] = (map[key] || 0) + 1; }

function aggregateGiftStats(sends) {
  sends = Array.isArray(sends) ? sends : [];
  var byStatus = {}, byType = {}, byChannel = {};
  var sent = 0, opened = 0, reacted = 0, completed = 0, failed = 0, pending = 0, capsules = 0;
  var openDelaySum = 0, openDelayN = 0;
  sends.forEach(function (r) {
    inc(byStatus, r.status); inc(byType, r.gift_type); inc(byChannel, r.channel);
    if (r.status === 'sent') sent++;
    if (r.status === 'failed') failed++;
    if (r.status === 'pending') pending++;
    if (r.opened_at) opened++;
    if (r.reveal_completed_at) completed++;
    if (r.reaction) reacted++;
    if (r.is_time_capsule) capsules++;
    if (r.first_open_delay_seconds != null && !isNaN(r.first_open_delay_seconds)) { openDelaySum += Number(r.first_open_delay_seconds); openDelayN++; }
  });
  var rate = function (num, den) { return den > 0 ? Math.round((num / den) * 1000) / 10 : 0; };
  var giftPerformance = Object.keys(byType).map(function (t) { return { gift_type: t, count: byType[t] }; })
    .sort(function (a, b) { return b.count - a.count; });
  return {
    total: sends.length, sent: sent, pending: pending, failed: failed, time_capsules: capsules,
    open_rate_pct: rate(opened, sent), completion_rate_pct: rate(completed, opened), reaction_rate_pct: rate(reacted, sent),
    avg_open_delay_seconds: openDelayN ? Math.round(openDelaySum / openDelayN) : null,
    by_status: byStatus, by_channel: byChannel, gift_performance: giftPerformance
  };
}

function buildFailedList(sends, limit) {
  limit = limit || 100;
  return (Array.isArray(sends) ? sends : [])
    .filter(function (r) { return r.status === 'failed'; })
    .map(function (r) { return { id: r.id, recipient_name: r.recipient_name || null, channel: r.channel || null,
      gift_type: r.gift_type || null, attempts: r.attempts || 0, error_message: r.error_message || null, created_at: r.created_at || null }; })
    .sort(function (a, b) { return (b.attempts || 0) - (a.attempts || 0); })
    .slice(0, limit);
}

function isNumeric(v) { return v != null && v !== '' && !isNaN(Number(v)); }

function detectAmountColumn(sampleRow) {
  if (!sampleRow || typeof sampleRow !== 'object') return null;
  var prefer = ['amount_paid', 'total_amount', 'amount', 'total', 'grand_total', 'price', 'order_total', 'paid_amount'];
  var keys = Object.keys(sampleRow);
  for (var i = 0; i < prefer.length; i++) if (keys.indexOf(prefer[i]) !== -1 && isNumeric(sampleRow[prefer[i]])) return prefer[i];
  for (var j = 0; j < keys.length; j++) { var k = keys[j]; if (/amount|total|price|paid/i.test(k) && isNumeric(sampleRow[k])) return k; }
  return null;
}

function aggregateRevenue(orders, opts) {
  opts = opts || {};
  orders = Array.isArray(orders) ? orders : [];
  if (!orders.length) return { available: false, reason: 'no_orders', total: 0 };
  var amountKey = opts.amountKey || detectAmountColumn(orders[0]);
  if (!amountKey) return { available: false, reason: 'no_amount_column_detected', total: 0 };
  var paid = opts.paidStatuses || ['paid', 'processing', 'packed', 'out_for_delivery', 'delivered'];
  var statusKey = opts.statusKey || (('status' in orders[0]) ? 'status' : null);
  var total = 0, count = 0, byStatus = {};
  orders.forEach(function (o) {
    var amt = Number(o[amountKey]); if (isNaN(amt)) return;
    var st = statusKey ? o[statusKey] : null;
    if (statusKey && paid.indexOf(st) === -1) return;
    total += amt; count++;
    if (st) byStatus[st] = (byStatus[st] || 0) + amt;
  });
  return { available: true, amount_column: amountKey, paid_orders: count, total: Math.round(total * 100) / 100, by_status: byStatus };
}

function ordersByDay(orders, dateKey) {
  orders = Array.isArray(orders) ? orders : [];
  dateKey = dateKey || 'created_at';
  var days = {};
  orders.forEach(function (o) { var d = o[dateKey]; if (!d) return; var day = String(d).slice(0, 10); days[day] = (days[day] || 0) + 1; });
  return Object.keys(days).sort().map(function (day) { return { day: day, count: days[day] }; });
}

module.exports = { aggregateGiftStats, buildFailedList, detectAmountColumn, aggregateRevenue, ordersByDay, isNumeric };

// netlify/functions/_lib/anthropicHelper.js
//
// Shared server-side AI call helper. Used by noteStoryHelper.js,
// numerologyHelper.js, moderateMessage.js, carePackageContentGuard.js,
// care-package-generator.js, and ai-generate.js (the single proxy every
// client-triggered AI feature calls: AI Polish, Character Drop, Roast
// Certificate, Horoscope Drop).
//
// SWITCHED FROM ANTHROPIC TO GOOGLE GEMINI (Jul 2026): the Anthropic
// account behind this key ran out of billing credit ("Your credit balance
// is too low..." — a paid-only account, no free tier), and the decision was
// made not to fund it. Gemini 2.5 Flash has a genuinely permanent free
// tier (no credit card, ~1,500 requests/day as of writing), so every
// caller above now runs at $0/month. Filename kept as anthropicHelper.js
// on purpose so the 6 files above didn't need their require() paths
// touched — only this file's internals changed. The exported function
// signature (generateText({system, prompt, maxTokens}) -> string) is
// unchanged, so no caller needed to change either.
//
// Needs env var GEMINI_API_KEY (get one free, no card required, at
// https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) set in Netlify → Site settings →
// Environment variables, then a redeploy.
//
// If GEMINI_API_KEY isn't set, generateText() throws — callers are
// expected to catch this and fall back to a static template so a missing
// env var never blocks an order confirmation email (or a studio feature)
// from working.

async function generateText({ system, prompt, maxTokens }) {
  const apiKey = process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY;
  if (!apiKey) {
    throw new Error('GEMINI_API_KEY not set');
  }

  const model = 'gemini-2.5-flash';
  const url = `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/${model}:generateContent?key=${apiKey}`;

  const body = {
    contents: [{ role: 'user', parts: [{ text: prompt }] }],
    generationConfig: { maxOutputTokens: maxTokens || 500 },
  };
  if (system) {
    body.systemInstruction = { parts: [{ text: system }] };
  }

  const res = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });

  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Gemini API error (${res.status}): ${text}`);
  }

  const data = await res.json();
  const candidate = data.candidates && data.candidates[0];
  const parts = candidate && candidate.content && candidate.content.parts;
  const text = parts && parts[0] ? (parts[0].text || '') : '';

  // Gemini can stop early with finishReason MAX_TOKENS on the tighter
  // maxTokens budgets some callers pass (e.g. 300) before emitting any
  // text — surface that clearly instead of throwing a confusing "empty
  // response" error.
  if (!text) {
    const reason = candidate && candidate.finishReason;
    throw new Error(`Gemini returned an empty response${reason ? ' (finishReason: ' + reason + ')' : ''}`);
  }
  return text.trim();
}

module.exports = { generateText };

// netlify/functions/_lib/audience.js
//
// THE SINGLE CHOKE POINT for "who receives a campaign".
//
// Every path that sends marketing -- the admin preview count, the test send,
// the real launch, and the festival scheduler -- resolves its recipient list
// through resolveAudience() here. That is deliberate: opt-out filtering and
// de-duplication are applied INSIDE this module, so there is no code path
// that can accidentally bypass them. If you add a new campaign trigger later,
// route it through here too.
//
// Data source is public.v_customers (see 60_campaigns_and_admin_ops.sql),
// which is a view over `orders` -- because public.profiles has no email
// column, orders is the only reachable source of customer contact details in
// this schema.
//
// Read with the SERVICE ROLE key. RLS on `orders` would otherwise reduce the
// view to the calling admin's own orders.

const SEGMENTS = {
  all: {
    label: 'Everyone who has ever ordered',
    describe: 'Every unique customer, paid or not.',
    apply: (q) => q,
  },
  paid: {
    label: 'Paid customers only',
    describe: 'At least one order that reached paid or beyond. This is your real customer list.',
    apply: (q) => q.gt('paid_orders_count', 0),
  },
  last_30: {
    label: 'Ordered in the last 30 days',
    describe: 'Warm and recent.',
    apply: (q) => q.gte('last_order_at', daysAgo(30)),
  },
  last_90: {
    label: 'Ordered in the last 90 days',
    describe: 'Still remember who you are.',
    apply: (q) => q.gte('last_order_at', daysAgo(90)),
  },
  last_180: {
    label: 'Ordered in the last 180 days',
    describe: 'The widest sensible reactivation window.',
    apply: (q) => q.gte('last_order_at', daysAgo(180)),
  },
  repeat: {
    label: 'Repeat buyers (2+ paid orders)',
    describe: 'Your best audience. Smallest, highest converting.',
    apply: (q) => q.gte('paid_orders_count', 2),
  },
  high_value: {
    label: 'High value (lifetime spend >= 1000)',
    describe: 'Worth a more premium offer than a blanket discount.',
    apply: (q) => q.gte('lifetime_value', 1000),
  },
  dormant_90: {
    label: 'Dormant (paid before, nothing for 90+ days)',
    describe: 'The win-back list. Pair this with an actual discount code.',
    apply: (q) => q.gt('paid_orders_count', 0).lt('last_order_at', daysAgo(90)),
  },
  digital_buyers: {
    label: 'Bought a digital gift',
    describe: 'Price-sensitive, fast-converting, good for impulse offers.',
    apply: (q) => q.eq('has_digital', true),
  },
  physical_buyers: {
    label: 'Bought a physical gift',
    describe: 'Higher order value. Good for festival and bulk pushes.',
    apply: (q) => q.eq('has_physical', true),
  },
};

function daysAgo(n) {
  return new Date(Date.now() - n * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
}

function segmentList() {
  return Object.keys(SEGMENTS).map((k) => ({
    key: k, label: SEGMENTS[k].label, describe: SEGMENTS[k].describe,
  }));
}

// Supabase caps a single PostgREST response (default 1000 rows). A silent
// truncation here would mean "campaign sent to everyone" quietly meaning
// "sent to the first 1000", which is exactly the kind of bug you would not
// notice until it mattered. So we page explicitly.
const PAGE = 1000;
const MAX_ROWS = 50000; // hard sanity ceiling

/**
 * Resolve a segment into a de-duplicated, opt-out-filtered recipient list.
 *
 * @param {object} supabase  service-role client
 * @param {string} segmentKey
 * @param {string} channel   'email' | 'whatsapp' | 'both'
 * @returns {Promise<{recipients:Array, stats:object}>}
 */
async function resolveAudience(supabase, segmentKey, channel) {
  const seg = SEGMENTS[segmentKey];
  if (!seg) throw new Error(`Unknown segment "${segmentKey}". Valid: ${Object.keys(SEGMENTS).join(', ')}`);

  const rows = [];
  for (let from = 0; from < MAX_ROWS; from += PAGE) {
    let q = supabase
      .from('v_customers')
      .select('customer_key, email, phone10, full_name, orders_count, paid_orders_count, lifetime_value, last_order_at, has_digital, has_physical, opted_out')
      .order('last_order_at', { ascending: false })
      .range(from, from + PAGE - 1);

    q = seg.apply(q);

    const { data, error } = await q;
    if (error) throw new Error(`Audience query failed: ${error.message}`);
    if (!data || !data.length) break;
    rows.push(...data);
    if (data.length < PAGE) break;
  }

  const stats = {
    segment: segmentKey,
    segment_label: seg.label,
    matched: rows.length,
    opted_out: 0,
    no_email: 0,
    no_phone: 0,
    email_recipients: 0,
    whatsapp_recipients: 0,
  };

  const wantEmail = channel === 'email' || channel === 'both';
  const wantWa = channel === 'whatsapp' || channel === 'both';

  const seen = new Set();
  const recipients = [];

  for (const r of rows) {
    // The view already computes opted_out, but re-checking here means the
    // filter survives even if someone later edits the view. Defence in depth
    // on the one thing that must never fail open.
    if (r.opted_out) { stats.opted_out += 1; continue; }
    if (seen.has(r.customer_key)) continue;
    seen.add(r.customer_key);

    const email = validEmail(r.email) ? r.email : null;
    const phone10 = validPhone10(r.phone10) ? r.phone10 : null;

    if (!email) stats.no_email += 1;
    if (!phone10) stats.no_phone += 1;

    const channels = [];
    if (wantEmail && email) { channels.push('email'); stats.email_recipients += 1; }
    if (wantWa && phone10) { channels.push('whatsapp'); stats.whatsapp_recipients += 1; }
    if (!channels.length) continue;

    recipients.push({
      customer_key: r.customer_key,
      full_name: firstName(r.full_name),
      email,
      phone10,
      channels,
    });
  }

  stats.reachable = recipients.length;
  return { recipients, stats };
}

// Intentionally conservative rather than RFC-complete. A malformed address in
// a bulk send costs sender reputation, so anything doubtful is dropped.
function validEmail(e) {
  if (!e) return false;
  const s = String(e).trim();
  if (s.length < 6 || s.length > 254) return false;
  if (!/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@,]+\.[a-z]{2,}$/i.test(s)) return false;
  if (/^(test|noreply|no-reply|example)@/i.test(s)) return false;
  return true;
}

// Matches the convention in _lib/phoneUtil.js -- Indian mobiles start 6-9.
function validPhone10(p) {
  if (!p) return false;
  const d = String(p).replace(/\D/g, '');
  return d.length === 10 && /^[6-9]/.test(d);
}

// WhatsApp templates and email greetings both take a first name. Falling back
// to "there" rather than an empty string keeps "Hey there 👋" readable.
function firstName(full) {
  const n = String(full || '').trim().split(/\s+/)[0];
  if (!n || n.length < 2) return 'there';
  return n.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + n.slice(1);
}

module.exports = { SEGMENTS, segmentList, resolveAudience, validEmail, validPhone10, firstName, daysAgo };

// netlify/functions/_lib/campaignEmail.js
//
// Renders a campaign into the SAME branded email shell every transactional
// Zivogift mail already uses, so a marketing email does not look like it came
// from a different company than the order confirmation.
//
// It imports emailShell / ctaButton / escapeHtml / BRAND from _lib/resend.js
// -- all four are already exported there, so nothing in resend.js changes.
//
// THE FOOTER IS THE POINT
// -----------------------
// emailShell() accepts a footerHtml override. That is the hook used here to
// inject the per-recipient unsubscribe link. Every marketing email built by
// this module carries one. There is no code path in campaign-sender.js that
// builds marketing HTML any other way, which is how the guarantee is kept.
//
// A plain-text alternative is also produced. sendEmail() already forwards
// `text` to Resend, and multipart/alternative scores materially better with
// spam filters than HTML-only -- which matters far more for bulk sends than
// for transactional ones.

const { emailShell, ctaButton, escapeHtml, BRAND } = require('./resend');
const { unsubUrl } = require('./unsubToken');

// Local row helpers. resend.js keeps its own `row` object module-private, so
// these are duplicated rather than imported -- deliberately, because changing
// resend.js's exports to share them would touch the transactional gift path,
// which is the one path in this codebase that must not be disturbed.
const R = {
  eyebrow: (t, accent) =>
    `<tr><td align="center" style="padding:0 0 10px;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:2px;text-transform:uppercase;color:${accent};">${escapeHtml(t)}</td></tr>`,
  headline: (t) =>
    `<tr><td align="center" class="zg-head" style="padding:0 0 12px;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:28px;line-height:36px;font-weight:bold;color:${BRAND.ink};">${escapeHtml(t)}</td></tr>`,
  body: (html) =>
    `<tr><td align="center" style="padding:0 0 20px;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:24px;color:${BRAND.muted};">${html}</td></tr>`,
  cta: (url, label, accent) =>
    `<tr><td align="center" style="padding:4px 0 8px;">${ctaButton(url, label, accent)}</td></tr>`,
};

/**
 * Turn the admin's plain-text message into safe HTML paragraphs.
 * Escaped first, then newlines become breaks -- so an admin pasting an
 * apostrophe or an ampersand cannot break the markup, and pasting a <script>
 * tag does nothing.
 */
function paragraphs(text) {
  return String(text || '')
    .split(/\n{2,}/)
    .map((p) => escapeHtml(p.trim()).replace(/\n/g, '<br />'))
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map((p) => `<div style="margin:0 0 14px;">${p}</div>`)
    .join('');
}

/**
 * @param {object} campaign  row from public.campaigns
 * @param {object} recipient {full_name, email, phone10, customer_key}
 * @returns {{subject:string, html:string, text:string}}
 */
function renderCampaignEmail(campaign, recipient) {
  const accent = BRAND.gold;
  const name = recipient.full_name || 'there';
  const ctaUrl = campaign.cta_url || (process.env.SITE_URL || 'https://zivogift.com');
  const ctaLabel = campaign.cta_label || 'Visit Zivogift';

  const link = unsubUrl({
    email: recipient.email,
    phone10: recipient.phone10,
    campaignId: campaign.id,
  });

  const bodyRows =
    R.eyebrow('Zivogift', accent) +
    R.headline(campaign.subject || campaign.name) +
    R.body(`<div style="margin:0 0 14px;">Hi ${escapeHtml(name)},</div>${paragraphs(campaign.body)}`) +
    R.cta(ctaUrl, ctaLabel, accent);

  // The unsubscribe link is plain and visible, not hidden in 8px grey. A link
  // people can find is a link they use INSTEAD of hitting "report spam", and
  // spam complaints are what actually kill a sending domain.
  const footerHtml =
    `Made with care at <a href="https://zivogift.com" style="color:#8a847b;text-decoration:underline;">zivogift.com</a>` +
    `<br /><br />You are receiving this because you ordered from Zivogift.` +
    `<br /><a href="${escapeHtml(link)}" style="color:#8a847b;text-decoration:underline;">Unsubscribe from offers</a>` +
    ` &middot; <a href="mailto:hello@zivogift.com" style="color:#8a847b;text-decoration:underline;">hello@zivogift.com</a>`;

  const html = emailShell({
    title: campaign.subject || campaign.name,
    preheader: String(campaign.body || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, 140),
    bodyRows,
    accent,
    footerHtml,
  });

  const text = [
    `Hi ${name},`,
    '',
    String(campaign.body || '').trim(),
    '',
    `${ctaLabel}: ${ctaUrl}`,
    '',
    '---',
    'You are receiving this because you ordered from Zivogift.',
    `Unsubscribe: ${link}`,
    'hello@zivogift.com',
  ].join('\n');

  return { subject: campaign.subject || campaign.name, html, text };
}

/**
 * List-Unsubscribe headers. Resend forwards custom headers, and Gmail /
 * Yahoo now REQUIRE one-click unsubscribe for bulk senders -- without these,
 * bulk mail to Gmail addresses gets throttled or junked regardless of
 * content quality.
 */
function unsubHeaders(campaign, recipient) {
  const link = unsubUrl({ email: recipient.email, phone10: recipient.phone10, campaignId: campaign.id });
  return {
    'List-Unsubscribe': `<${link}>`,
    'List-Unsubscribe-Post': 'List-Unsubscribe=One-Click',
  };
}

module.exports = { renderCampaignEmail, unsubHeaders, paragraphs };
