// netlify/functions/_lib/cardFonts.js
//
// THE ONLY PLACE IN THIS CODEBASE THAT MAY `require('sharp')`.
//
// ── Why this file exists ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Sharp rasterizes SVG through librsvg, and librsvg resolves every
// `font-family` through fontconfig. The Netlify Functions Lambda image ships
// no fonts and no fontconfig cache. Geometry (<rect>, <circle>, <line>,
// gradients) is font-independent so it draws normally — but every <text> and
// <tspan> resolves to no font and rasterizes to NOTHING.
//
// That is the exact symptom the gift cards had: a correct-looking PNG with all
// the copy missing, returned as HTTP 200, mailed out, and marked `sent`.
//
// ── The fix ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 1. Ship our own TTFs in netlify/fonts/ (populated by scripts/fetch-fonts.js,
//    bundled via `included_files` in netlify.toml).
// 2. Point fontconfig at ONLY that directory with our own fonts.conf, so the
//    render is identical on a laptop with 400 system fonts and on a bare
//    Lambda with zero.
// 3. Set FONTCONFIG_PATH / FONTCONFIG_FILE at module top level — BEFORE
//    require('sharp') runs. The native binding reads these once at
//    initialisation; setting them afterwards is a no-op. This is also why no
//    other module may require Sharp directly: whoever requires it first wins.
// 4. Probe on cold start. Render a known glyph, count non-background pixels,
//    and throw if the bitmap is blank. A fontless deploy now fails LOUDLY
//    (500 → gift-scheduler retries → admin alert) instead of silently
//    delivering blank cards.

const path = require('path');
const fs   = require('fs');

// ── 1. Locate the bundled font directory ────────────────────────────────────
// Netlify's esbuild bundler flattens functions into .netlify/functions-serve/
// <name>/, and `included_files` are copied relative to the repo root. Both
// layouts are checked so this works locally (netlify dev), in `netlify build`
// and in production.
const FONT_DIR_CANDIDATES = [
  path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'fonts'),                 // netlify/fonts  (source tree)
  path.join(process.env.LAMBDA_TASK_ROOT || '', 'netlify', 'fonts'),
  path.join(process.cwd(), 'netlify', 'fonts'),
];

function findFontDir() {
  for (const dir of FONT_DIR_CANDIDATES) {
    if (!dir) continue;
    try {
      if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'fonts.conf'))) return dir;
    } catch { /* unreadable candidate — try the next */ }
  }
  return null;
}

const FONT_DIR = findFontDir();

// ── 2. Point fontconfig at it, before Sharp loads ───────────────────────────
// netlify/fonts/fonts.conf is a TEMPLATE containing __ZG_FONT_DIR__. A
// relative <dir> in fontconfig resolves against the process CWD, not against
// the config file — and the CWD on Lambda is not the bundle directory, so a
// relative path would silently find no fonts (fontconfig only warns:
// "ambiguous path in <dir> element"). We substitute the absolute path and
// write the resolved config to /tmp, which is the one writable path on Lambda.
if (FONT_DIR) {
  try {
    const template = fs.readFileSync(path.join(FONT_DIR, 'fonts.conf'), 'utf8');
    const resolvedDir = '/tmp/zg-fontconfig';
    fs.mkdirSync(resolvedDir, { recursive: true });
    fs.mkdirSync('/tmp/fontconfig-cache', { recursive: true });

    const resolvedConf = path.join(resolvedDir, 'fonts.conf');
    fs.writeFileSync(resolvedConf, template.split('__ZG_FONT_DIR__').join(FONT_DIR));

    process.env.FONTCONFIG_PATH = resolvedDir;
    process.env.FONTCONFIG_FILE = resolvedConf;
    // fontconfig needs a writable cache dir, or it re-scans on every cold
    // start and logs a warning each time.
    process.env.XDG_CACHE_HOME = process.env.XDG_CACHE_HOME || '/tmp';
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('cardFonts: could not materialise fonts.conf:', err.message);
  }
} else {
  console.error(
    'cardFonts: netlify/fonts/fonts.conf not found. Run `node scripts/fetch-fonts.js` ' +
    'and confirm netlify.toml has the fonts directory in [functions] included_files. ' +
    'Card text WILL be blank until this is fixed.'
  );
}

// ── 3. Load Sharp (single require site for the whole codebase) ──────────────
let sharp = null;
let sharpLoadError = null;
try {
  sharp = require('sharp');
} catch (err) {
  sharpLoadError = err;
}

// ── 4. Font family names ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// These are the *real* family names inside the TTFs fetched by
// scripts/fetch-fonts.js. fonts.conf aliases the generic CSS families
// (sans-serif / serif / monospace / system-ui / cursive) onto them, so the SVG
// builders can keep using generic names and still get a deterministic render.
const FAMILIES = {
  sans:  'Inter',
  serif: 'Playfair Display',
  mono:  'JetBrains Mono',
  hand:  'Caveat',
  display: 'Bebas Neue',
};

// Maps the `font` hint stored on each vibe token to a concrete family.
function familyFor(fontHint) {
  switch (fontHint) {
    case 'serif':     return FAMILIES.serif;
    case 'monospace': return FAMILIES.mono;
    case 'cursive':   return FAMILIES.hand;
    default:          return FAMILIES.sans;
  }
}

// ── 5. Cold-start glyph probe ───────────────────────────────────────────────
// Renders one large letter on a black square and counts pixels that are not
// black. If fontconfig found nothing the canvas stays uniformly black and the
// count is 0 — which is precisely the failure we are guarding against.
let probeState = null; // null = not run, true = ok, Error = failed

async function assertGlyphsRender() {
  if (probeState === true) return;
  if (probeState instanceof Error) throw probeState;

  if (!sharp) {
    probeState = new Error(
      'sharp is not installed or failed to load: ' +
      (sharpLoadError ? sharpLoadError.message : 'unknown') +
      '. Run `npm install sharp` and keep it in external_node_modules in netlify.toml.'
    );
    throw probeState;
  }

  // ── PRE-FLIGHT: at least one real font file must exist ────────────────────
  // This check is NOT redundant with the pixel probe below, and it must come
  // first. If fontconfig resolves to a directory containing zero fonts,
  // librsvg does not return a blank bitmap — it SEGFAULTS the whole process
  // (reproduced: exit 139). A segfault cannot be caught in JS, so by the time
  // the pixel probe would run it is already too late. Refusing here, in pure
  // JS, is the only guard that actually holds.
  const fontFiles = (() => {
    if (!FONT_DIR) return [];
    try {
      return fs.readdirSync(FONT_DIR).filter((f) => /\.(ttf|otf|ttc)$/i.test(f));
    } catch {
      return [];
    }
  })();

  if (fontFiles.length === 0) {
    probeState = new Error(
      'cardFonts: no font files in ' + (FONT_DIR || '(no font dir found)') + '. ' +
      'Run `node scripts/fetch-fonts.js` and commit netlify/fonts/*.ttf, and check that ' +
      'netlify.toml [functions] included_files contains "netlify/fonts/**". ' +
      'Refusing to rasterize — librsvg segfaults with an empty font path.'
    );
    throw probeState;
  }

  const probeSvg = Buffer.from(
    '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120">' +
    '<rect width="120" height="120" fill="#000000"/>' +
    '<text x="60" y="92" font-size="96" font-family="' + FAMILIES.sans + ', sans-serif" ' +
    'font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle" fill="#ffffff">A</text></svg>'
  );

  try {
    const { data, info } = await sharp(probeSvg)
      .greyscale()
      .raw()
      .toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });

    let lit = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i += 1) {
      if (data[i] > 40) lit += 1;
    }
    // A 96px 'A' on a 120×120 canvas covers well over 300 pixels. Anything
    // below that means the glyph did not rasterize.
    if (lit < 300) {
      probeState = new Error(
        'cardFonts: glyph probe rendered ' + lit + ' lit pixels on a ' +
        info.width + 'x' + info.height + ' canvas — fonts are NOT resolving. ' +
        'FONTCONFIG_PATH=' + (process.env.FONTCONFIG_PATH || '(unset)') + '. ' +
        'Card text would be blank, so this render is being refused.'
      );
      throw probeState;
    }
    console.log('cardFonts: glyph probe OK (' + lit + ' px) — fontDir=' + FONT_DIR);
    probeState = true;
  } catch (err) {
    if (!(probeState instanceof Error)) probeState = err;
    throw probeState;
  }
}

/**
 * Returns the Sharp instance with fontconfig already wired up, after
 * verifying that text actually rasterizes.
 *
 * Every caller that rasterizes an SVG containing <text> MUST obtain Sharp
 * through here rather than requiring it directly.
 */
async function loadSharp() {
  await assertGlyphsRender();
  return sharp;
}

/**
 * For callers that only composite raster layers (no <text> at all) and so do
 * not need the font probe — e.g. compose-memory-board.js photo tiling.
 */
function loadSharpUnchecked() {
  if (!sharp) {
    throw new Error('sharp is not installed: ' + (sharpLoadError ? sharpLoadError.message : 'unknown'));
  }
  return sharp;
}

module.exports = {
  loadSharp,
  loadSharpUnchecked,
  assertGlyphsRender,
  familyFor,
  FAMILIES,
  FONT_DIR,
};

// netlify/functions/_lib/carePackageContentGuard.js
//
// Defense-in-depth check on GENERATED care package content — same principle
// as moderateMessage.js: prompt instructions ("no medical claims, no
// mental-health diagnosis language") reduce the chance of bad output, they
// don't guarantee it. This checks the actual generated text afterward,
// before it's ever stored as sendable or shown to anyone.
//
// Context this matters for: postpartum is a period with real, elevated risk
// of maternal depression/anxiety. Content that inadvertently reads as
// medical advice or pop-diagnoses ("sounds like you have PPD") to a new
// parent is a real harm, not just an off-brand tone slip.

const { generateText } = require('./anthropicHelper');

const SYSTEM_PROMPT = `You are a content safety checker for Zivogift's Care Package feature — short supportive WhatsApp messages sent to new parents over several weeks, written by a friend/family member's AI-assisted note, not a doctor.

Flag a message if it contains:
- Medical claims or advice (about the baby's or parent's physical health, feeding, sleep training methods, medication, or any "you should do X medically" framing)
- Mental-health diagnostic language (naming or implying a diagnosis like "postpartum depression," "PPD," "anxiety disorder," etc. — even sympathetically)
- Anything that could read as a substitute for professional medical or mental health care

Do NOT flag: warmth, encouragement, humor, practical non-medical support ("order food," "nap when the baby naps," "you're doing great"), or emotional validation that doesn't diagnose.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object, nothing else: {"verdict":"ok"|"flag","reason":"<one short sentence, empty string if ok>"}`;

async function checkCarePackageContent(text) {
  const trimmed = String(text || '').trim();
  if (!trimmed) return { ok: true, reason: null };

  try {
    const raw = await generateText({
      system: SYSTEM_PROMPT,
      prompt: `Message to check:\n"""${trimmed}"""`,
      maxTokens: 150,
    });

    const cleaned = raw.replace(/```json|```/g, '').trim();
    const parsed = JSON.parse(cleaned);

    return {
      ok: parsed.verdict !== 'flag',
      reason: parsed.reason || null,
    };
  } catch (err) {
    // Fails SAFE here, deliberately opposite of moderateMessage.js's
    // fail-open: this only runs on YOUR OWN generated content at low
    // volume (14 checks per order, not a per-user checkout gate), so
    // there's no availability pressure to let it through unchecked. If the
    // checker itself breaks, treat the content as unverified rather than
    // assume it's fine — same "flagged, needs a human look" outcome as a
    // real flag, via guardrail_flagged in the schema.
    console.error('checkCarePackageContent: check failed, failing CLOSED (flagged for review):', err.message);
    return { ok: false, reason: 'Guardrail check itself failed — needs manual review', checkFailed: true };
  }
}

module.exports = { checkCarePackageContent };

// netlify/functions/_lib/carePackageHelper.js
//
// Mirrors digitalSendsHelper.js's scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder — same
// calling convention, called from the same two places for the same reason
// (free/zero-value orders confirm inline in create-cashfree-order.js; paid
// orders confirm via cashfree-webhook.js after Cashfree calls back).
//
// A care package line item is identified by product_id starting with
// 'carepkg_' — added to DIGITAL_PREFIXES_CHECK in create-cashfree-order.js
// so it automatically gets sender-phone-verification AND message moderation
// for free, same gates every other digital gift goes through. personal_note
// is mapped onto item.message before that moderation check runs, since it's
// the one piece of free text a sender writes that feeds into AI generation
// for 14 messages — worth checking, not worth skipping.

async function scheduleCarePackagesForOrder(supabase, order, lineItems) {
  const carePackageItems = (lineItems || []).filter(
    (item) => item.product_id && String(item.product_id).startsWith('carepkg_')
  );
  if (carePackageItems.length === 0) return;

  const rows = carePackageItems.map((item) => {
    const opts = item.selected_options || {};
    return {
      order_id: order.id,
      recipient_phone: normalizeStoredPhone(item.recipient_phone),
      sender_name: order.contact_name,
      sender_phone: normalizeStoredPhone(order.contact_phone),
      package_type: opts.package_type || 'postpartum',
      relationship_tone: opts.relationship_tone || 'friend',
      personal_note: opts.personal_note || null,
      trigger_date: opts.trigger_date,
      start_date: opts.start_date || opts.trigger_date,
      cadence_days: opts.cadence_days || 3,
      total_messages: opts.total_messages || 14,
      status: 'pending_generation',
    };
  }).filter((r) => r.recipient_phone && r.trigger_date); // skip malformed rows rather than fail the whole order

  if (rows.length === 0) return;

  const { error } = await supabase.from('care_package_orders').insert(rows);
  if (error) {
    console.error('carePackageHelper: insert failed:', error.message);
    // Non-fatal by design, same as the rest of the order-confirmation path —
    // an order shouldn't fail post-payment because of this table specifically.
  }
}

function normalizeStoredPhone(raw) {
  const digits = String(raw || '').replace(/\D/g, '');
  if (digits.length === 10) return '91' + digits;
  if (digits.length === 12 && digits.startsWith('91')) return digits;
  return digits || null;
}

module.exports = { scheduleCarePackagesForOrder };

// Thin wrapper around the Cashfree Payment Gateway REST API (PG API v2023-08-01).
// Docs: https://docs.cashfree.com/docs/payment-gateway-quick-start
const crypto = require('crypto');

const CASHFREE_ENV = process.env.CASHFREE_ENV === 'production' ? 'production' : 'sandbox';
const BASE_URL = CASHFREE_ENV === 'production'
  ? 'https://api.cashfree.com/pg'
  : 'https://sandbox.cashfree.com/pg';

function headers() {
  const appId = process.env.CASHFREE_APP_ID;
  const secret = process.env.CASHFREE_SECRET_KEY;
  if (!appId || !secret) throw new Error('Missing CASHFREE_APP_ID / CASHFREE_SECRET_KEY env vars');
  return {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'x-api-version': '2023-08-01',
    'x-client-id': appId,
    'x-client-secret': secret,
  };
}

// Creates a Cashfree order and returns { cf_order_id, payment_session_id }
async function createCashfreeOrder({ orderId, orderNumber, amount, customer, returnUrl, notifyUrl }) {
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/orders`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: headers(),
    body: JSON.stringify({
      order_id: orderNumber,                 // human-friendly, must be unique at Cashfree
      order_amount: Number(amount.toFixed(2)),
      order_currency: 'INR',
      customer_details: {
        customer_id: customer.id || orderId,
        customer_name: customer.name,
        customer_email: customer.email,
        customer_phone: customer.phone,
      },
      order_meta: {
        return_url: `${returnUrl}${returnUrl.includes('?') ? '&' : '?'}order_number=${orderNumber}`,
        notify_url: notifyUrl,
      },
    }),
  });
  const data = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Cashfree order creation failed: ${data.message || res.statusText}`);
  }
  return { cfOrderId: data.cf_order_id, paymentSessionId: data.payment_session_id, raw: data };
}

// Verifies the `x-webhook-signature` header Cashfree sends with every webhook.
// Cashfree signs: timestamp + rawBody using HMAC-SHA256 with your webhook secret,
// base64 encoded. See: https://docs.cashfree.com/docs/webhooks
//
// Two checks, both required:
//  1. Signature match, via a timing-safe comparison — a plain `===` on two
//     strings leaks how many leading bytes matched through response-time
//     differences, which is the textbook setup for a timing attack against
//     the secret. crypto.timingSafeEqual removes that signal.
//  2. Timestamp freshness — the signature alone doesn't stop someone who
//     captured a legitimate webhook (e.g. from logs) from resending that
//     exact request later. Rejecting anything older than a few minutes
//     closes that replay window. Paired with the replay-dedup table in
//     cashfree-webhook.js for defense in depth within that window too.
const WEBHOOK_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 5 * 60; // 5 minutes

function verifyWebhookSignature({ rawBody, timestamp, signature }) {
  const secret = process.env.CASHFREE_WEBHOOK_SECRET;
  if (!secret) throw new Error('Missing CASHFREE_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var');

  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac('sha256', secret)
    .update(timestamp + rawBody)
    .digest('base64');

  const expectedBuf = Buffer.from(expected, 'utf8');
  const signatureBuf = Buffer.from(String(signature || ''), 'utf8');
  const signatureMatches =
    expectedBuf.length === signatureBuf.length &&
    crypto.timingSafeEqual(expectedBuf, signatureBuf);

  if (!signatureMatches) return false;

  // Cashfree sends timestamp as an epoch value (seconds). Reject anything
  // unparseable or outside the freshness window in either direction (a
  // timestamp from the future is just as suspicious as a stale replay).
  const tsNum = Number(timestamp);
  if (!Number.isFinite(tsNum)) return false;
  const tsMs = tsNum < 1e12 ? tsNum * 1000 : tsNum; // seconds vs already-ms
  const ageSeconds = Math.abs(Date.now() - tsMs) / 1000;
  if (ageSeconds > WEBHOOK_MAX_AGE_SECONDS) {
    console.error(`Cashfree webhook timestamp outside freshness window (${Math.round(ageSeconds)}s) — rejecting as possible replay.`);
    return false;
  }

  return true;
}

// Fetches order status directly from Cashfree as a double-check (defense in depth).
async function fetchCashfreeOrder(orderNumber) {
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/orders/${orderNumber}`, { headers: headers() });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Could not fetch Cashfree order ${orderNumber}`);
  return res.json();
}

module.exports = { createCashfreeOrder, verifyWebhookSignature, fetchCashfreeOrder };

// netlify/functions/_lib/clipFrames.js
//
// Renders the personalised "share clip" — recipient photo (optional),
// recipient name, message, sender sign-off — as an animated MP4.
//
// Used by clip-scheduler.js (the async job worker). NOT called synchronously
// from a request handler — this is deliberately async/queued because photo
// compositing pushes frame-render time close to Netlify's 10s sync limit
// (~9s measured locally for 90 frames with a photo; unsafe with production
// network/cold-start overhead on top). See handoff notes for the benchmark.
//
// Perf notes (don't undo these without re-benchmarking):
//   - The recipient photo is fetched + cover-cropped + circle-masked ONCE,
//     not per frame. Only the ~16 frames of the scale-pop-in transition need
//     a resized copy; everything after uses one cached full-size buffer.
//   - Frames are written as PNG with compressionLevel:1 (fast, not small —
//     they're deleted right after ffmpeg consumes them, so size doesn't matter).
//   - Do NOT embed the photo as a base64 data URI inside the SVG string; that
//     forces the SVG rasterizer to decode it on every frame and was ~5x slower
//     in testing. Composite it as a raster layer via sharp instead.

// Sharp MUST come from _lib/cardFonts.js, not from require('sharp') directly.
// cardFonts points FONTCONFIG_PATH at our bundled TTFs before the native
// binding initialises, and whoever requires sharp FIRST wins that race.
//
// Without it, librsvg finds no fonts on the Netlify Lambda runtime and every
// <text> element in the frame SVGs below rasterizes to nothing — the share
// clip came out as a correct-looking animated gradient with no name, no
// message and no sign-off, exactly like the gift cards did.
const { loadSharpUnchecked, assertGlyphsRender, FAMILIES } = require('./cardFonts');
const { resolveVibe } = require('../../../js/vibe-tokens');
const sharp = loadSharpUnchecked();
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const os = require('os');
const { execFileSync } = require('child_process');
const ffmpegPath = require('ffmpeg-static');

const W = 1080, H = 1080;
const FPS = 20;
const DURATION = 4.5;
const TOTAL_FRAMES = Math.round(FPS * DURATION);
const PHOTO_SIZE = 640;
const PHOTO_CX = W / 2, PHOTO_CY = 360;
const PHOTO_POP_START = 8, PHOTO_POP_END = 24;

// Vibe colours come from js/vibe-tokens.js — the same table the card
// generator, the delivery emails and gift.html read. This file used to keep
// its own hand-copied fork "following the existing convention"; that
// convention is exactly why the clip, the card and the email had drifted
// apart. One table now, resolved through resolveVibe().

function easeOutCubic(t) { return 1 - Math.pow(1 - t, 3); }
function clamp01(x) { return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, x)); }
function beat(t, startT, durT) { return easeOutCubic(clamp01((t - startT) / durT)); }

function escXml(s) {
  return String(s || '').replace(/&/g, '&amp;').replace(/</g, '&lt;').replace(/>/g, '&gt;').replace(/"/g, '&quot;');
}

function wrapText(text, maxCharsPerLine) {
  const words = (text || '').split(/\s+/);
  const lines = [];
  let current = '';
  for (const word of words) {
    if ((current + ' ' + word).trim().length > maxCharsPerLine) {
      if (current) lines.push(current);
      current = word;
    } else {
      current = (current + ' ' + word).trim();
    }
  }
  if (current) lines.push(current);
  return lines;
}

// One-time: fetch + cover-crop + circular-mask the recipient photo.
// Returns null if no photo URL given, or if the fetch fails (clip still
// generates fine without a photo — same fallback spirit as gift-scheduler.js
// falling back to a static card image on generation failure).
async function prepareCircularPhoto(photoUrl, accentColor) {
  if (!photoUrl) return null;
  try {
    const res = await fetch(photoUrl);
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`photo fetch failed (${res.status})`);
    const arrBuf = await res.arrayBuffer();

    const maskSvg = Buffer.from(
      `<svg width="${PHOTO_SIZE}" height="${PHOTO_SIZE}"><circle cx="${PHOTO_SIZE/2}" cy="${PHOTO_SIZE/2}" r="${PHOTO_SIZE/2}" fill="#fff"/></svg>`
    );
    const ringSvg = Buffer.from(
      `<svg width="${PHOTO_SIZE}" height="${PHOTO_SIZE}"><circle cx="${PHOTO_SIZE/2}" cy="${PHOTO_SIZE/2}" r="${PHOTO_SIZE/2 - 4}" fill="none" stroke="${accentColor}" stroke-width="6" opacity="0.9"/></svg>`
    );

    const circular = await sharp(Buffer.from(arrBuf))
      .resize(PHOTO_SIZE, PHOTO_SIZE, { fit: 'cover', position: 'attention' })
      .composite([{ input: maskSvg, blend: 'dest-in' }])
      .png()
      .toBuffer();

    return await sharp(circular).composite([{ input: ringSvg }]).png().toBuffer();
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn('clipFrames: photo prepare failed, continuing without photo:', err.message);
    return null;
  }
}

// Precompute the handful of resized buffers needed for the pop-in scale
// transition, so the main frame loop never resizes on the fly.
async function buildPhotoBuffers(baseCircularBuffer) {
  const buffers = new Map();
  if (!baseCircularBuffer) {
    for (let i = 0; i < TOTAL_FRAMES; i++) buffers.set(i, null);
    return buffers;
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < TOTAL_FRAMES; i++) {
    if (i < PHOTO_POP_START) { buffers.set(i, null); continue; }
    if (i >= PHOTO_POP_END) { buffers.set(i, { buf: baseCircularBuffer, size: PHOTO_SIZE }); continue; }
    const progress = easeOutCubic((i - PHOTO_POP_START) / (PHOTO_POP_END - PHOTO_POP_START));
    const size = Math.round(PHOTO_SIZE * (0.85 + 0.15 * progress));
    const resized = await sharp(baseCircularBuffer).resize(size, size).toBuffer();
    buffers.set(i, { buf: resized, size });
  }
  return buffers;
}

function buildFrameSvg(frameIdx, { recipientName, senderName, message, style, hasPhoto }) {
  const t = frameIdx / FPS;
  const bgOpacity = beat(t, 0, 0.4);

  // Name/message/sender beats shift earlier when there's no photo to wait for.
  const nameStart = hasPhoto ? 1.1 : 0.5;
  const msgStart = hasPhoto ? 1.8 : 1.2;
  const senderStart = hasPhoto ? 2.9 : 2.3;
  const logoStart = hasPhoto ? 3.3 : 2.7;

  const nameProgress = beat(t, nameStart, 0.7);
  const nameY = (hasPhoto ? 745 : 485) + (1 - nameProgress) * 20;

  const msgProgress = beat(t, msgStart, 0.9);
  const msgStartY = (hasPhoto ? 800 : 540) + (1 - msgProgress) * 16;

  const senderProgress = beat(t, senderStart, 0.8);
  const senderY = (hasPhoto ? 970 : 710) + (1 - senderProgress) * 16;

  const logoProgress = beat(t, logoStart, 0.7);
  const logoOpacity = logoProgress * 0.7;

  const msgLines = wrapText(message, 34);
  const msgSvg = msgLines.map((line, i) => {
    const dy = i === 0 ? 0 : 40;
    return `<tspan x="${W/2}" dy="${dy}">${escXml(line)}</tspan>`;
  }).join('');

  return `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg width="${W}" height="${H}" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="bg" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="${style.bg1}"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="${style.bg2}"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <radialGradient id="glow" cx="50%" cy="30%" r="55%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="${style.accent}" stop-opacity="0.20"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="${style.accent}" stop-opacity="0"/>
    </radialGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect width="${W}" height="${H}" fill="url(#bg)" opacity="${bgOpacity}"/>
  <rect width="${W}" height="${H}" fill="url(#glow)" opacity="${bgOpacity}"/>
  <rect x="40" y="40" width="${W-80}" height="${H-80}" rx="28" fill="none"
        stroke="${style.accent}" stroke-opacity="0.35" stroke-width="2" opacity="${bgOpacity}"/>
  <text x="${W/2}" y="${nameY}" text-anchor="middle" font-family="${FAMILIES.sans}, sans-serif" font-weight="700"
        font-size="64" fill="${style.accent}" opacity="${nameProgress}">${escXml(recipientName)}</text>
  <text x="${W/2}" y="${msgStartY}" text-anchor="middle" font-family="${FAMILIES.sans}, sans-serif"
        font-size="34" fill="${style.text}" opacity="${msgProgress}">${msgSvg}</text>
  <text x="${W/2}" y="${senderY}" text-anchor="middle" font-family="${FAMILIES.sans}, sans-serif" font-style="italic"
        font-size="30" fill="${style.text}" opacity="${senderProgress}">— ${escXml(senderName)}</text>
  <text x="${W/2}" y="1030" text-anchor="middle" font-family="${FAMILIES.sans}, sans-serif" letter-spacing="4"
        font-size="20" fill="${style.text}" opacity="${logoOpacity}">ZIVOGIFT</text>
</svg>`;
}

// Renders all frames to a fresh temp directory. Returns { workDir, framesDir }.
async function renderFrames({ vibeKey, recipientName, senderName, message, recipientPhotoUrl }) {
  // Refuse to render before confirming glyphs actually rasterize. A clip with
  // no text is worse than a failed job: the job would be marked done and the
  // recipient would download a blank video.
  await assertGlyphsRender();

  const style = resolveVibe(vibeKey);
  const recipient = (recipientName || 'Friend').trim();
  const sender = (senderName || 'Someone special').trim();
  const msgText = (message || '').trim() || 'Wishing you an amazing day!';

  const baseCircular = await prepareCircularPhoto(recipientPhotoUrl, style.accent);
  const photoBuffers = await buildPhotoBuffers(baseCircular);
  const hasPhoto = !!baseCircular;

  const workDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'clip-'));
  const framesDir = path.join(workDir, 'frames');
  fs.mkdirSync(framesDir);

  for (let i = 0; i < TOTAL_FRAMES; i++) {
    const svg = buildFrameSvg(i, { recipientName: recipient, senderName: sender, message: msgText, style, hasPhoto });
    const baseImg = sharp(Buffer.from(svg));
    const photo = photoBuffers.get(i);
    let pipeline = baseImg;
    if (photo) {
      const half = photo.size / 2;
      pipeline = baseImg.composite([{
        input: photo.buf,
        left: Math.round(PHOTO_CX - half),
        top: Math.round(PHOTO_CY - half),
      }]);
    }
    const png = await pipeline.png({ compressionLevel: 1 }).toBuffer();
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(framesDir, `f_${String(i).padStart(3, '0')}.png`), png);
  }

  return { workDir, framesDir };
}

// Encodes the frames directory into an H.264 MP4, returns the buffer, and
// cleans up the temp directory (frames + video) once read into memory.
function encodeToMp4({ workDir, framesDir }) {
  const outPath = path.join(workDir, 'out.mp4');
  execFileSync(ffmpegPath, [
    '-y',
    '-framerate', String(FPS),
    '-i', path.join(framesDir, 'f_%03d.png'),
    '-c:v', 'libx264',
    '-pix_fmt', 'yuv420p',
    '-movflags', '+faststart',
    outPath,
  ], { stdio: 'pipe' });

  const buffer = fs.readFileSync(outPath);
  fs.rmSync(workDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  return buffer;
}

module.exports = { renderFrames, encodeToMp4, TOTAL_FRAMES, FPS, DURATION };

// Shared helper: schedules digital_sends rows for digital/squad products in
// an order. Supports WhatsApp, Email, or both delivery modes.
// Updated for Group 2: handles gift_type, media_url, media_type, persona_key,
// squad_drop contributor invites, and character_drop reply tokens.

const { normalizePhone } = require('./phoneUtil');

const DIGITAL_PREFIXES = ['digital_', 'squad_'];

function nextMidnightIST() {
  const now = new Date();
  const istOffsetMs = 330 * 60 * 1000; // UTC+5:30
  const nowIST = new Date(now.getTime() + istOffsetMs);
  nowIST.setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
  if (nowIST.getTime() <= now.getTime() + istOffsetMs) {
    nowIST.setUTCDate(nowIST.getUTCDate() + 1);
  }
  return new Date(nowIST.getTime() - istOffsetMs).toISOString();
}

async function scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder(supabase, order, items) {
  const siteUrl = process.env.SITE_URL || 'https://zivogift.com';
  const digitalItems = (items || []).filter(
    (i) => i.product_id && DIGITAL_PREFIXES.some((p) => i.product_id.startsWith(p))
  );
  if (!digitalItems.length) return;

  const sendRows = [];
  // Track which send rows need post-insert processing (reply token, squad invites)
  const postInsertTasks = [];

  for (const item of digitalItems) {
    // Normalize to E.164-without-'+' ('919876543210'). Different entry points
    // format this differently -- js/studio.js and js/studio-group2.js prepend
    // '91' client-side, but js/care-package.js sends a bare 10-digit number.
    // Meta ACCEPTS a 10-digit `to` and then never delivers, so an
    // un-normalized number looked like a successful send and failed silently.
    // Normalizing here covers every caller in one place.
    const recipientPhone = normalizePhone(item.recipient_phone) || item.recipient_phone || null;
    const recipientEmail = item.recipient_email;
    const deliveryMode = item.delivery_mode || (recipientPhone ? 'whatsapp' : 'email');

    if (item.recipient_phone && !normalizePhone(item.recipient_phone)) {
      console.warn(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: recipient_phone "${item.recipient_phone}" on item ${item.id} is not a recognizable Indian mobile -- WhatsApp delivery will likely fail`);
    }
    const scheduledAt = item.scheduled_send_at || nextMidnightIST();
    const opts = item.selected_options || {};

    // Resolve gift_type — stored on item directly or in selected_options
    const giftType = item.gift_type || opts.gift_type || 'standard';
    const mediaUrl = item.media_url || opts.media_url || null;
    const mediaType = item.media_type || opts.media_type || null;
    const personaKey = item.persona_key || opts.persona_key || null;
    const contributorPhones = item.contributor_phones || opts.contributor_phones || [];
    const contributorNames = item.contributor_names || opts.contributor_names || [];

    const baseRow = {
      order_id: order.id,
      order_item_id: item.id,
      recipient_name: item.recipient_name || 'Friend',
      sender_name: order.contact_name,
      personal_message: item.personalization_message || null,
      occasion: opts.Occasion || 'Birthday',
      // Normalized for the same reason as recipient_phone: this number
      // receives the "your gift was delivered" notify and, for condition
      // gifts, must match the inbound webhook's `from` when the sender texts
      // the keyword back.
      sender_phone: normalizePhone(order.contact_phone) || order.contact_phone || null,
      vibe_key: opts.vibe_key || null,
      card_image_url: null,                // Generated at send time by gift-scheduler
      scheduled_at: scheduledAt,
      status: 'pending',
      // Group 2 additions
      gift_type: giftType,
      media_url: mediaUrl,
      media_type: mediaType,
      persona_key: personaKey,
      // Group 3 additions
      is_time_capsule: !!item.is_time_capsule,
      condition_type:  item.condition_type  || 'none',
      condition_met:   item.condition_type === 'sender_confirm' ? false : true,
      condition_keyword: item.condition_type === 'sender_confirm'
        ? buildConditionKeyword(item.recipient_name)
        : null,
      condition_label: item.condition_label || null,
      // Group 4 additions
      photo_urls: opts.photo_urls || item.photo_urls || null,
      // Share-clip addition — single recipient photo, shown as-is (no styling) in gift.html's animated clip
      recipient_photo_url: opts.recipient_photo_url || item.recipient_photo_url || null,
    };

    // Part 2 (Voice/Video/Group Tribute): optional sender-chosen gift title.
    // Added CONDITIONALLY so existing gift inserts are byte-identical and
    // unaffected if the additive `gift_title` column has not been applied yet.
    // Requires supabase/schema-voice-video-tribute.sql to have been run.
    var giftTitle = opts.gift_title || item.gift_title || null;
    if (giftTitle) baseRow.gift_title = giftTitle;

    // Schedule WhatsApp send
    if ((deliveryMode === 'whatsapp' || deliveryMode === 'both') && recipientPhone) {
      const rowIdx = sendRows.length;
      // ── recipient_email IS CARRIED ON THE WHATSAPP ROW TOO ───────────────
      // 50_whatsapp_delivery.sql added an email rescue path: when Meta
      // reports a terminal delivery failure, whatsapp-webhook.js requeues the
      // row as a pending EMAIL send so the gift still lands. But that rescue
      // is gated on `if (row.recipient_email)`, and this row was previously
      // inserted WITHOUT one -- so for a whatsapp-only gift, the fallback
      // could never fire. It only ever worked for delivery_mode 'both', which
      // is precisely the case that least needed rescuing.
      //
      // Attaching the address here makes the rescue actually reachable.
      //
      // CRITICAL: only for whatsapp-ONLY sends. Under delivery_mode 'both' a
      // separate email row is already created below, so letting the WhatsApp
      // row fall back to email as well would deliver the same gift twice to
      // the same inbox. The fallback is a rescue for someone who would
      // otherwise get nothing -- not a second copy for someone already served.
      const fallbackEmail = deliveryMode === 'both' ? null : (recipientEmail || null);
      sendRows.push({
        ...baseRow,
        recipient_phone: recipientPhone,
        recipient_email: fallbackEmail,
        channel: 'whatsapp',
      });

      // Queue post-insert tasks for special gift types
      if (giftType === 'character_drop' && personaKey && order.contact_phone) {
        postInsertTasks.push({ rowIdx, type: 'create_reply_token', senderPhone: order.contact_phone });
      }
      if (giftType === 'squad_drop' && Array.isArray(contributorPhones) && contributorPhones.length > 0) {
        const contributors = contributorPhones.map((phone, i) => ({
          phone: String(phone).replace(/\D/g, ''),
          name: contributorNames[i] || 'Friend',
        })).filter((c) => c.phone.length >= 10);
        if (contributors.length > 0) {
          postInsertTasks.push({
            rowIdx,
            type: 'send_squad_invites',
            contributors,
            recipientName: item.recipient_name || 'Friend',
            senderName: order.contact_name,
          });
        }
      }
    } else if (deliveryMode !== 'email' && !recipientPhone) {
      console.warn(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: no recipient_phone for item ${item.id} — skipping WhatsApp`);
    }

    // Schedule Email send
    if ((deliveryMode === 'email' || deliveryMode === 'both') && recipientEmail) {
      sendRows.push({ ...baseRow, recipient_email: recipientEmail, channel: 'email' });
    } else if (deliveryMode !== 'whatsapp' && !recipientEmail) {
      console.warn(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: no recipient_email for item ${item.id} — skipping email`);
    }
  }

  if (!sendRows.length) return;

  // ── Resilient insert ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // These rows used to go in as ONE batch. Postgres rejects a batch atomically,
  // so a single malformed row -- an email item whose address never made it
  // through checkout, say -- silently dropped the WhatsApp rows from the SAME
  // order too. The buyer paid and nothing was ever scheduled, and the only
  // trace was a console.error nobody reads. (That exact failure is documented
  // at the top of supabase/schema-fix-digital-sends-email.sql.)
  //
  // Now: try the fast batch first, and if it fails, insert row by row so the
  // good rows survive and the bad ones are named individually in the logs.
  let insertedRows = [];
  const { data: batchRows, error } = await supabase
    .from('digital_sends')
    .insert(sendRows)
    .select('id');

  if (!error) {
    insertedRows = batchRows || [];
  } else {
    console.error(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: batch insert failed (${error.message}) -- falling back to per-row inserts so one bad row cannot drop the rest`);

    const perRow = await Promise.all(sendRows.map(async (row, idx) => {
      const { data, error: rowErr } = await supabase
        .from('digital_sends')
        .insert(row)
        .select('id')
        .single();
      if (rowErr) {
        console.error(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: row ${idx} (channel=${row.channel}, item=${row.order_item_id}) rejected: ${rowErr.message}`);
        return null;
      }
      return data;
    }));

    // Keep index alignment with sendRows -- postInsertTasks reference rowIdx.
    insertedRows = perRow;

    const ok = perRow.filter(Boolean).length;
    if (ok === 0) {
      console.error(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: NO sends could be scheduled for order ${order.order_number || order.id}`);
      return;
    }
    console.warn(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: recovered ${ok}/${sendRows.length} sends for order ${order.order_number || order.id}`);
  }

  console.log(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: queued ${sendRows.length} sends for order ${order.order_number || order.id}`);

  // ── Post-insert: Group 2 special gift type tasks + Group 3 condition notify ──
  // Build a map from rowIdx → inserted send id now that we have real DB ids
  const insertedIdByIdx = {};
  if (insertedRows) {
    // `row` can be null on the per-row fallback path above (that row was
    // rejected), so guard before dereferencing -- otherwise a single rejected
    // row throws here and takes the squad invites and reply tokens with it.
    insertedRows.forEach((row, i) => { if (row && row.id) insertedIdByIdx[i] = row.id; });
  }

  // Notify condition-based gift senders of the keyword they need to text (#23)
  const conditionRows = sendRows
    .map((row, idx) => ({ row, idx }))
    .filter(({ row }) => row.condition_type === 'sender_confirm' && row.sender_phone && row.condition_keyword);

  if (conditionRows.length > 0) {
    const { sendWhatsAppTemplate } = require('./whatsapp');
    await Promise.allSettled(conditionRows.map(async ({ row, idx }) => {
      const sendId = insertedIdByIdx[idx];
      if (!sendId) return;
      try {
        await sendWhatsAppTemplate({
          recipientPhone: row.sender_phone,
          templateName: 'zg_condition_gift_instructions',
          bodyVariables: [
            row.sender_name || 'Hey',
            row.recipient_name,
            row.condition_keyword,
            row.condition_label || 'when the moment is right',
          ],
        });
        console.log(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: condition keyword sent to sender for send ${sendId}`);
      } catch (e) {
        console.warn(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: condition notify failed for send ${sendId}:`, e.message);
      }
    }));
  }

  // Run post-insert tasks now that we have the real send IDs
  if (postInsertTasks.length > 0) {
    await Promise.allSettled(
      postInsertTasks.map(async (task) => {
        const sendId = insertedIdByIdx[task.rowIdx];
        if (!sendId) return;

        if (task.type === 'create_reply_token') {
          try {
            const res = await fetch(`${process.env.SITE_URL || 'https://zivogift.com'}/.netlify/functions/create-reply-token`, {
              method: 'POST',
              headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
              body: JSON.stringify({ gift_id: sendId, real_sender_phone: task.senderPhone }),
            });
            if (res.ok) {
              const data = await res.json();
              // Store the reply token on the digital_sends row for gift.html to read
              await supabase
                .from('digital_sends')
                .update({ reply_token: data.token })
                .eq('id', sendId);
              console.log(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: reply_token created for send ${sendId}`);
            }
          } catch (e) {
            console.warn('scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: create-reply-token failed:', e.message);
          }
        }

        if (task.type === 'send_squad_invites') {
          try {
            await fetch(`${process.env.SITE_URL || 'https://zivogift.com'}/.netlify/functions/send-reaction-invites`, {
              method: 'POST',
              headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
              body: JSON.stringify({
                gift_id: sendId,
                recipient_name: task.recipientName,
                sender_name: task.senderName,
                contributors: task.contributors,
              }),
            });
            console.log(`scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: squad invites dispatched for send ${sendId}`);
          } catch (e) {
            console.warn('scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder: send-reaction-invites failed:', e.message);
          }
        }
      })
    );
  }
}

module.exports = { scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder, nextMidnightIST };

/**
 * Derives a unique, easy-to-type WhatsApp keyword from the recipient name.
 * e.g. "Priya Sharma" → "SEND PRIYA"
 * The sender texts exactly this keyword to unlock the gift (#23).
 */
function buildConditionKeyword(recipientName) {
  const first = (recipientName || 'GIFT').trim().split(/\s+/)[0].toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z]/g, '');
  return `SEND ${first || 'GIFT'}`;
}

// netlify/functions/_lib/dobUtils.js
//
// Small shared helpers for turning a recipient's DOB (stored as DD/MM/YYYY,
// see js/catalog.js finalizeAddToCart) into the two things both the Currency
// Note Story Card (#14) and the Numerology Upgrade (#22) need:
//   1. A serial-style digit string — mirrors how the physical note is
//      actually sourced (its real serial number is chosen to encode the
//      birth date), so the AI narrative talks about digits that are
//      genuinely meaningful rather than invented.
//   2. A numerology Life Path number — computed deterministically in code
//      (not hallucinated by the model) so the reading Claude writes is
//      anchored to a real number.

function parseDob(dobStr) {
  const s = (dobStr || '').trim();

  // Supabase/PostgREST serializes a Postgres `date` column as ISO
  // YYYY-MM-DD — this is what recipient_dob actually looks like when read
  // back from order_items in cashfree-webhook.js. This is the primary,
  // expected format.
  let m = /^(\d{4})-(\d{1,2})-(\d{1,2})$/.exec(s);
  if (m) {
    const year = parseInt(m[1], 10), month = parseInt(m[2], 10), day = parseInt(m[3], 10);
    if (day >= 1 && day <= 31 && month >= 1 && month <= 12) return { day, month, year };
  }

  // Fallback: DD/MM/YYYY — in case this is ever called with the raw string
  // js/catalog.js builds client-side (pending.recipientDob) before it round-trips
  // through the `date` column.
  m = /^(\d{1,2})\/(\d{1,2})\/(\d{4})$/.exec(s);
  if (m) {
    const day = parseInt(m[1], 10), month = parseInt(m[2], 10), year = parseInt(m[3], 10);
    if (day >= 1 && day <= 31 && month >= 1 && month <= 12) return { day, month, year };
  }

  return null;
}

// e.g. 15/08/2003 → "150803" — the DDMMYY pattern the note's real serial mirrors.
function serialDigitsFromDob(dobStr) {
  const parsed = parseDob(dobStr);
  if (!parsed) return null;
  const dd = String(parsed.day).padStart(2, '0');
  const mm = String(parsed.month).padStart(2, '0');
  const yy = String(parsed.year).slice(-2);
  return dd + mm + yy;
}

// Standard numerology Life Path calculation: sum every digit of the full
// DDMMYYYY date, keep reducing to a single digit — except master numbers
// 11, 22, 33, which are traditionally kept unreduced.
function reduceDigits(n) {
  while (n > 9 && n !== 11 && n !== 22 && n !== 33) {
    n = String(n).split('').reduce((s, d) => s + parseInt(d, 10), 0);
  }
  return n;
}

function lifePathNumber(dobStr) {
  const parsed = parseDob(dobStr);
  if (!parsed) return null;
  const full = `${String(parsed.day).padStart(2, '0')}${String(parsed.month).padStart(2, '0')}${parsed.year}`;
  const sum = full.split('').reduce((s, d) => s + parseInt(d, 10), 0);
  return reduceDigits(sum);
}

module.exports = { parseDob, serialDigitsFromDob, lifePathNumber };

// netlify/functions/_lib/mediaSizeGuard.js
//
// Server-side enforcement for uploaded media. The client-side checks in
// studio.js (photo) and studio-group2.js (video/audio) are convenience only
// — someone can call get-media-upload-url.js's presigned PUT URL directly
// and upload anything, any size, any content. This is the real enforcement
// point, called from create-cashfree-order.js at the same checkpoint as
// phone verification and message moderation — can't be bypassed by calling
// the order API directly, same as those two. It now checks, in order:
//   1. The URL actually points at our own R2 bucket (not an attacker-
//      supplied external URL smuggled in as "media").
//   2. Real size, as reported by R2 itself (HeadObjectCommand), not
//      anything the client claims.
//   3. Magic-byte content validation — the bytes actually match the claimed
//      file type (see _lib/mediaValidation.js for why this matters and what
//      it does and doesn't catch).
//   4. For images: full decode + re-encode via sharp, which also strips
//      EXIF/embedded-payload metadata.
//   5. Optional virus scan (VirusTotal, best-effort, see mediaValidation.js).
//
// Deletes rejected objects rather than just failing the order — an
// oversized or invalid upload someone abandoned at checkout shouldn't sit
// in R2 costing storage forever. A full lifecycle policy for
// abandoned/expired-but-valid uploads is still a separate, unbuilt piece.

const { getObjectSize, deleteObject, extractKeyFromPublicUrl } = require('./r2Client');
const { validateMagicBytes, reencodeImageInPlace, scanBufferForMalware, fetchFullObject, IMAGE_EXTENSIONS, extOf } = require('./mediaValidation');

const MAX_BYTES = {
  image: 8 * 1024 * 1024,   // 8MB — matches the existing client-side photo check
  video: 25 * 1024 * 1024,  // 25MB — placeholder, not a measured recommendation;
                              // tune against your actual Personal Message video
                              // lengths once you have real usage data
  audio: 10 * 1024 * 1024,  // 10MB — placeholder, same caveat as video
};

// Only run the (comparatively expensive) full-buffer virus scan on files up
// to this size, so a 25MB video upload can't stall order creation.
const MAX_SCAN_BYTES = 12 * 1024 * 1024;

function guessCategory(url) {
  const ext = extOf(url);
  if (['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'webp'].includes(ext)) return 'image';
  if (['mp4', 'webm'].includes(ext)) return 'video';
  if (['mp3', 'ogg'].includes(ext)) return 'audio';
  return 'image'; // safest default — smallest limit
}

// Rejects any URL that isn't actually pointing at our own R2 bucket, so a
// tampered checkout request can't pass off an external URL (arbitrary
// content, arbitrary domain, possible SSRF/privacy-leak vector via <video>/
// <audio> src on the recipient's gift page) as if it were an uploaded file.
function isOwnBucketUrl(url) {
  try {
    const publicUrl = (process.env.R2_PUBLIC_URL || '').replace(/\/$/, '');
    if (publicUrl && url.startsWith(publicUrl + '/')) return true;
    // Fallback form: https://<bucket>.<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/...
    const bucketName = process.env.R2_BUCKET_NAME;
    const accountId = process.env.R2_ACCOUNT_ID;
    if (bucketName && accountId) {
      const fallbackHost = `${bucketName}.${accountId}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`;
      const u = new URL(url);
      if (u.hostname === fallbackHost) return true;
    }
    return false;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

// Checks one URL. Returns { ok, sizeBytes, error }. Deletes the object if
// it's over limit or fails content validation, so a rejected order doesn't
// leave the file behind.
async function checkAndEnforce(url) {
  if (!url) return { ok: true };

  if (!isOwnBucketUrl(url)) {
    return { ok: false, error: 'Media must be uploaded through Zivogift, not linked externally' };
  }

  const key = extractKeyFromPublicUrl(url);
  if (!key) {
    return { ok: false, error: 'Could not verify uploaded file' };
  }

  let sizeBytes;
  try {
    sizeBytes = await getObjectSize(key);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('mediaSizeGuard: HEAD check failed for', key, err.message);
    return { ok: false, error: 'Could not verify uploaded file' };
  }

  const category = guessCategory(url);
  const limit = MAX_BYTES[category];
  if (sizeBytes > limit) {
    try { await deleteObject(key); } catch (err) {
      console.error('mediaSizeGuard: failed to delete oversized object', key, err.message);
    }
    return { ok: false, error: `Uploaded file is too large (${Math.round(sizeBytes / 1024 / 1024)}MB, limit ${Math.round(limit / 1024 / 1024)}MB)`, sizeBytes };
  }

  // Content validation — real bytes vs claimed type.
  const magicCheck = await validateMagicBytes(key);
  if (!magicCheck.ok) {
    try { await deleteObject(key); } catch (err) {
      console.error('mediaSizeGuard: failed to delete invalid object', key, err.message);
    }
    return { ok: false, error: magicCheck.error, sizeBytes };
  }

  // Images: full decode+re-encode, strips metadata, rejects anything that
  // merely fakes a valid header.
  if (IMAGE_EXTENSIONS.has(extOf(url))) {
    const reencode = await reencodeImageInPlace(key);
    if (!reencode.ok) {
      try { await deleteObject(key); } catch (err) {
        console.error('mediaSizeGuard: failed to delete invalid image', key, err.message);
      }
      return { ok: false, error: reencode.error, sizeBytes };
    }
  }

  // Best-effort virus scan (skipped entirely if VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY isn't
  // set — see mediaValidation.js). Never blocks the order on a scan error;
  // only blocks on a confirmed-malicious result.
  if (sizeBytes <= MAX_SCAN_BYTES) {
    try {
      const buffer = await fetchFullObject(key);
      const scan = await scanBufferForMalware(buffer);
      if (!scan.skipped && scan.clean === false) {
        try { await deleteObject(key); } catch (err) {
          console.error('mediaSizeGuard: failed to delete flagged object', key, err.message);
        }
        return { ok: false, error: 'Uploaded file was flagged by malware scanning', sizeBytes };
      }
      if (scan.skipped) {
        console.warn('mediaSizeGuard: virus scan skipped for', key, '—', scan.reason);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn('mediaSizeGuard: virus scan errored (non-fatal) for', key, err.message);
    }
  }

  return { ok: true, sizeBytes };
}

// Checks every media URL a cart item might carry — recipient photo, a
// Personal Message/Character Drop video/audio, or a Squad Memory Board's
// multi-photo array. Returns the first failure found, or { ok: true }.
async function checkCartItemMedia(item) {
  const opts = item.selectedOptions || {};
  const urlsToCheck = [];

  if (opts.recipient_photo_url) urlsToCheck.push(opts.recipient_photo_url);
  if (item.mediaUrl) urlsToCheck.push(item.mediaUrl);
  if (Array.isArray(opts.photo_urls)) urlsToCheck.push(...opts.photo_urls);

  for (const url of urlsToCheck) {
    const result = await checkAndEnforce(url);
    if (!result.ok) return result;
  }
  return { ok: true };
}

module.exports = { checkCartItemMedia };

FILE: netlify\functions\_lib\mediaValidation.js
=====================================================

// netlify/functions/_lib/mediaValidation.js
//
// Real content validation for uploaded media — this is what closes the gap
// that mediaSizeGuard.js alone leaves open: mediaSizeGuard confirms the
// object isn't too big, but never confirms the bytes are actually what the
// extension/Content-Type claim. Since uploads go straight from the browser
// to R2 via a presigned PUT (get-media-upload-url.js), anyone who calls that
// presigned URL directly can PUT arbitrary bytes with any Content-Type they
// like — an ".mp4" key can contain anything.
//
// Three layers, in order, each cheap enough to run at order-creation time:
//   1. Magic-byte signature check — does the file actually start with the
//      bytes a real file of its claimed type would have? Catches disguised
//      executables/scripts/HTML far more reliably than trusting extension
//      or the client-supplied Content-Type header.
//   2. Image re-encode (sharp, already a project dependency) — fully decodes
//      and re-writes any image upload. A file that doesn't decode as a real
//      image is rejected outright; one that does gets its metadata (EXIF,
//      embedded scripts some image parsers have historically choked on,
//      polyglot payloads) stripped by the re-encode, and the sanitized
//      version replaces the original in R2.
//   3. Virus scan (optional, VirusTotal) — best effort, feature-flagged on
//      VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY. If the key isn't set, this step is skipped and
//      logged as skipped, not silently treated as "passed" — see
//      scanBufferForMalware's return shape.

const { GetObjectCommand, PutObjectCommand } = require('@aws-sdk/client-s3');
const crypto = require('crypto');

// ---- magic-byte signatures --------------------------------------------------
// Each entry: byte offset → array of possible starting byte sequences (hex).
const SIGNATURES = {
  jpg:  [{ offset: 0, bytes: [0xff, 0xd8, 0xff] }],
  jpeg: [{ offset: 0, bytes: [0xff, 0xd8, 0xff] }],
  png:  [{ offset: 0, bytes: [0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a] }],
  webp: [{ offset: 0, bytes: [0x52, 0x49, 0x46, 0x46] }, { offset: 8, bytes: [0x57, 0x45, 0x42, 0x50] }], // 'RIFF'....'WEBP'
  mp4:  [{ offset: 4, bytes: [0x66, 0x74, 0x79, 0x70] }], // 'ftyp' at byte 4 (ISO base media)
  webm: [{ offset: 0, bytes: [0x1a, 0x45, 0xdf, 0xa3] }], // EBML header
  mp3:  [{ offset: 0, bytes: [0x49, 0x44, 0x33] }, { offset: 0, bytes: [0xff, 0xfb] }, { offset: 0, bytes: [0xff, 0xf3] }, { offset: 0, bytes: [0xff, 0xf2] }],
  ogg:  [{ offset: 0, bytes: [0x4f, 0x67, 0x67, 0x53] }], // 'OggS'
};

const IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = new Set(['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'webp']);

function extOf(url) {
  return (url.split('.').pop() || '').toLowerCase().split('?')[0];
}

function matchesAnySignature(buf, sigs) {
  return sigs.some(({ offset, bytes }) => {
    if (buf.length < offset + bytes.length) return false;
    for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) {
      if (buf[offset + i] !== bytes[i]) return false;
    }
    return true;
  });
}

function getR2Client() {
  const { S3Client } = require('@aws-sdk/client-s3');
  const accountId = process.env.R2_ACCOUNT_ID;
  const accessKey = process.env.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID;
  const secretKey = process.env.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY;
  return new S3Client({
    region: 'auto',
    endpoint: `https://${accountId}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`,
    credentials: { accessKeyId: accessKey, secretAccessKey: secretKey },
  });
}

async function streamToBuffer(stream) {
  const chunks = [];
  for await (const chunk of stream) chunks.push(Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk : Buffer.from(chunk));
  return Buffer.concat(chunks);
}

// Fetches just the first `length` bytes of an R2 object via a ranged GET —
// cheap even for large video files, since we never pull the whole object
// just to check its header.
async function fetchHeadBytes(key, length = 64) {
  const client = getR2Client();
  const bucketName = process.env.R2_BUCKET_NAME;
  const res = await client.send(new GetObjectCommand({
    Bucket: bucketName,
    Key: key,
    Range: `bytes=0-${length - 1}`,
  }));
  return streamToBuffer(res.Body);
}

async function fetchFullObject(key) {
  const client = getR2Client();
  const bucketName = process.env.R2_BUCKET_NAME;
  const res = await client.send(new GetObjectCommand({ Bucket: bucketName, Key: key }));
  return streamToBuffer(res.Body);
}

async function putObject(key, buffer, contentType) {
  const client = getR2Client();
  const bucketName = process.env.R2_BUCKET_NAME;
  await client.send(new PutObjectCommand({
    Bucket: bucketName,
    Key: key,
    Body: buffer,
    ContentType: contentType,
    CacheControl: 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable',
  }));
}

// Checks the object's real bytes against what its extension claims.
// Returns { ok, error? }.
async function validateMagicBytes(key) {
  const ext = extOf(key);
  const sigs = SIGNATURES[ext];
  if (!sigs) {
    // Extension isn't one we have a signature for (shouldn't happen — the
    // presign step only allows a known extension list) — fail closed.
    return { ok: false, error: 'Unrecognized file type' };
  }

  let head;
  try {
    head = await fetchHeadBytes(key, 32);
  } catch (err) {
    return { ok: false, error: `Could not read uploaded file: ${err.message}` };
  }

  if (!matchesAnySignature(head, sigs)) {
    return { ok: false, error: 'File content does not match its extension — upload rejected' };
  }
  return { ok: true };
}

// Fully decodes and re-encodes an image via sharp, replacing the R2 object
// with the sanitized version. Rejects anything that doesn't decode as a
// genuine image (a magic-byte match alone doesn't guarantee the rest of the
// file is well-formed / free of appended or embedded payloads).
async function reencodeImageInPlace(key) {
  const sharp = require('sharp');
  let original;
  try {
    original = await fetchFullObject(key);
  } catch (err) {
    return { ok: false, error: `Could not read uploaded image: ${err.message}` };
  }

  let cleaned;
  try {
    // Re-encoding to a fresh buffer drops EXIF/XMP/ICC metadata and any
    // trailing/embedded bytes that aren't part of the actual pixel data —
    // sharp only ever reads what libvips needs to decode the image.
    cleaned = await sharp(original, { limitInputPixels: 40_000_000 })
      .rotate() // apply EXIF orientation, then metadata is stripped
      .toFormat('jpeg', { quality: 88 })
      .toBuffer();
  } catch (err) {
    return { ok: false, error: 'Uploaded file is not a valid image' };
  }

  // Replace the object with the sanitized version (same key — extension
  // in the key may now not match jpeg internally, but Content-Type is what
  // browsers/clients actually trust for rendering, and we set it correctly).
  try {
    await putObject(key, cleaned, 'image/jpeg');
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('mediaValidation: failed to write re-encoded image:', err.message);
    // Non-fatal — the original (already magic-byte-validated) is still usable.
  }

  return { ok: true, sizeBytes: cleaned.length };
}

// Best-effort virus scan via VirusTotal's public API. Skipped (not "passed")
// if VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY isn't configured — callers should treat `skipped`
// distinctly from `clean`, and decide their own policy (this codebase logs
// it and lets the order proceed, since blocking launch on a paid AV
// integration isn't worth it at low volume — see SETUP.md).
async function scanBufferForMalware(buffer) {
  const apiKey = process.env.VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY;
  if (!apiKey) {
    return { skipped: true, reason: 'VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY not configured' };
  }

  try {
    // Cheap first check: has VT already seen this exact file? (hash lookup,
    // no upload needed, no rate-limit pressure)
    const hash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buffer).digest('hex');
    const lookupRes = await fetch(`https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/${hash}`, {
      headers: { 'x-apikey': apiKey },
    });

    if (lookupRes.status === 200) {
      const data = await lookupRes.json();
      const stats = data?.data?.attributes?.last_analysis_stats || {};
      const malicious = (stats.malicious || 0) + (stats.suspicious || 0);
      return { skipped: false, clean: malicious === 0, stats };
    }
    if (lookupRes.status === 404) {
      // VT has never seen this file — for a personal photo/video that's
      // expected and not itself suspicious. We don't upload user media to
      // a third party automatically (privacy), so treat unknown as
      // "not flagged" rather than paying the upload-and-wait cost here.
      return { skipped: false, clean: true, unknown: true };
    }
    return { skipped: true, reason: `VirusTotal lookup returned ${lookupRes.status}` };
  } catch (err) {
    return { skipped: true, reason: err.message };
  }
}

module.exports = {
  validateMagicBytes,
  reencodeImageInPlace,
  scanBufferForMalware,
  fetchHeadBytes,
  fetchFullObject,
  IMAGE_EXTENSIONS,
  extOf,
};

// netlify/functions/_lib/moderateMessage.js
//
// Reuses the existing generateText() helper (same Anthropic key already
// wired up for AI Polish / Character Drop / Roast Certificate) to classify
// a gift message before an order is created.
//
// WHY A MODEL AND NOT A KEYWORD LIST: several of your gift types (Savage
// Roast, Roast Certificate) are DESIGNED to be edgy/insulting between
// friends — a blunt profanity blocklist would break the actual product. A
// model can tell "affectionate roast between friends" apart from "genuine
// threat/hate speech/harassment aimed at a real person," which a keyword
// list structurally cannot.
//
// FAIL-OPEN, ON PURPOSE, MATCHING EXISTING SITE PHILOSOPHY: if the
// moderation call itself fails (Anthropic API down, key missing, rate
// limited), this ALLOWS the message through rather than blocking checkout.
// anthropicHelper.js's own header comment states this is the site's existing
// pattern ("a missing env var never blocks an order... from working"). This
// is a real security/availability tradeoff — a filter that fails open is not
// a filter during an outage — flagged explicitly here, not hidden. If you'd
// rather fail CLOSED (block checkout when moderation can't run), that's a
// one-line change (see the catch block below) — your call, not mine to
// silently decide.

const { generateText } = require('./anthropicHelper');

const SYSTEM_PROMPT = `You are a content safety classifier for Zivogift, a peer-to-peer digital gifting platform used by Indian college students to send each other personalized messages (birthday notes, memes, and INTENTIONALLY edgy "roast" content between friends).

Playful insults, roasting, dark humor, and affectionate teasing between friends are NORMAL and ALLOWED on this platform — do not flag those.

Block ONLY messages that contain:
- Direct threats of violence or harm against a real person
- Hate speech or slurs targeting race, religion, caste, gender, sexual orientation, disability, or other protected characteristics
- Sexual harassment or non-consensual sexual content about a real, identifiable person
- Content that appears to target a public official, celebrity, or authority figure with harassment, defamation, or threats
- Doxxing (sharing someone's private information with intent to harm)
- Content promoting self-harm or suicide directed at the recipient

Respond with ONLY a JSON object, nothing else: {"verdict":"allow"|"block","reason":"<one short sentence, empty string if allowed>"}`;

async function moderateMessage(text) {
  const trimmed = String(text || '').trim();
  if (!trimmed) return { allowed: true, reason: null };

  try {
    const raw = await generateText({
      system: SYSTEM_PROMPT,
      prompt: `Message to classify:\n"""${trimmed}"""`,
      maxTokens: 150,
    });

    // Model is instructed to return only JSON, but strip any stray fencing defensively.
    const cleaned = raw.replace(/```json|```/g, '').trim();
    const parsed = JSON.parse(cleaned);

    return {
      allowed: parsed.verdict !== 'block',
      reason: parsed.reason || null,
    };
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('moderateMessage: check failed, failing OPEN (message allowed through):', err.message);
    return { allowed: true, reason: null, checkFailed: true };
  }
}

module.exports = { moderateMessage };

// MSG91 OTP helper (SMS-based phone verification).
// Docs: https://docs.msg91.com/otp/otp-api/send-otp
//
// CORRECTION to an earlier version of this comment: DLT registration is
// NOT a precondition for sending any SMS through MSG91, and MSG91 account
// signup does NOT require a GST number (their signup flow explicitly lets
// you continue without one). If you're pre-registration/pre-GST right now,
// use path A below — it's a genuine, intended bridge, not a workaround.
//
// ── PATH A: trial phase, no GST/DLT yet (start here) ───────────────────────
// 1. Sign up at msg91.com — no GST required, skip that field if you don't
//    have one yet.
// 2. Dashboard → API → generate an Auth Key → Netlify env: MSG91_AUTH_KEY
// 3. Dashboard → OTP → every account gets a default OTP SMS template,
//    provided by MSG91 specifically "to use till your template is approved
//    on DLT" — no business documents, no fee. Copy its template ID →
//    Netlify env: MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID. Leave MSG91_SENDER_ID unset (the
//    default template uses MSG91's own shared sender ID, not a custom one).
// Tradeoffs, worth knowing before depending on this for real orders:
//   - The SMS carries no Zivogift branding — generic wording, shared
//     sender ID, not a custom "Zivogift" header.
//   - MSG91's OTP dashboard won't show delivery logs for it (only for
//     DLT-registered templates) — harder to debug delivery issues.
//   - Deliverability on a shared sender ID is generally a bit worse than a
//     DLT-registered branded header. Test end-to-end against real
//     Jio/Airtel/Vi numbers before fully depending on it.
//
// ── PATH B: once you've registered the business (GST + DLT) ────────────────
// Nothing in this file needs to change — only Dashboard config + env vars:
// 3. DLT registration (mandatory once you want branded/reliable delivery —
//    this is a telecom regulation, not an MSG91 rule, and it's unavoidable
//    no matter which SMS provider you pick):
//    a. Register as a "Principal Entity" on your telecom operator's DLT
//       portal (e.g. trueconnect.jio.com / airtel DLT / vilpower.in — MSG91
//       has a guided flow for this under Dashboard → DLT).
//    b. Register a Sender ID / Header (6-character alphanumeric, e.g.
//       "ZIVOGF") on the same DLT portal.
//    c. Register your exact OTP message template text on the DLT portal.
//       Variables on DLT use {#var#}, e.g.:
//         "Your Zivogift verification code is {#var#}. It expires in
//          {#var#} minutes. Don't share this code with anyone."
//       DLT approval is usually same-day to 24h.
//    d. Once approved, copy the DLT Template ID and register the *same*
//       template inside MSG91 (Dashboard → SMS → Templates → add DLT
//       Template ID + Sender ID + the exact approved content). MSG91 gives
//       you back an MSG91 Template ID — swap Netlify env MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID
//       to point at it, and set MSG91_SENDER_ID to your approved header.
//
// COST: pay-per-SMS, no subscription, on either path. Indian transactional
// SMS via MSG91 typically runs ~₹0.15–0.25/SMS.

const MSG91_BASE = 'https://control.msg91.com/api/v5/otp';

/**
 * Send an OTP to a phone number. MSG91 generates and stores the code —
 * we never see or persist it ourselves.
 *
 * @param {string} phone - normalized, e.g. '919876543210' (no '+')
 * @param {object} [opts]
 * @param {number} [opts.otpLength] - default 6
 * @param {number} [opts.otpExpiryMinutes] - default 10
 */
async function sendOtp(phone, opts = {}) {
  const authkey = process.env.MSG91_AUTH_KEY;
  const templateId = process.env.MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID;
  const senderId = process.env.MSG91_SENDER_ID;

  if (!authkey) throw new Error('Missing MSG91_AUTH_KEY env var');
  if (!templateId) throw new Error('Missing MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID env var');

  const otpLength = opts.otpLength || 6;
  const otpExpiry = opts.otpExpiryMinutes || 10;

  const params = new URLSearchParams({
    template_id: templateId,
    mobile: phone,
    otp_length: String(otpLength),
    otp_expiry: String(otpExpiry),
  });
  if (senderId) params.set('sender', senderId);

  const res = await fetch(`${MSG91_BASE}?${params.toString()}`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { authkey, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  });

  const data = await res.json();

  if (!res.ok || data.type === 'error') {
    throw new Error(`MSG91 send OTP failed: ${data.message || JSON.stringify(data)}`);
  }

  return { requestId: data.request_id || null, raw: data };
}

/**
 * Verify a code the user typed against MSG91's record for that phone.
 *
 * @param {string} phone - normalized, e.g. '919876543210'
 * @param {string} otp   - the digits the user entered
 * @returns {Promise<boolean>} true if verified
 */
async function verifyOtp(phone, otp) {
  const authkey = process.env.MSG91_AUTH_KEY;
  if (!authkey) throw new Error('Missing MSG91_AUTH_KEY env var');

  const params = new URLSearchParams({ mobile: phone, otp: String(otp) });

  const res = await fetch(`${MSG91_BASE}/verify?${params.toString()}`, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: { authkey },
  });

  const data = await res.json();

  // MSG91 returns { type: 'success', message: 'OTP verified success' }
  // or { type: 'error', message: '...' } for wrong/expired codes.
  if (data.type === 'success') return true;
  return false;
}

/**
 * Verify a Widget access-token server-side. This is the OTP WIDGET flow —
 * a different product from sendOtp/verifyOtp above, and the one that
 * actually works without DLT/Entity registration. The widget (loaded
 * client-side via https://verify.msg91.com/otp-provider.js) handles OTP
 * send + verify entirely in the browser using its own default template,
 * and hands back an access-token on success. That token proves nothing on
 * its own — anyone could fake calling a client-side success callback — so
 * this function is what actually establishes trust: it round-trips the
 * token to MSG91's own server with our secret account authkey, and only a
 * token MSG91 itself issued and hasn't already consumed will verify.
 *
 * CONFIRMED: this endpoint and payload shape were verified directly
 * against the "2. Server Side Integration" tab of the actual Zivogift
 * MSG91 widget dashboard (not just documentation) — this is exactly what
 * MSG91 shows for this account, including headers.
 *
 * @param {string} accessToken - the token from the widget's success callback
 * @returns {Promise<boolean>} true if MSG91 confirms this token is valid
 */
async function verifyAccessToken(accessToken) {
  const authkey = process.env.MSG91_AUTH_KEY;
  if (!authkey) throw new Error('Missing MSG91_AUTH_KEY env var');
  if (!accessToken) return false;

  const url = process.env.MSG91_VERIFY_TOKEN_URL || 'https://control.msg91.com/api/v5/widget/verifyAccessToken';

  const res = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Accept': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ authkey, 'access-token': accessToken }),
  });

  let data;
  try {
    data = await res.json();
  } catch {
    console.error('verifyAccessToken: non-JSON response from MSG91, status', res.status);
    return false;
  }

  // DIAGNOSTIC (Jul 2026): correct OTPs are being rejected here — see the
  // comment below, this was a known-unverified assumption. Logging the
  // full raw response on every call (success or failure) until we have
  // one real example to confirm the actual field names, then this whole
  // block should be replaced with a check against the confirmed shape.
  console.log('verifyAccessToken: raw MSG91 response, status', res.status, JSON.stringify(data));

  // MSG91's documented response shape uses type: 'success' | 'error' across
  // this API family — same convention as sendOtp/verifyOtp above. The
  // confirmed dashboard snippet for this endpoint didn't show the actual
  // response body shape (just `.then(json => console.log(json))`), so if
  // verification unexpectedly fails despite a correct OTP, log `data` here
  // once and confirm the real field name matches this assumption.
  if (res.ok && data.type === 'success') return true;

  console.warn('verifyAccessToken: MSG91 rejected token —', data.message || JSON.stringify(data));
  return false;
}

module.exports = { sendOtp, verifyOtp, verifyAccessToken };

// netlify/functions/_lib/noteStoryHelper.js
//
// Feature #14 — The Currency Note Story Card.
// For every physical note/bundle item in a paid order that has a recipient
// DOB, generates a short AI narrative ("Your Note's Story") and returns an
// HTML block to insert into the order confirmation email. Zero cost
// increase to fulfilment — it rides along in the email Resend already sends.
//
// If ANTHROPIC_API_KEY isn't set or the call fails, falls back to a warm
// static template so a missing key never blocks the confirmation email.

const { generateText } = require('./anthropicHelper');
const { serialDigitsFromDob } = require('./dobUtils');

const NOTE_PREFIXES = ['note_', 'bundle_'];

const STORY_SYSTEM_PROMPT =
  'You write short, warm "note story" narratives that ship alongside a real currency note gift — the note\'s ' +
  'serial number is chosen to encode the recipient\'s birth date. Given the denomination(s), the digits their ' +
  'birth date forms, the recipient\'s name, and optionally a note from the sender, write a ~120-150 word piece ' +
  'in second person addressed to the recipient. Touch on: what a note like this has likely travelled through ' +
  '(hands, cities, years) before reaching them, what it means that its serial number carries their exact birth ' +
  'date, and (if a sender message was given) a light nod to why it was chosen for them. Tone: tender, a little ' +
  'poetic, never saccharine or corny. Respond with ONLY the narrative text — no title, no preamble, no quotes.';

function fallbackStory(recipientName, denominationLabel, serialDigits) {
  return `This ${denominationLabel} has likely passed through more hands than either of us could count — ` +
    `market stalls, someone's first salary, a wallet forgotten in a bus seat — long before it found its way ` +
    `here, to you. What makes this one different is small but deliberate: its serial number carries ${serialDigits}, ` +
    `the exact shape of ${recipientName}'s birth date. Everything else about it is ordinary. That one detail isn't. ` +
    `Keep it somewhere it won't get spent by accident — it's worth more as a story than as ten rupees.`;
}

function denominationLabelFor(item) {
  // name_snapshot is already a clean label, e.g. "₹100 Birthday Serial Note" or "Classic Set"
  return item.name_snapshot || 'this note';
}

async function buildOneStory(item) {
  const serialDigits = serialDigitsFromDob(item.recipient_dob);
  if (!serialDigits) return null;

  const recipientName = item.recipient_name || 'them';
  const denominationLabel = denominationLabelFor(item);

  let story;
  try {
    const prompt = `Denomination(s): ${denominationLabel}. Recipient name: ${recipientName}. ` +
      `Serial-encoded digits (from their birth date): ${serialDigits}.` +
      (item.personalization_message ? ` Sender's note to include a light nod to: "${item.personalization_message}".` : '');
    story = await generateText({ system: STORY_SYSTEM_PROMPT, prompt, maxTokens: 300 });
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn('noteStoryHelper: Claude generation failed, using fallback —', err.message);
    story = fallbackStory(recipientName, denominationLabel, serialDigits);
  }

  return { recipientName, denominationLabel, story };
}

// Returns an HTML string (possibly empty) to append into the order
// confirmation email, one block per qualifying item.
async function buildNoteStoryEmailSection(items) {
  const qualifying = (items || []).filter(
    (i) => i.product_id && NOTE_PREFIXES.some((p) => i.product_id.startsWith(p)) && i.recipient_dob
  );
  if (!qualifying.length) return '';

  const results = await Promise.all(qualifying.map(buildOneStory));
  const blocks = results.filter(Boolean).map(({ recipientName, denominationLabel, story }) => `
    <div style="margin:18px 0;padding:20px 18px;border-radius:12px;background:linear-gradient(160deg,#1a1200,#0d0a00);border:1px solid rgba(212,160,23,0.35);">
      <div style="font-size:11px;letter-spacing:3px;color:#D4A017;opacity:0.85;margin-bottom:8px;">✦ YOUR NOTE'S STORY ✦</div>
      <div style="font-size:13px;color:#9c9890;margin-bottom:10px;">${denominationLabel} — for ${recipientName}</div>
      <div style="font-size:14px;color:#f5f5f0;line-height:1.7;font-style:italic;">${story}</div>
    </div>`);

  if (!blocks.length) return '';

  return `
    <div style="margin-top:8px;">
      <h3 style="font-size:15px;font-weight:700;margin:20px 0 4px;color:#f5f5f0;">A little extra, just for this order 📜</h3>
      ${blocks.join('')}
    </div>`;
}

module.exports = { buildNoteStoryEmailSection };
