// netlify/functions/_lib/waNotify.js
//
// "TELL SURESH A CUSTOMER MESSAGED" — the alerting layer.
//
// Storing a message guarantees it is not LOST. It does not guarantee it is
// SEEN, and an unseen bulk-order enquiry is a missed order. This file closes
// that gap with two independent channels:
//
//   1. EMAIL  (free, ON by default)
//      Resend -> ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL. Costs nothing, arrives as a phone
//      notification within seconds. This alone solves the problem.
//
//   2. WHATSAPP RELAY  (paid, OFF by default)
//      A WhatsApp message to ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER (a personal number) so a
//      reply can be typed without opening anything. Business-initiated, so
//      the first message after a quiet spell costs a utility-template fee —
//      which is exactly why it ships disabled.
//
// BOTH are behind DB kill switches (pause_wa_alerts / pause_wa_relay) so they
// can be flipped from Supabase with no redeploy and no build credits.
//
// THROTTLING
// ----------
// A customer sending eight rapid messages must not produce eight alerts. Both
// channels are throttled to once per contact per ALERT_THROTTLE_MINUTES using
// wa_contacts.last_alert_at. The messages are all stored regardless — this
// throttles the NOTIFICATION, never the capture.
//
// ENV:
//   ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL       — where the free alert goes
//   ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER    — personal number for the relay (Run D)
//   WHATSAPP_RELAY_TEMPLATE  — approved template used when the relay's own
//                              24h window with you has closed
//   SITE_URL                 — for the deep link into the admin inbox

const { getSettings } = require('./adminSettings');
const { sendEmail, emailShell, ctaButton, escapeHtml, BRAND } = require('./resend');
const { sendWhatsAppText } = require('./whatsappSession');
const { sendWhatsAppTemplate } = require('./whatsapp');
const { toPhone10 } = require('./waInbox');

const ALERT_THROTTLE_MINUTES = 60;

function siteUrl() {
  return (process.env.SITE_URL || 'https://zivogift.com').replace(/\/+$/, '');
}

/**
 * True when this contact has not been alerted on recently.
 * Fail-OPEN: if the check itself errors we alert anyway, because a duplicate
 * notification is harmless and a suppressed one is not.
 */
function throttleAllows(contact) {
  if (!contact || !contact.last_alert_at) return true;
  const elapsedMin = (Date.now() - new Date(contact.last_alert_at).getTime()) / 60000;
  return !(elapsedMin < ALERT_THROTTLE_MINUTES);
}

function contactLabel(contact) {
  const name = contact && contact.profile_name;
  const phone = (contact && contact.phone10) || '';
  return name ? `${name} (${phone})` : phone;
}

// ── EMAIL (free) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

async function sendEmailAlert(contact, preview) {
  const to = process.env.ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL;
  if (!to) {
    console.warn('waNotify: ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL not set — no free alert will be sent.');
    return { ok: false, reason: 'ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL not set' };
  }

  const who = contactLabel(contact);
  const link = `${siteUrl()}/admin.html#messages`;
  const quoted = escapeHtml(String(preview || '').slice(0, 400));

  // Built from the exported shell primitives. The internal `row` helpers in
  // resend.js are NOT exported, so these rows are written out longhand in the
  // same table-row shape emailShell expects for `bodyRows`.
  const bodyRows =
    `
                      <tr><td align="center" style="padding:0 0 10px;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:2px;text-transform:uppercase;color:${BRAND.gold};">New customer message</td></tr>
                      <tr><td align="center" class="zg-head" style="padding:0 0 10px;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:28px;line-height:36px;font-weight:bold;color:${BRAND.ink};">${escapeHtml(who)}</td></tr>
                      <tr><td align="left" style="padding:0 0 18px;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:23px;color:${BRAND.muted};">
                        <div style="border-left:3px solid ${BRAND.gold};padding:10px 14px;background:${BRAND.panelAlt};border-radius:8px;white-space:pre-wrap;">${quoted}</div>
                      </td></tr>
                      <tr><td align="left" style="padding:0 0 20px;font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:13px;line-height:20px;color:${BRAND.faint};">
                        You can reply free of charge for the next 24 hours. After that Meta requires an approved template.
                      </td></tr>
                      <tr><td align="center" style="padding:0 0 8px;">${ctaButton(link, 'Open Customer Messages', BRAND.gold)}</td></tr>`;

  const html = emailShell({
    title: `WhatsApp message from ${who}`,
    preheader: String(preview || '').slice(0, 120),
    bodyRows,
  });

  try {
    await sendEmail({
      to,
      subject: `💬 WhatsApp from ${who}`,
      html,
      text: `${who} messaged ZivoGift on WhatsApp:\n\n${preview}\n\nReply: ${link}`,
    });
    return { ok: true };
  } catch (e) {
    console.warn('waNotify: email alert failed:', (e && e.message) || e);
    return { ok: false, reason: String((e && e.message) || e) };
  }
}

// ── WHATSAPP RELAY (paid, off by default) ───────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Forwards the customer's message to your personal number.
 *
 * Tries FREE TEXT first. That succeeds whenever you have replied to the relay
 * within the last 24h — i.e. during any active support day, this costs
 * nothing. Only when that window has closed does it fall back to a billable
 * template, and only if one is configured.
 *
 * The phone10 is embedded in the text on purpose: it is what makes a
 * prefix-style reply ("9876543210 yes we can do 50 boxes") resolvable, and it
 * is the fallback when a quoted reply carries no context id.
 */
async function sendWhatsAppRelay(contact, preview) {
  const adminNumber = process.env.ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER;
  if (!adminNumber) return { ok: false, reason: 'ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER not set' };

  // Guard against configuring the business number as the relay target, which
  // would make the number message itself in a loop.
  if (toPhone10(adminNumber) === toPhone10(contact && contact.phone10)) {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'relay target is the customer — refusing to loop' };
  }

  const who = contactLabel(contact);
  const text =
    `💬 *${who}*\n\n${String(preview || '').slice(0, 900)}\n\n` +
    `Reply to this message to answer them, or send:\n` +
    `\`${contact.phone10} your reply\``;

  const direct = await sendWhatsAppText({ to: adminNumber, text });
  if (direct.ok) return { ok: true, via: 'session', messageId: direct.messageId };

  if (!direct.windowExpired) {
    return { ok: false, reason: (direct.error && direct.error.message) || 'relay send failed' };
  }

  // Window with the admin has closed — a template is the only way through.
  const tpl = process.env.WHATSAPP_RELAY_TEMPLATE;
  if (!tpl) {
    return { ok: false, reason: '24h relay window closed and WHATSAPP_RELAY_TEMPLATE is not set' };
  }
  try {
    const res = await sendWhatsAppTemplate({
      recipientPhone: adminNumber,
      templateName: tpl,
      bodyVariables: [who, String(preview || '').slice(0, 300)],
    });
    return { ok: true, via: 'template', messageId: res.messageId };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, reason: String((e && e.message) || e) };
  }
}

// ── ORCHESTRATOR ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Called by whatsapp-webhook.js AFTER the message is safely stored.
 *
 * Never throws. An alerting failure must never propagate into the webhook,
 * because the webhook returning non-200 makes Meta retry the whole payload.
 *
 * @returns {Promise<{email:object, relay:object, throttled:boolean}>}
 */
async function notifyNewMessage(supabase, { contact, preview, isDuplicate, sourceWaId }) {
  const result = { email: { ok: false }, relay: { ok: false }, throttled: false };
  // A webhook retry is not a new customer message.
  if (isDuplicate || !contact) return result;

  try {
    if (!throttleAllows(contact)) {
      result.throttled = true;
      return result;
    }

    const settings = await getSettings(supabase);

    if (settings.pause_wa_alerts !== true) {
      result.email = await sendEmailAlert(contact, preview);
    } else {
      result.email = { ok: false, reason: 'pause_wa_alerts is ON' };
    }

    // Ships TRUE (off). Flip the row in admin_settings to enable.
    if (settings.pause_wa_relay !== true) {
      result.relay = await sendWhatsAppRelay(contact, preview);

      // Remember which customer this forwarded message was about, so that
      // long-pressing it on the phone and hitting Reply resolves back to the
      // right conversation. Without this, replies depend on typing the
      // number prefix.
      if (result.relay.ok && result.relay.messageId) {
        try {
          const { registerRelay } = require('./waRelay');
          await registerRelay(supabase, {
            relayWaId: result.relay.messageId,
            contact,
            sourceWaId: sourceWaId || null,
          });
        } catch (e) {
          console.warn('waNotify: relay map registration skipped:', (e && e.message) || e);
        }
      }
    } else {
      result.relay = { ok: false, reason: 'pause_wa_relay is ON' };
    }

    // Stamp the throttle only if something actually went out, so a
    // misconfiguration does not silently suppress the next hour of alerts.
    if (result.email.ok || result.relay.ok) {
      await supabase.from('wa_contacts')
        .update({ last_alert_at: new Date().toISOString() })
        .eq('id', contact.id);
    }
  } catch (e) {
    console.warn('waNotify.notifyNewMessage failed:', (e && e.message) || e);
  }
  return result;
}

module.exports = {
  ALERT_THROTTLE_MINUTES,
  notifyNewMessage,
  sendEmailAlert,
  sendWhatsAppRelay,
  throttleAllows,
};



=====================================================
FILE: netlify\functions\_lib\waRelay.js

// netlify/functions/_lib/waRelay.js
//
// THE PERSONAL-NUMBER RELAY — answer customers from your own WhatsApp.
//
// HOW IT WORKS
// ------------
// When ZivoGift's number sends a notification TO your personal number, your
// phone shows it as an ordinary chat. If you reply, that reply travels back
// to the ZivoGift number — which means it lands on the SAME inbound webhook.
// This file recognises those replies, works out which customer they are meant
// for, and forwards them on from the ZivoGift number.
//
// The customer never sees your personal number. You never install anything.
//
// RESOLVING "WHICH CUSTOMER IS THIS FOR?"
// ---------------------------------------
// Three strategies, in descending order of certainty:
//
//   1. QUOTED REPLY (best). Long-press the notification -> Reply. Meta puts
//      the quoted message id in context.id, which wa_relay_map resolves to
//      exactly one customer. Zero typing, zero ambiguity.
//
//   2. NUMBER PREFIX. "9876543210 Sure, we can do 50 boxes."
//      Works even when quoting fails, and is how you START a conversation
//      rather than continue one.
//
//   3. LAST CONVERSATION, but ONLY when it is unambiguous — a single customer
//      relayed within the last AMBIGUITY_WINDOW_MIN minutes. If two or more
//      customers are in play, the relay REFUSES TO GUESS and asks which one.
//      Sending a reply to the wrong customer is far worse than one extra tap.
//
// COMMANDS
//   LIST              — open conversations with unread messages
//   CLOSE <phone10>   — mark a conversation done
//   HELP              — usage
//
// ENV: ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER (required), plus the usual WhatsApp vars.
// Kill switch: admin_settings.pause_wa_relay (seeded TRUE = relay OFF).

const { sendWhatsAppText } = require('./whatsappSession');
const { recordOutbound, toPhone10 } = require('./waInbox');
const { getSettings } = require('./adminSettings');

// How recently a customer must have been relayed for strategy 3 to consider
// them "the current conversation".
const AMBIGUITY_WINDOW_MIN = 90;

/** Is this inbound message from the configured admin personal number? */
function isFromAdmin(fromPhone) {
  const admin = process.env.ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER;
  if (!admin) return false;
  const a = toPhone10(admin);
  return !!a && a === toPhone10(fromPhone);
}

async function replyToAdmin(text) {
  try {
    await sendWhatsAppText({ to: process.env.ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER, text });
  } catch (e) {
    console.warn('waRelay: could not message the admin back:', (e && e.message) || e);
  }
}

/** Records the mapping so a quoted reply to this relay message resolves later. */
async function registerRelay(supabase, { relayWaId, contact, sourceWaId }) {
  if (!relayWaId || !contact) return;
  try {
    await supabase.from('wa_relay_map').insert({
      relay_wa_id: relayWaId,
      contact_id: contact.id,
      phone10: contact.phone10,
      source_wa_id: sourceWaId || null,
    });
  } catch (e) {
    // A missing table just means quoted replies fall back to the prefix form.
    console.warn('waRelay: relay map write failed (quoted replies will need the number prefix):', (e && e.message) || e);
  }
}

// ── COMMANDS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

async function commandList(supabase) {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('wa_contacts')
    .select('phone10, profile_name, unread_count, last_message_preview, last_message_at, window_expires_at')
    .eq('status', 'open')
    .order('last_message_at', { ascending: false })
    .limit(10);

  if (error) return replyToAdmin(`Could not read conversations: ${error.message}`);
  if (!data || !data.length) return replyToAdmin('No open conversations right now. 👍');

  const lines = data.map((c) => {
    const open = c.window_expires_at && new Date(c.window_expires_at) > new Date();
    const unread = c.unread_count > 0 ? ` (${c.unread_count} unread)` : '';
    return `• *${c.profile_name || c.phone10}* ${c.phone10}${unread}${open ? '' : ' ⏳'}\n  ${String(c.last_message_preview || '').slice(0, 70)}`;
  });
  return replyToAdmin(`*Open conversations*\n\n${lines.join('\n')}\n\n⏳ = 24h window closed\nReply with: \`<number> your message\``);
}

async function commandClose(supabase, phone10) {
  const { error } = await supabase.from('wa_contacts')
    .update({ status: 'closed', unread_count: 0, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() })
    .eq('phone10', phone10);
  if (error) return replyToAdmin(`Could not close ${phone10}: ${error.message}`);
  return replyToAdmin(`✅ Marked ${phone10} as done.`);
}

function commandHelp() {
  return replyToAdmin(
    '*ZivoGift relay*\n\n' +
    '• Reply to a forwarded message to answer that customer\n' +
    '• Or type: `9876543210 your message`\n\n' +
    '*Commands*\n' +
    '• `LIST` — open conversations\n' +
    '• `CLOSE 9876543210` — mark done\n' +
    '• `HELP` — this message'
  );
}

// ── TARGET RESOLUTION ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

async function resolveTarget(supabase, msg, text) {
  // 1. Quoted reply
  const quotedId = msg.context && msg.context.id;
  if (quotedId) {
    try {
      const { data } = await supabase
        .from('wa_relay_map').select('contact_id, phone10').eq('relay_wa_id', quotedId).limit(1);
      if (data && data.length) {
        const { data: c } = await supabase
          .from('wa_contacts').select('*').eq('id', data[0].contact_id).limit(1);
        if (c && c.length) return { contact: c[0], body: text, via: 'quote' };
      }
    } catch (e) { /* fall through to the prefix form */ }
  }

  // 2. Number prefix
  const m = /^(?:\+?91)?\s*([6-9]\d{9})\b[\s:,-]*([\s\S]*)$/.exec(text.trim());
  if (m) {
    const phone10 = m[1];
    const rest = (m[2] || '').trim();
    const { data: c } = await supabase.from('wa_contacts').select('*').eq('phone10', phone10).limit(1);
    if (c && c.length) return { contact: c[0], body: rest, via: 'prefix' };
    // Unknown number: still a valid target — this is how you open a
    // conversation with someone who has not messaged first (template rules
    // still apply, and the send below will report if it is not allowed).
    return { contact: { phone10, wa_phone: `91${phone10}`, window_expires_at: null, id: null }, body: rest, via: 'prefix-new' };
  }

  // 3. Last conversation, only if unambiguous
  const since = new Date(Date.now() - AMBIGUITY_WINDOW_MIN * 60000).toISOString();
  try {
    const { data } = await supabase
      .from('wa_relay_map').select('contact_id, phone10').gte('created_at', since)
      .order('created_at', { ascending: false }).limit(20);
    const distinct = [...new Set((data || []).map((r) => r.contact_id))];
    if (distinct.length === 1) {
      const { data: c } = await supabase.from('wa_contacts').select('*').eq('id', distinct[0]).limit(1);
      if (c && c.length) return { contact: c[0], body: text, via: 'implicit' };
    }
    if (distinct.length > 1) {
      return { ambiguous: true, count: distinct.length };
    }
  } catch (e) { /* treated as "no recent relay" */ }

  return { none: true };
}

// ── ENTRY POINT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Handles an inbound message that came FROM the admin's personal number.
 *
 * @returns {Promise<boolean>} true if this message was a relay instruction and
 *          must NOT be treated as a customer message. false means "not mine".
 */
async function handleAdminRelayMessage(supabase, msg) {
  if (!isFromAdmin(msg && msg.from)) return false;

  // The relay is billable, so it respects the same kill switch as the
  // outbound notification. With it paused, your own messages are simply
  // ignored rather than silently forwarded to a customer.
  try {
    const settings = await getSettings(supabase);
    if (settings.pause_wa_relay === true) {
      console.log('waRelay: inbound admin message ignored — pause_wa_relay is ON');
      return true;
    }
  } catch (e) { /* settings unreadable — continue, the admin is trusted */ }

  const text = ((msg.text && msg.text.body) || '').trim();
  if (!text) {
    await replyToAdmin('I can only relay text replies. Send `HELP` for the commands.');
    return true;
  }

  const upper = text.toUpperCase();
  if (upper === 'HELP' || upper === '?') { await commandHelp(); return true; }
  if (upper === 'LIST') { await commandList(supabase); return true; }
  const closeMatch = /^CLOSE\s+(?:\+?91)?\s*([6-9]\d{9})$/.exec(upper);
  if (closeMatch) { await commandClose(supabase, closeMatch[1]); return true; }

  const target = await resolveTarget(supabase, msg, text);

  if (target.ambiguous) {
    await replyToAdmin(
      `⚠️ ${target.count} conversations are active, so I will not guess who that was for.\n\n` +
      'Reply directly to the forwarded message, or start with the number:\n`9876543210 your message`'
    );
    return true;
  }
  if (target.none) {
    await replyToAdmin('I could not tell which customer that was for. Reply to a forwarded message, or use `9876543210 your message`. Send `LIST` to see open conversations.');
    return true;
  }
  if (!target.body) {
    await replyToAdmin('That looked like a number with no message after it. Try `9876543210 your message`.');
    return true;
  }

  // ── Forward to the customer ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  const to = target.contact.wa_phone || target.contact.phone10;
  const res = await sendWhatsAppText({ to, text: target.body });

  await recordOutbound(supabase, {
    phone: to,
    waMessageId: res.ok ? res.messageId : null,
    msgType: 'text',
    body: target.body,
    status: res.ok ? 'sent' : 'failed',
    source: 'relay',
    sentByAdmin: 'relay:' + toPhone10(process.env.ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER || ''),
    errorCode: res.ok ? null : String((res.error && res.error.code) || ''),
    errorMessage: res.ok ? null : (res.error && res.error.message) || null,
    markRead: true,
  });

  if (res.ok) {
    await replyToAdmin(`✅ Sent to ${target.contact.profile_name || target.contact.phone10}.`);
  } else if (res.windowExpired) {
    // Honest, specific, and tells you what to do instead — rather than a bare
    // "failed" that leaves you assuming the customer got it.
    await replyToAdmin(
      `❌ Not sent. The 24-hour window with ${target.contact.phone10} has closed, so Meta will only deliver an approved template.\n\n` +
      'Open the Messages tab in the admin panel to send one.'
    );
  } else {
    await replyToAdmin(`❌ Not sent to ${target.contact.phone10}: ${(res.error && res.error.message) || 'unknown error'}`);
  }

  return true;
}

module.exports = {
  AMBIGUITY_WINDOW_MIN,
  isFromAdmin,
  registerRelay,
  handleAdminRelayMessage,
  resolveTarget,
};

FILE: netlify\functions\_lib\whatsapp.js

// netlify/functions/_lib/whatsapp.js
//
// Meta WhatsApp Cloud API helper -- ZivoGift.
//
// ============================================================================
// WHAT CHANGED IN THIS VERSION AND WHY
// ============================================================================
//
// The previous version GUESSED the shape of every template send: it walked a
// list of candidate language codes, then retried with/without an image header,
// and threw on the first error it did not recognise. That works, but it means
// every single send pays 1-6 wasted round trips to Meta, and a template whose
// real body has 3 variables while the code sends 2 fails permanently with no
// way to self-correct.
//
// This version INTROSPECTS instead of guessing. On first use it calls
//     GET /{WHATSAPP_WABA_ID}/message_templates
// and caches, per template name:
//     - the exact approved language code
//     - the exact BODY variable count
//     - whether there is a HEADER, and of what format (IMAGE / TEXT / none)
//     - whether there are dynamic URL buttons
//     - the approval status (APPROVED / PENDING / REJECTED / PAUSED / DISABLED)
// The outbound payload is then built to match the approved definition exactly,
// on the first try. This is the single biggest reason WhatsApp sends were
// failing while email worked: the payload shape never matched the template.
//
// Everything degrades gracefully. If WHATSAPP_WABA_ID is not set, or the
// introspection call fails (permissions, network), we fall back to the old
// candidate-ladder behaviour so nothing regresses.
//
// Other fixes in this version:
//
//   1. ERROR CLASSIFICATION. Meta errors are now sorted into RETRYABLE
//      (rate limit, transient 5xx, internal) vs TERMINAL (bad token, paused
//      template, recipient not on WhatsApp). Retryable errors get exponential
//      backoff with jitter INSIDE this helper, so a 12:00 AM burst that trips
//      Meta's per-second cap no longer burns one of the scheduler's four
//      attempts. Terminal errors throw immediately with `.terminal = true` so
//      the caller can stop retrying and fall back to email.
//
//   2. BODY PARAMETER COUNT is now reconciled against the real template.
//      Too few variables are padded with a safe placeholder; too many are
//      truncated. Meta rejects the whole message on a count mismatch
//      (#132000), so this alone fixes templates that drifted from the code.
//
//   3. BODY PARAMETER CONTENT. Meta forbids newlines, tabs and runs of 4+
//      spaces inside a body variable, AND rejects empty strings. Variables are
//      flattened and empty ones replaced with a single dash, which Meta
//      accepts. (An empty variable is error #132012 and was silently possible
//      whenever recipient_name or occasion was null.)
//
//   4. STRUCTURED RESULT. Every send returns { messageId, language, waId,
//      templateName, usedIntrospection, attempts } so gift-scheduler can
//      persist the message id and later match it to a delivery receipt from
//      whatsapp-webhook.js.
//
// ============================================================================
// REQUIRED ENV
//   WHATSAPP_TOKEN             - permanent System User token
//   WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID   - Phone Number ID (digits only)
// STRONGLY RECOMMENDED
//   WHATSAPP_WABA_ID           - WhatsApp Business Account ID. Enables
//                                introspection. WhatsApp Manager -> Settings,
//                                or Business Settings -> Accounts -> WhatsApp
//                                Accounts -> (your account) -> ID.
// OPTIONAL
//   WHATSAPP_GRAPH_VERSION     - defaults to v20.0
//   WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_LANG     - fallback language when introspection is off
//   WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_NAME     - override for the gift delivery template
// ============================================================================

const GRAPH_API_VERSION = process.env.WHATSAPP_GRAPH_VERSION || 'v20.0';

// ── Meta error codes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const ERR_TEMPLATE_TRANSLATION_MISSING = 132001; // wrong/unknown language code
const ERR_PARAM_COUNT_MISMATCH         = 132000; // component/param count wrong
const ERR_TEMPLATE_PAUSED              = 132015; // paused for quality reasons
const ERR_TEMPLATE_DISABLED            = 132016; // disabled for quality reasons
const ERR_PARAM_FORMAT_MISMATCH        = 132012; // param format wrong
const ERR_GENERIC_INVALID_PARAM        = 100;    // Meta catch-all bad payload
const ERR_AUTH                         = 190;    // token expired/invalid
const ERR_RATE_LIMIT                   = 130429; // cloud api throughput cap
const ERR_SPAM_RATE_LIMIT              = 131048; // spam-rate limit hit
const ERR_ACCOUNT_LIMIT                = 131056; // pair rate limit
const ERR_TOO_MANY_CALLS               = 4;      // application request limit
const ERR_TEMPORARILY_BLOCKED          = 368;
const ERR_INTERNAL                     = 131000; // generic Meta internal
const ERR_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD               = 131052; // could not download the media
const ERR_MEDIA_UPLOAD                 = 131053; // could not use the media
const ERR_RECIPIENT_NOT_WA             = 131026; // "message undeliverable"

// Errors where waiting and trying the identical payload again is sensible.
const RETRYABLE = new Set([
  ERR_RATE_LIMIT, ERR_SPAM_RATE_LIMIT, ERR_ACCOUNT_LIMIT, ERR_TOO_MANY_CALLS,
  ERR_TEMPORARILY_BLOCKED, ERR_INTERNAL,
]);

// Errors that mean "Meta could not fetch the header image you linked".
//
// THIS IS A LIKELY ORIGINAL CAUSE OF THE LAUNCH FAILURE, so it gets its own
// handling rather than being lumped in with generic failures. _lib/r2Client.js
// falls back to `https://{bucket}.{accountId}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/...`
// when R2_PUBLIC_URL is unset -- that is the S3 API endpoint, which returns
// 401 to an unauthenticated fetch. Email delivers fine with a broken <img>;
// WhatsApp rejects the ENTIRE message if it cannot download the header media.
// That asymmetry is exactly "the email pipeline works but WhatsApp never sends".
//
// A gift that arrives without its card image is enormously better than a gift
// that does not arrive, so we drop the header and resend.
const MEDIA_ERRORS = new Set([ERR_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD, ERR_MEDIA_UPLOAD]);

function looksLikeMediaError(described) {
  if (MEDIA_ERRORS.has(described.code)) return true;
  // Meta also reports link-fetch problems as a generic #100 whose detail text
  // names the media/link parameter.
  return described.code === ERR_GENERIC_INVALID_PARAM &&
         /media|image|url|link|download/i.test(described.message || '');
}

// Errors where nothing about this send will ever work. Fail fast so the
// caller can fall back to email instead of burning retries.
const TERMINAL = new Set([
  ERR_AUTH, ERR_TEMPLATE_PAUSED, ERR_TEMPLATE_DISABLED, ERR_RECIPIENT_NOT_WA,
]);

const MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES = 3;

// ── Per-container caches ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
let templateCatalogue = null;      // Map<name, definition> once introspected
let templateCataloguePromise = null;
let introspectionFailed = false;
const resolvedLanguage   = new Map(); // fallback path: name -> working language
const headerlessTemplate = new Set(); // fallback path: name -> reject header
const mediaUnreachable   = new Set(); // name -> Meta cannot fetch our image URL

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Template introspection
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Counts the highest {{n}} placeholder in a body string. Meta returns the raw
// template text, so this is the authoritative variable count.
function countPositionalParams(text) {
  const matches = String(text || '').match(/\{\{\s*(\d+)\s*\}\}/g) || [];
  let max = 0;
  for (const m of matches) {
    const n = parseInt(m.replace(/[^\d]/g, ''), 10);
    if (Number.isFinite(n) && n > max) max = n;
  }
  return max;
}

function parseTemplateDefinition(tpl) {
  const components = tpl.components || [];
  const body   = components.find((c) => String(c.type).toUpperCase() === 'BODY');
  const header = components.find((c) => String(c.type).toUpperCase() === 'HEADER');
  const buttons = components.find((c) => String(c.type).toUpperCase() === 'BUTTONS');

  const headerFormat = header ? String(header.format || 'TEXT').toUpperCase() : null;

  // A URL button with a {{1}} in it needs a matching button component on send.
  let dynamicUrlButtonIndex = -1;
  if (buttons && Array.isArray(buttons.buttons)) {
    buttons.buttons.forEach((b, i) => {
      if (String(b.type).toUpperCase() === 'URL' && /\{\{\s*\d+\s*\}\}/.test(b.url || '')) {
        if (dynamicUrlButtonIndex === -1) dynamicUrlButtonIndex = i;
      }
    });
  }

  return {
    name: tpl.name,
    language: tpl.language,
    status: String(tpl.status || '').toUpperCase(),
    category: tpl.category,
    bodyParamCount: body ? countPositionalParams(body.text) : 0,
    headerFormat,                                   // 'IMAGE' | 'TEXT' | 'VIDEO' | 'DOCUMENT' | null
    headerParamCount: header && headerFormat === 'TEXT' ? countPositionalParams(header.text) : 0,
    dynamicUrlButtonIndex,
  };
}

// Fetches every template on the WABA (paginated) and builds the catalogue.
// Only APPROVED templates are usable; we keep the others so error messages can
// say "your template is PENDING" instead of "not found".
async function loadTemplateCatalogue() {
  const wabaId = process.env.WHATSAPP_WABA_ID;
  const token  = process.env.WHATSAPP_TOKEN;
  if (!wabaId || !token) return null;

  const catalogue = new Map();
  let url = `https://graph.facebook.com/${GRAPH_API_VERSION}/${wabaId}/message_templates` +
            `?fields=name,language,status,category,components&limit=100`;

  for (let page = 0; page < 10 && url; page += 1) {
    const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
    const data = await res.json().catch(() => null);
    if (!res.ok || !data || data.error) {
      const msg = data && data.error ? data.error.message : `HTTP ${res.status}`;
      throw new Error(`template introspection failed: ${msg}`);
    }
    for (const tpl of data.data || []) {
      const def = parseTemplateDefinition(tpl);
      const existing = catalogue.get(def.name);
      // Prefer an APPROVED translation over any other, otherwise first wins.
      if (!existing || (def.status === 'APPROVED' && existing.status !== 'APPROVED')) {
        catalogue.set(def.name, def);
      }
    }
    url = data.paging && data.paging.next ? data.paging.next : null;
  }
  return catalogue;
}

// Memoised, and never retried in the same container once it has hard-failed --
// a missing WABA_ID must not add latency to every send for the whole lifetime.
async function getTemplateCatalogue() {
  if (templateCatalogue) return templateCatalogue;
  if (introspectionFailed) return null;
  if (!templateCataloguePromise) {
    templateCataloguePromise = loadTemplateCatalogue()
      .then((cat) => {
        if (cat && cat.size) {
          templateCatalogue = cat;
          console.log(`whatsapp: introspected ${cat.size} templates from WABA`);
        } else {
          introspectionFailed = true;
          if (!process.env.WHATSAPP_WABA_ID) {
            console.warn('whatsapp: WHATSAPP_WABA_ID not set -- falling back to shape guessing. Set it to make sends deterministic.');
          }
        }
        return templateCatalogue;
      })
      .catch((err) => {
        introspectionFailed = true;
        console.warn(`whatsapp: ${err.message} -- falling back to shape guessing`);
        return null;
      });
  }
  return templateCataloguePromise;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Payload building
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Meta rejects body parameters containing newlines, tabs or 4+ consecutive
// spaces, and rejects empty strings outright. Flatten, collapse, and never
// return ''. A single dash is accepted everywhere and reads as "not supplied".
function sanitizeBodyVariable(value) {
  const flat = String(value === null || value === undefined ? '' : value)
    .replace(/[\r\n]+/g, ' ')
    .replace(/\t+/g, ' ')
    .replace(/ {2,}/g, ' ')
    .trim();
  return flat.length ? flat : '-';
}

function textParams(values) {
  return values.map((v) => ({ type: 'text', text: sanitizeBodyVariable(v) }));
}

// Reconciles what the caller supplied against what the template actually
// declares. Padding/truncating here is what turns a hard #132000 rejection
// into a delivered message.
function reconcileBodyVariables(supplied, expectedCount, templateName) {
  const vars = Array.isArray(supplied) ? supplied.slice() : [];
  if (expectedCount === null || expectedCount === undefined) return vars;
  if (vars.length > expectedCount) {
    console.warn(`whatsapp: "${templateName}" expects ${expectedCount} body vars, got ${vars.length} -- truncating`);
    return vars.slice(0, expectedCount);
  }
  while (vars.length < expectedCount) {
    console.warn(`whatsapp: "${templateName}" expects ${expectedCount} body vars, got ${supplied.length} -- padding`);
    vars.push('-');
  }
  return vars;
}

// Builds the exact component array the approved template requires.
function buildComponentsFromDefinition(def, { bodyVariables, imageUrl, headerVariables, urlButtonParam }) {
  const components = [];

  if (def.headerFormat === 'IMAGE' && imageUrl) {
    components.push({ type: 'header', parameters: [{ type: 'image', image: { link: imageUrl } }] });
  } else if (def.headerFormat === 'TEXT' && def.headerParamCount > 0) {
    const hv = reconcileBodyVariables(headerVariables || [], def.headerParamCount, def.name);
    components.push({ type: 'header', parameters: textParams(hv) });
  }

  if (def.bodyParamCount > 0) {
    const bv = reconcileBodyVariables(bodyVariables, def.bodyParamCount, def.name);
    components.push({ type: 'body', parameters: textParams(bv) });
  }

  if (def.dynamicUrlButtonIndex >= 0 && urlButtonParam) {
    components.push({
      type: 'button',
      sub_type: 'url',
      index: String(def.dynamicUrlButtonIndex),
      parameters: [{ type: 'text', text: sanitizeBodyVariable(urlButtonParam) }],
    });
  }

  return components;
}

// Legacy guessing path, used only when introspection is unavailable.
function buildComponentsLegacy({ bodyVariables, imageUrl, includeHeader }) {
  const components = [];
  if (includeHeader && imageUrl) {
    components.push({ type: 'header', parameters: [{ type: 'image', image: { link: imageUrl } }] });
  }
  if (bodyVariables.length > 0) {
    components.push({ type: 'body', parameters: textParams(bodyVariables) });
  }
  return components;
}

function languageCandidates(explicit) {
  return [...new Set([
    explicit,
    process.env.WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_LANG,
    'en_US', 'en', 'en_GB',
  ].filter(Boolean))];
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Transport
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function describeMetaError(data, status) {
  const err = data && data.error;
  if (!err) return { code: null, message: `HTTP ${status}: ${JSON.stringify(data).slice(0, 300)}` };
  const details = err.error_data && err.error_data.details ? ` -- ${err.error_data.details}` : '';
  return { code: err.code, subcode: err.error_subcode, message: `${err.message} (code ${err.code})${details}` };
}

function sleep(ms) { return new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); }

async function postToMeta(payload, { token, phoneNumId }) {
  const url = `https://graph.facebook.com/${GRAPH_API_VERSION}/${phoneNumId}/messages`;
  let res;
  try {
    res = await fetch(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
      body: JSON.stringify(payload),
    });
  } catch (netErr) {
    // A DNS/socket failure is transient by definition -- surface it as one.
    return { ok: false, status: 0, data: { error: { message: `Network error reaching Meta: ${netErr.message}`, code: ERR_INTERNAL } } };
  }

  let data;
  try { data = await res.json(); }
  catch { data = { error: { message: `Non-JSON response from Meta (HTTP ${res.status})`, code: res.status >= 500 ? ERR_INTERNAL : res.status } }; }

  return { ok: res.ok && !data.error, status: res.status, data };
}

// Sends one payload, absorbing transient failures with exponential backoff.
// Returns { ok, data, error } -- it never throws for a Meta-level error.
async function postWithBackoff(payload, creds, label) {
  let lastError = null;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES; attempt += 1) {
    const { ok, status, data } = await postToMeta(payload, creds);
    if (ok) return { ok: true, data, attempts: attempt + 1 };

    const described = describeMetaError(data, status);
    lastError = described;

    const isTransient = RETRYABLE.has(described.code) || status === 429 || status >= 500;
    if (!isTransient || attempt === MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES) {
      return { ok: false, error: described, attempts: attempt + 1 };
    }
    // 400ms, 800ms, 1600ms + jitter. Well inside a Netlify function budget.
    const backoff = 400 * Math.pow(2, attempt) + Math.floor(Math.random() * 250);
    console.warn(`whatsapp: transient error on ${label} (${described.message}) -- retry ${attempt + 1}/${MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES} in ${backoff}ms`);
    await sleep(backoff);
  }
  return { ok: false, error: lastError, attempts: MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES + 1 };
}

function sendError(message, { terminal = false, code = null } = {}) {
  const e = new Error(message);
  e.terminal = terminal;
  e.metaCode = code;
  e.channel = 'whatsapp';
  return e;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Public API
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Send any approved WhatsApp template via the Meta Cloud API.
 *
 * @param {object}   opts
 * @param {string}   opts.recipientPhone   - E.164 without '+', e.g. '919876543210'
 * @param {string}   opts.templateName     - exact approved name
 * @param {string[]} [opts.bodyVariables]  - ordered {{1}}, {{2}} ... body values
 * @param {string}   [opts.imageUrl]       - public https URL for an IMAGE header
 * @param {string[]} [opts.headerVariables]- values for a TEXT header
 * @param {string}   [opts.urlButtonParam] - suffix for a dynamic URL button
 * @param {string}   [opts.language]       - force a language code
 * @returns {Promise<{messageId:string, waId:string, language:string, templateName:string, usedIntrospection:boolean, attempts:number}>}
 */
async function sendWhatsAppTemplate({
  recipientPhone,
  templateName,
  bodyVariables = [],
  imageUrl,
  headerVariables,
  urlButtonParam,
  language,
}) {
  const token      = process.env.WHATSAPP_TOKEN;
  const phoneNumId = process.env.WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID;

  if (!token)          throw sendError('Missing WHATSAPP_TOKEN env var', { terminal: true });
  if (!phoneNumId)     throw sendError('Missing WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID env var', { terminal: true });
  if (!templateName)   throw sendError('Missing templateName for WhatsApp send', { terminal: true });
  if (!recipientPhone) throw sendError('Missing recipientPhone for WhatsApp send', { terminal: true });

  // Meta wants digits only. A bare 10-digit Indian mobile has no country code
  // and Meta will accept the call but never deliver, so fix it here rather
  // than let it look like a successful send.
  let to = String(recipientPhone).replace(/\D/g, '');
  if (to.length === 10 && /^[6-9]/.test(to)) to = `91${to}`;
  if (to.length === 11 && to.startsWith('0')) to = `91${to.slice(1)}`;
  if (to.length < 11) {
    throw sendError(`Invalid recipient phone for WhatsApp send: "${recipientPhone}" (needs a country code)`, { terminal: true });
  }

  // Meta only fetches header media over public HTTPS.
  const safeImageUrl = imageUrl && /^https:\/\//i.test(imageUrl) ? imageUrl : null;
  const creds = { token, phoneNumId };

  // ── Preferred path: build the payload from the real approved definition ──
  const catalogue = await getTemplateCatalogue();
  if (catalogue) {
    const def = catalogue.get(templateName);

    if (!def) {
      throw sendError(
        `WhatsApp template "${templateName}" does not exist on this WhatsApp Business Account. ` +
        `Available: ${[...catalogue.keys()].sort().join(', ')}`,
        { terminal: true }
      );
    }
    if (def.status !== 'APPROVED') {
      throw sendError(
        `WhatsApp template "${templateName}" is ${def.status}, not APPROVED -- Meta will not deliver it.`,
        { terminal: true }
      );
    }

    const buildPayload = (withImage) => ({
      messaging_product: 'whatsapp',
      recipient_type: 'individual',
      to,
      type: 'template',
      template: {
        name: def.name,
        language: { code: language || def.language },
        components: buildComponentsFromDefinition(def, {
          bodyVariables, imageUrl: withImage ? safeImageUrl : null, headerVariables, urlButtonParam,
        }),
      },
    });

    // If we already learnt this container that Meta cannot fetch our images,
    // do not pay for the failure again on every subsequent send.
    const skipImage = mediaUnreachable.has(templateName);
    let result = await postWithBackoff(buildPayload(!skipImage), creds, `${templateName} -> ${to}`);
    let imageDropped = skipImage;

    // Media fetch failure -> resend immediately without the header image.
    if (!result.ok && !skipImage && safeImageUrl && def.headerFormat === 'IMAGE' && looksLikeMediaError(result.error)) {
      console.warn(
        `whatsapp: Meta could not download the header image for "${templateName}" (${result.error.message}). ` +
        `URL was ${safeImageUrl}. Resending WITHOUT the image so the gift still arrives. ` +
        `FIX: set R2_PUBLIC_URL to your public r2.dev / custom-domain base -- the ` +
        `*.r2.cloudflarestorage.com fallback is the authenticated S3 endpoint and Meta cannot read it.`
      );
      mediaUnreachable.add(templateName);
      imageDropped = true;
      result = await postWithBackoff(buildPayload(false), creds, `${templateName} -> ${to} [no image]`);
    }

    if (result.ok) {
      const msg = result.data.messages && result.data.messages[0];
      const contact = result.data.contacts && result.data.contacts[0];
      return {
        messageId: msg ? msg.id : null,
        waId: contact ? contact.wa_id : to,
        language: language || def.language,
        templateName: def.name,
        usedIntrospection: true,
        attempts: result.attempts,
        imageHeaderSent: !imageDropped && !!safeImageUrl && def.headerFormat === 'IMAGE',
      };
    }

    const { code, message } = result.error;
    // The catalogue can go stale mid-container if you edit a template in
    // WhatsApp Manager. Drop it so the next send re-introspects.
    if (code === ERR_PARAM_COUNT_MISMATCH || code === ERR_TEMPLATE_TRANSLATION_MISSING) {
      templateCatalogue = null;
      templateCataloguePromise = null;
    }
    throw sendError(
      `Meta WhatsApp send failed for "${templateName}" [lang=${language || def.language}, ` +
      `bodyVars=${def.bodyParamCount}, header=${def.headerFormat || 'none'}]: ${message}`,
      { terminal: TERMINAL.has(code), code }
    );
  }

  // ── Fallback path: no introspection available, guess the shape ───────────
  const cachedLang = resolvedLanguage.get(templateName);
  const candidates = languageCandidates(language || cachedLang);
  let lastError = null;
  const triedLanguages = [];

  for (const lang of candidates) {
    const headerModes = headerlessTemplate.has(templateName) || !safeImageUrl ? [false] : [true, false];

    for (const includeHeader of headerModes) {
      const payload = {
        messaging_product: 'whatsapp',
        recipient_type: 'individual',
        to,
        type: 'template',
        template: {
          name: templateName,
          language: { code: lang },
          components: buildComponentsLegacy({ bodyVariables, imageUrl: safeImageUrl, includeHeader }),
        },
      };

      const result = await postWithBackoff(payload, creds, `${templateName} -> ${to} [lang=${lang}]`);

      if (result.ok) {
        resolvedLanguage.set(templateName, lang);
        if (!includeHeader && safeImageUrl) headerlessTemplate.add(templateName);
        const msg = result.data.messages && result.data.messages[0];
        const contact = result.data.contacts && result.data.contacts[0];
        return {
          messageId: msg ? msg.id : null,
          waId: contact ? contact.wa_id : to,
          language: lang,
          templateName,
          usedIntrospection: false,
          attempts: result.attempts,
        };
      }

      const { code, message } = result.error;
      lastError = message;
      if (!triedLanguages.includes(lang)) triedLanguages.push(lang);

      const headerMightBeTheProblem = includeHeader &&
        (code === ERR_PARAM_COUNT_MISMATCH || code === ERR_PARAM_FORMAT_MISMATCH ||
         code === ERR_GENERIC_INVALID_PARAM || looksLikeMediaError(result.error));
      if (headerMightBeTheProblem) {
        console.warn(`whatsapp: "${templateName}" rejected the image header (${message}) -- retrying without it`);
        continue;
      }
      if (code === ERR_TEMPLATE_TRANSLATION_MISSING) {
        console.warn(`whatsapp: "${templateName}" not found in language "${lang}" -- trying next language`);
        break;
      }
      throw sendError(
        `Meta WhatsApp send failed for template "${templateName}" [lang=${lang}]: ${message}`,
        { terminal: TERMINAL.has(code), code }
      );
    }
  }

  throw sendError(
    `Meta WhatsApp send failed for template "${templateName}". Tried languages: ${triedLanguages.join(', ')}. ` +
    `Last error: ${lastError}. Fix: set WHATSAPP_WABA_ID in Netlify env so this helper can read the ` +
    `approved template definition instead of guessing.`,
    { terminal: false }
  );
}

/**
 * Convenience wrapper for ZivoGift's gift delivery message.
 * The message passed in is a TEASER -- it lands on a lock screen, so it must
 * never contain the sender's personal message. See gift-scheduler.js.
 */
async function sendGiftMessage({
  recipientPhone, senderName, personalMessage, occasion, imageUrl,
  templateName, language, giftUrl,
}) {
  const message = personalMessage
    ? personalMessage
    : `Happy ${occasion || 'Birthday'}! Wishing you an incredible day.`;

  const name = templateName || process.env.WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_NAME || 'zivogift_birthday_surprise';

  return sendWhatsAppTemplate({
    recipientPhone,
    templateName: name,
    bodyVariables: [senderName || 'Someone special', message],
    imageUrl,
    language,
    // Only used if the approved template has a dynamic URL button.
    urlButtonParam: giftUrl || undefined,
  });
}

/**
 * Diagnostics helper -- returns the introspected catalogue as a plain array.
 * Used by admin-whatsapp-diagnostics.js. Never throws.
 */
async function describeTemplates() {
  try {
    const cat = await getTemplateCatalogue();
    if (!cat) return { available: false, reason: process.env.WHATSAPP_WABA_ID ? 'introspection failed' : 'WHATSAPP_WABA_ID not set', templates: [] };
    return { available: true, templates: [...cat.values()] };
  } catch (err) {
    return { available: false, reason: err.message, templates: [] };
  }
}

// Test seam: lets unit tests inject a catalogue without hitting the network.
function __setTemplateCatalogueForTests(map) {
  templateCatalogue = map;
  templateCataloguePromise = map ? Promise.resolve(map) : null;
  introspectionFailed = !map;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// CONVERSATION MIRROR
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Every template this helper sends -- gift deliveries, order updates, campaign
// blasts, OTPs -- is also written into the customer's conversation thread
// (wa_messages) so the Customer Messages tab shows the FULL history, not just
// the half the customer typed.
//
// Why this matters operationally: when someone replies "what is this?", the
// answer is on the screen you are already looking at. Without the mirror you
// would be reading one side of a conversation and guessing the other.
//
// WHY IT WRAPS THE EXPORT RATHER THAN EDITING THE FUNCTION
// -------------------------------------------------------
// sendWhatsAppTemplate has three separate success `return` points (the
// introspection path, the legacy-ladder path, and the no-image retry). Adding
// a mirror call at each one would mean three chances to get it wrong and
// three places to keep in sync. Wrapping the single export captures all of
// them exactly once.
//
// SAFETY: the mirror is strictly best-effort and never alters the result or
// the thrown error. A bookkeeping failure must never turn a delivered gift
// into a reported failure -- gift-scheduler treats a throw as a delivery
// failure and would fire the email fallback for a message that actually
// arrived. So both branches below re-throw / return the original outcome
// untouched.
//
// Lazily required inside the function: _lib/waInbox.js pulls in the Supabase
// client, and a top-level require would make every consumer of this helper
// pay that cost even when only reading the template catalogue.
async function mirrorOutbound(entry) {
  try {
    const { recordOutbound } = require('./waInbox');
    await recordOutbound(null, entry);
  } catch (e) {
    console.warn('whatsapp: conversation mirror skipped:', (e && e.message) || e);
  }
}

async function sendWhatsAppTemplateMirrored(opts) {
  const o = opts || {};
  try {
    const result = await sendWhatsAppTemplateCore(o);
    await mirrorOutbound({
      phone: o.recipientPhone,
      waMessageId: result && result.messageId,
      msgType: 'template',
      // The stored body is the template name plus its variables. The fully
      // rendered text lives only on Meta's side, and reconstructing it here
      // would drift from the approved copy the moment a template is edited.
      body: [o.templateName, ...(Array.isArray(o.bodyVariables) ? o.bodyVariables : [])]
        .filter(Boolean).join(' · '),
      templateName: (result && result.templateName) || o.templateName,
      status: 'sent',
      source: 'automation',
      // Deliberately does NOT clear the unread badge: an automated gift
      // notification going out is not you reading the customer's question.
      markRead: false,
    });
    return result;
  } catch (err) {
    // Record the failed attempt too. A template that Meta rejected is exactly
    // the thing you want to see in the thread when the customer says they
    // never received anything.
    await mirrorOutbound({
      phone: o.recipientPhone,
      waMessageId: null,
      msgType: 'template',
      body: o.templateName,
      templateName: o.templateName,
      status: 'failed',
      source: 'automation',
      errorCode: err && err.metaCode ? String(err.metaCode) : null,
      errorMessage: String((err && err.message) || err),
      markRead: false,
    });
    throw err;
  }
}

// ── REBIND, DO NOT JUST RE-EXPORT ───────────────────────────────────────────
// Capture the original implementation first...
const sendWhatsAppTemplateCore = sendWhatsAppTemplate;

// ...then point the in-module name at the mirrored wrapper.
//
// This line is load-bearing. sendGiftMessage() calls sendWhatsAppTemplate()
// BY NAME, internally. If we only swapped the export, every gift delivery --
// the highest-volume outbound message the site sends -- would bypass the
// mirror and never appear in the customer's thread, while campaign sends
// (which call the export directly) would. The result would be a thread that
// is silently missing exactly the messages you most need to see.
//
// Reassigning the function binding fixes that for ALL internal callers at
// once, present and future. No recursion: the wrapper invokes
// sendWhatsAppTemplateCore, which was captured above before the reassignment.
sendWhatsAppTemplate = sendWhatsAppTemplateMirrored;

module.exports = {
  sendWhatsAppTemplate: sendWhatsAppTemplateMirrored,
  sendGiftMessage,
  sanitizeBodyVariable,
  describeTemplates,
  // The unmirrored original, for diagnostics and tests that must not write
  // rows into a live conversation.
  sendWhatsAppTemplateRaw: sendWhatsAppTemplateCore,
  // exported for tests
  countPositionalParams,
  parseTemplateDefinition,
  reconcileBodyVariables,
  buildComponentsFromDefinition,
  __setTemplateCatalogueForTests,
};

// netlify/functions/_lib/whatsappSession.js
//
// FREE-TEXT ("session") WhatsApp messaging + inbound media retrieval.
//
// WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM _lib/whatsapp.js
// ------------------------------------------
// _lib/whatsapp.js sends TEMPLATES: business-initiated, pre-approved, billable,
// and shaped by Meta's template introspection. This file sends FREE TEXT,
// which is a different Meta capability with different rules:
//
//   • Permitted ONLY inside the 24-hour customer service window, i.e. within
//     24h of the customer's last inbound message.
//   • Not billable as a template (it is part of the service conversation).
//   • No approval, no components, no variable reconciliation.
//
// Before this file existed, the two free-text replies in whatsapp-webhook.js
// were raw inline fetch() calls with no retry, no error classification and no
// record of whether they worked. Those are now routed through here.
//
// ENV: WHATSAPP_TOKEN, WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID

const GRAPH_API_VERSION = 'v20.0';

// Meta's hard cap on a text message body.
const MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 4096;

// Refuse to pull anything larger than this out of Meta into R2. A 90MB video
// would blow the Netlify function memory/time budget and is not something the
// admin panel can usefully display inline anyway.
const MAX_MEDIA_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024;

// Transient Meta error codes worth one retry. Mirrors the classification in
// _lib/whatsapp.js rather than inventing a second, divergent list.
const RETRYABLE_CODES = new Set([1, 2, 4, 80007, 130429, 131048, 131056]);

function creds() {
  const token = process.env.WHATSAPP_TOKEN;
  const phoneNumId = process.env.WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID;
  if (!token) throw new Error('Missing WHATSAPP_TOKEN env var');
  if (!phoneNumId) throw new Error('Missing WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID env var');
  return { token, phoneNumId };
}

function normalizeTo(raw) {
  let to = String(raw || '').replace(/\D/g, '');
  if (to.length === 10 && /^[6-9]/.test(to)) to = `91${to}`;
  if (to.length === 11 && to.startsWith('0')) to = `91${to.slice(1)}`;
  return to.length >= 11 ? to : null;
}

function sleep(ms) { return new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)); }

function describeError(data, status) {
  const err = (data && data.error) || {};
  const detail = (err.error_data && err.error_data.details) || err.message || `HTTP ${status}`;
  return { code: err.code || status, message: detail, subcode: err.error_subcode || null };
}

/**
 * POSTs to the Cloud API messages endpoint with one retry on transient errors.
 * Returns { ok, messageId, error } and never throws for a Meta-level error —
 * callers need to record the failed attempt in the thread rather than lose it.
 */
async function postMessage(payload) {
  const { token, phoneNumId } = creds();
  const url = `https://graph.facebook.com/${GRAPH_API_VERSION}/${phoneNumId}/messages`;

  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt += 1) {
    let res, data;
    try {
      res = await fetch(url, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify(payload),
      });
      data = await res.json().catch(() => ({}));
    } catch (netErr) {
      if (attempt === 0) { await sleep(500); continue; }
      return { ok: false, error: { code: 0, message: `Network error reaching Meta: ${netErr.message}` } };
    }

    if (res.ok && !data.error) {
      const msg = data.messages && data.messages[0];
      return { ok: true, messageId: msg ? msg.id : null, raw: data };
    }

    const described = describeError(data, res.status);
    const transient = RETRYABLE_CODES.has(described.code) || res.status === 429 || res.status >= 500;
    if (transient && attempt === 0) {
      await sleep(600);
      continue;
    }
    return { ok: false, error: described, raw: data };
  }
  return { ok: false, error: { code: 0, message: 'unreachable' } };
}

/**
 * Sends a free-text WhatsApp message.
 *
 * ONLY valid inside the 24h window. Outside it Meta returns error 131047
 * ("Message failed to send because more than 24 hours have passed since the
 * customer last replied"), which is surfaced verbatim with
 * `windowExpired: true` so the UI can offer a template instead of showing a
 * meaningless error.
 *
 * @returns {Promise<{ok:boolean, messageId?:string, error?:object, windowExpired?:boolean}>}
 */
async function sendWhatsAppText({ to, text, previewUrl = false, contextMessageId }) {
  const recipient = normalizeTo(to);
  if (!recipient) return { ok: false, error: { code: 0, message: `Invalid recipient phone "${to}"` } };

  const body = String(text || '').trim();
  if (!body) return { ok: false, error: { code: 0, message: 'Message text is empty' } };

  const payload = {
    messaging_product: 'whatsapp',
    recipient_type: 'individual',
    to: recipient,
    type: 'text',
    text: { body: body.slice(0, MAX_TEXT_LENGTH), preview_url: !!previewUrl },
  };
  // Quoting the customer's message makes a reply unambiguous on their screen
  // when several conversations are in flight.
  if (contextMessageId) payload.context = { message_id: contextMessageId };

  const res = await postMessage(payload);
  if (!res.ok && res.error && (res.error.code === 131047 || res.error.code === 131051)) {
    return { ...res, windowExpired: true };
  }
  return res;
}

/**
 * Sends a media message by public HTTPS link (image/document).
 * Used for sending a quote PDF or a product photo back to a customer.
 */
async function sendWhatsAppMedia({ to, link, type = 'image', caption, filename }) {
  const recipient = normalizeTo(to);
  if (!recipient) return { ok: false, error: { code: 0, message: `Invalid recipient phone "${to}"` } };
  if (!/^https:\/\//i.test(link || '')) {
    return { ok: false, error: { code: 0, message: 'Media link must be a public https URL' } };
  }

  const media = { link };
  if (caption && (type === 'image' || type === 'video' || type === 'document')) media.caption = caption;
  if (filename && type === 'document') media.filename = filename;

  const res = await postMessage({
    messaging_product: 'whatsapp',
    recipient_type: 'individual',
    to: recipient,
    type,
    [type]: media,
  });
  if (!res.ok && res.error && (res.error.code === 131047 || res.error.code === 131051)) {
    return { ...res, windowExpired: true };
  }
  return res;
}

/**
 * Downloads an inbound media item from Meta.
 *
 * TWO STEPS, and both need the bearer token:
 *   1. GET /{media_id}          -> a short-lived, authenticated download URL
 *   2. GET that url             -> the bytes
 *
 * The step-1 URL expires in about five minutes, which is precisely why the
 * webhook stores only the media_id and this runs later, on demand, when an
 * admin actually opens the conversation.
 *
 * @returns {Promise<{ok:boolean, buffer?:Buffer, mime?:string, size?:number, error?:string}>}
 */
async function fetchInboundMedia(mediaId) {
  if (!mediaId) return { ok: false, error: 'No media id' };
  let token;
  try { ({ token } = creds()); } catch (e) { return { ok: false, error: e.message }; }

  try {
    const metaRes = await fetch(`https://graph.facebook.com/${GRAPH_API_VERSION}/${mediaId}`, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
    });
    const meta = await metaRes.json().catch(() => ({}));
    if (!metaRes.ok || !meta.url) {
      const d = describeError(meta, metaRes.status);
      return { ok: false, error: `Could not resolve media ${mediaId}: ${d.message}` };
    }

    // Guard before downloading, not after — the whole point is to avoid
    // pulling a huge file into a 10s function.
    const declared = Number(meta.file_size || 0);
    if (declared && declared > MAX_MEDIA_BYTES) {
      return { ok: false, error: `Media is ${Math.round(declared / 1048576)}MB, over the ${MAX_MEDIA_BYTES / 1048576}MB limit` };
    }

    // The CDN URL also requires the token — a plain fetch returns 401.
    const binRes = await fetch(meta.url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
    if (!binRes.ok) return { ok: false, error: `Media download failed (HTTP ${binRes.status})` };

    const buffer = Buffer.from(await binRes.arrayBuffer());
    if (buffer.length > MAX_MEDIA_BYTES) {
      return { ok: false, error: `Media is ${Math.round(buffer.length / 1048576)}MB, over the limit` };
    }

    return {
      ok: true,
      buffer,
      mime: meta.mime_type || binRes.headers.get('content-type') || 'application/octet-stream',
      size: buffer.length,
      sha256: meta.sha256 || null,
    };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, error: String((e && e.message) || e) };
  }
}

/** Marks an inbound message as read (blue ticks on the customer's phone). */
async function markMessageRead(waMessageId) {
  if (!waMessageId) return { ok: false };
  try {
    const { token, phoneNumId } = creds();
    const res = await fetch(`https://graph.facebook.com/${GRAPH_API_VERSION}/${phoneNumId}/messages`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ messaging_product: 'whatsapp', status: 'read', message_id: waMessageId }),
    });
    return { ok: res.ok };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, error: String((e && e.message) || e) };
  }
}

module.exports = {
  GRAPH_API_VERSION,
  MAX_TEXT_LENGTH,
  MAX_MEDIA_BYTES,
  normalizeTo,
  sendWhatsAppText,
  sendWhatsAppMedia,
  fetchInboundMedia,
  markMessageRead,
};

#!/usr/bin/env node
/* scripts/fetch-fonts.js
 *
 * Downloads the TTFs that netlify/fonts/fonts.conf expects.
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS
 * The Netlify Functions Lambda image ships no fonts, so librsvg (inside Sharp)
 * rasterizes every <text> element to nothing — that is the "card PNG renders
 * without text" bug. netlify/fonts/ is the fix.
 *
 * HOW IT RESOLVES URLS
 * It asks the Google Fonts CSS v1 API for each family and parses the .ttf URLs
 * out of the @font-face blocks it returns.
 *
 * The previous version of this script hardcoded raw.githubusercontent.com
 * paths into the google/fonts repo. Every one of them 404'd: that repo names
 * variable fonts "FamilyName[axis1,axis2].ttf" and reorganises families
 * between static/ and variable layouts over time, so any hardcoded path is a
 * guess with a shelf life. The CSS API is a stable, documented contract that
 * hands back a working URL for whatever the current layout happens to be.
 *
 * The User-Agent matters. Google serves woff2 to modern browsers and TTF to
 * older/unknown ones. librsvg + fontconfig want TTF, so we send a plain UA.
 *
 * RUN IT TWO WAYS — pick one:
 *
 *   A. Commit the fonts (RECOMMENDED)
 *        node scripts/fetch-fonts.js
 *        git add netlify/fonts/*.ttf && git commit
 *      The build then never touches the network and can never deploy fontless.
 *
 *   B. Fetch at build time
 *      package.json runs this from `postinstall`, and netlify.toml's build
 *      command is `npm install`, so a clean Netlify build populates the
 *      directory before functions are bundled.
 *
 *   C. If BOTH are blocked (corporate proxy, air-gapped machine)
 *      See the manual instructions this script prints on failure. Any TTF with
 *      the right family name works — the filenames below are just convention.
 *
 * Idempotent: files already present are skipped, so postinstall on a populated
 * checkout costs nothing.
 *
 * All five families are SIL Open Font License 1.1 — free to bundle and
 * redistribute in a commercial product.
 */

'use strict';

const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const FONT_DIR = path.join(__dirname, '..', 'netlify', 'fonts');

// Old-style UA so the API returns format('truetype') rather than woff2.
const TTF_UA = 'Mozilla/5.0';
const CSS_API = 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css';

// `family` must match the family name embedded in the TTF, because
// netlify/fonts/fonts.conf aliases the generic CSS families onto these exact
// strings. `weights` picks which faces to pull: regular for body copy, 700
// where the layouts use font-weight:700/800.
const FONTS = [
  { file: 'Inter-Regular.ttf',           family: 'Inter',            weights: '400' },
  { file: 'Inter-Bold.ttf',              family: 'Inter',            weights: '700' },
  { file: 'PlayfairDisplay-Regular.ttf', family: 'Playfair Display', weights: '400' },
  { file: 'PlayfairDisplay-Bold.ttf',    family: 'Playfair Display', weights: '700' },
  { file: 'JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf',   family: 'JetBrains Mono',   weights: '400' },
  { file: 'Caveat-Regular.ttf',          family: 'Caveat',           weights: '400' },
  { file: 'BebasNeue-Regular.ttf',       family: 'Bebas Neue',       weights: '400' },
];

const OFL_NOTICE = `These fonts are licensed under the SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1.

  Inter             — Copyright (c) The Inter Project Authors
  Playfair Display  — Copyright (c) The Playfair Display Project Authors
  JetBrains Mono    — Copyright (c) The JetBrains Mono Project Authors
  Caveat            — Copyright (c) The Caveat Project Authors
  Bebas Neue        — Copyright (c) The Bebas Neue Project Authors

Full licence text: https://openfontlicense.org

They are bundled here so that server-side card rendering (Sharp/librsvg) has
fonts available on the Netlify Functions runtime, which ships none. See
netlify/functions/_lib/cardFonts.js.
`;

/** Asks the CSS API for a family and returns the first .ttf URL it advertises. */
async function resolveTtfUrl(family, weights) {
  const url = `${CSS_API}?family=${encodeURIComponent(family)}:${weights}`;
  const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { 'User-Agent': TTF_UA } });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`CSS API ${res.status} for "${family}"`);

  const css = await res.text();
  const match = css.match(/url\((https:\/\/fonts\.gstatic\.com\/[^)]+\.ttf)\)/);
  if (!match) {
    throw new Error(
      `no .ttf in CSS for "${family}" — the API returned woff2, which librsvg cannot use`
    );
  }
  return match[1];
}

async function download(url, dest) {
  const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { 'User-Agent': TTF_UA }, redirect: 'follow' });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${res.status} ${res.statusText}`);
  const buf = Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer());

  // Verify the magic number. A proxy login page or an error page is still a
  // 200 on some corporate networks, and a bogus "font" would fail silently at
  // render time — which is the whole class of bug this directory exists to
  // prevent.
  const magic = buf.readUInt32BE(0);
  const OK = [0x00010000, 0x74727565 /* 'true' */, 0x4f54544f /* 'OTTO' */];
  if (!OK.includes(magic)) {
    throw new Error(`not a TTF/OTF (magic=0x${magic.toString(16)}, ${buf.length} bytes)`);
  }

  fs.writeFileSync(dest, buf);
  return buf.length;
}

function manualInstructions() {
  return `
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 MANUAL FALLBACK — do this if the download is blocked
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Your network may be blocking fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com.
 That is common on a corporate laptop behind a TLS-inspecting proxy.

 1. On any machine with open internet, download these families:
       https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Inter
       https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Playfair+Display
       https://fonts.google.com/specimen/JetBrains+Mono
       https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Caveat
       https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Bebas+Neue
    (each page has a "Get font" → "Download all" button)

 2. Unzip and copy the .ttf files into:
       ${FONT_DIR}

 3. Filenames do not matter — fontconfig reads the family name from
    inside the file. Static or variable both work.

 4. Verify:
       npm run verify:cards

 5. Commit them so no deploy ever depends on the network:
       git add netlify/fonts/*.ttf
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────`;
}

async function main() {
  fs.mkdirSync(FONT_DIR, { recursive: true });

  let fetched = 0;
  let skipped = 0;
  const failures = [];

  for (const font of FONTS) {
    const dest = path.join(FONT_DIR, font.file);
    if (fs.existsSync(dest) && fs.statSync(dest).size > 1024) {
      skipped++;
      continue;
    }
    try {
      const url = await resolveTtfUrl(font.family, font.weights);
      const bytes = await download(url, dest);
      console.log(`fetch-fonts: ${font.file.padEnd(30)} ${(bytes / 1024).toFixed(0).padStart(4)} KB  (${font.family} ${font.weights})`);
      fetched++;
    } catch (err) {
      failures.push(`${font.file} [${font.family}]: ${err.message}`);
    }
  }

  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(FONT_DIR, 'OFL.txt'), OFL_NOTICE);

  // What actually matters is whether the directory has usable fonts now —
  // not whether every individual download succeeded.
  const present = fs.readdirSync(FONT_DIR).filter((f) => /\.(ttf|otf|ttc)$/i.test(f));

  console.log(`\nfetch-fonts: ${fetched} downloaded, ${skipped} already present`);
  console.log(`fetch-fonts: ${present.length} font file(s) in ${FONT_DIR}`);

  if (failures.length) {
    console.error('\nfetch-fonts: FAILURES:\n  ' + failures.join('\n  '));
  }

  if (present.length === 0) {
    console.error('\nfetch-fonts: NO FONTS AVAILABLE — card rendering will refuse to run.');
    console.error(manualInstructions());
  } else if (failures.length) {
    console.warn('\nfetch-fonts: some families are missing; cards will render but may fall back to Inter.');
    console.warn('Run `npm run verify:cards` to confirm text still rasterizes.');
  } else {
    console.log('fetch-fonts: all good. Next: npm run verify:cards\n');
  }

  // Deliberately never exits non-zero. This runs from `postinstall`, and
  // failing the install would block a deploy that is otherwise fine.
  // _lib/cardFonts.js refuses to render blank cards at runtime instead —
  // loud warning here, hard stop there.
}

main().catch((err) => {
  console.error('fetch-fonts: unexpected error:', err.message);
  console.error(manualInstructions());
});

/* scripts/verify-campaigns.js
 *
 * Offline verification for the Campaign Center / Emergency Console /
 * Export Center / Festival Automation build.
 *
 * Run:  node scripts/verify-campaigns.js
 *
 * Tests ONLY what can be tested without live services: pure logic, token
 * signing, audience filtering, CSV encoding, email rendering, and the
 * PostgREST query chains (via a recording fake client).
 *
 * It explicitly does NOT test Resend delivery, Meta delivery, or the real
 * Supabase schema -- those require your live credentials.

process.env.UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET = 'test-secret-for-verification-only';
process.env.SITE_URL = 'https://zivogift.com';

const assert = require('assert');

let pass = 0, fail = 0;
function test(name, fn) {
  try { fn(); console.log(`  ✓ ${name}`); pass++; }
  catch (e) { console.log(`  ✗ ${name}\n      ${e.message}`); fail++; }
}
async function atest(name, fn) {
  try { await fn(); console.log(`  ✓ ${name}`); pass++; }
  catch (e) { console.log(`  ✗ ${name}\n      ${e.message}`); fail++; }
}
function section(s) { console.log(`\n${s}`); }

// ── A fake PostgREST client that records the query chain ───────────────────
// Enough fidelity to prove the filter chains are built correctly without a
// database. Every builder method returns `this` and records itself.
function fakeClient(tableData) {
  return {
    from(table) {
      const q = {
        _table: table, _calls: [], _range: null,
        select(cols, opts) { this._calls.push(['select', cols, opts]); return this; },
        eq(c, v) { this._calls.push(['eq', c, v]); return this; },
        neq(c, v) { this._calls.push(['neq', c, v]); return this; },
        gt(c, v) { this._calls.push(['gt', c, v]); return this; },
        gte(c, v) { this._calls.push(['gte', c, v]); return this; },
        lt(c, v) { this._calls.push(['lt', c, v]); return this; },
        is(c, v) { this._calls.push(['is', c, v]); return this; },
        or(s) { this._calls.push(['or', s]); return this; },
        in(c, v) { this._calls.push(['in', c, v]); return this; },
        limit(n) { this._calls.push(['limit', n]); return this; },
        order(c, o) { this._calls.push(['order', c, o]); return this; },
        range(a, b) { this._range = [a, b]; this._calls.push(['range', a, b]); return this; },
        update(p) { this._calls.push(['update', p]); return this; },
        insert(p) { this._calls.push(['insert', p]); return this; },
        upsert(p, o) { this._calls.push(['upsert', p, o]); return this; },
        delete() { this._calls.push(['delete']); return this; },
        single() { this._calls.push(['single']); return this; },
        then(res) {
          const rows = (tableData[table] || []);
          // Emulate PostgREST paging so the paging loop is genuinely exercised.
          const out = this._range ? rows.slice(this._range[0], this._range[1] + 1) : rows;
          return Promise.resolve({ data: out, error: null, count: rows.length }).then(res);
        },
      };
      return q;
    },
  };
}

section('1. Unsubscribe token (HMAC signing)');
const { makeToken, readToken, unsubUrl } = require('../netlify/functions/_lib/unsubToken');

test('round-trips an email and phone', () => {
  const t = makeToken({ email: 'Aisha@Example.com', phone10: '9876543210', campaignId: 'abc-123' });
  const r = readToken(t);
  assert.strictEqual(r.valid, true, 'token should verify');
  assert.strictEqual(r.email, 'aisha@example.com', 'email should be lowercased');
  assert.strictEqual(r.phone10, '9876543210');
  assert.strictEqual(r.campaignId, 'abc-123');
});

test('rejects a tampered token', () => {
  const t = makeToken({ email: 'a@b.com' });
  const raw = Buffer.from(t.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/'), 'base64').toString('utf8');
  const evil = raw.replace('a@b.com', 'victim@b.com');
  const forged = Buffer.from(evil).toString('base64').replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, '');
  const r = readToken(forged);
  assert.strictEqual(r.valid, false, 'a forged token MUST NOT verify');
  assert.strictEqual(r.reason, 'bad_signature');
});

test('rejects garbage', () => {
  assert.strictEqual(readToken('not-a-token').valid, false);
  assert.strictEqual(readToken('').valid, false);

const CUSTOMERS = [
  { customer_key: 'a@b.com', email: 'a@b.com', phone10: '9876543210', full_name: 'Aisha Khan', paid_orders_count: 2, lifetime_value: 1500, last_order_at: '2026-09-01', opted_out: false },
