-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SOURCE: schema-fix-digital-sends-email.sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- ============================================================================
-- ZIVOGIFT — Fix: digital_sends has no recipient_email column
-- Run in Supabase: Dashboard → SQL Editor → New query → paste → Run
-- Safe to re-run.
--
-- ROOT CAUSE of "digital gifts not delivering by email or WhatsApp":
-- public.digital_sends was created with `recipient_phone text not null`
-- and a comment marking email as "(future)" — that future migration never
-- happened. _lib/digitalSendsHelper.js inserts email-channel rows as
-- { recipient_email: '...', channel: 'email' }, but digital_sends has no
-- recipient_email column at all, and recipient_phone is NOT NULL and gets
-- left out of that row. Every insert containing an email-channel row is
-- rejected by Postgres outright — and because scheduleDigitalSendsForOrder
-- inserts all of an order's send rows in a single batch, a single email
-- item in an order poisons the whole insert, silently dropping the
-- WhatsApp-channel rows from the SAME order too. The function only
-- console.error()s the failure and returns, so nothing in the UI or the
-- order ever surfaces it — it just looks like delivery "didn't happen".
-- ============================================================================

DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='digital_sends' AND column_name='recipient_email') THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends ADD COLUMN recipient_email text;
  END IF;
END $$;

-- recipient_phone can no longer be NOT NULL — an email-channel row
-- legitimately has no phone number.
ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends ALTER COLUMN recipient_phone DROP NOT NULL;

-- Guardrail: every row must have an address that actually matches its
-- channel, so a malformed insert fails loudly (a clear Postgres constraint
-- error in the logs) instead of silently sending to nobody.
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.table_constraints
    WHERE table_name = 'digital_sends' AND constraint_name = 'digital_sends_channel_address_chk'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends
      ADD CONSTRAINT digital_sends_channel_address_chk
      CHECK (
        (channel = 'whatsapp' AND recipient_phone IS NOT NULL)
        OR (channel = 'email' AND recipient_email IS NOT NULL)
      );
  END IF;
END $$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SOURCE: schema-fix-track-order-leak.sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- ============================================================================
-- ZIVOGIFT — Fix track_order() leaking sender_phone/sender_name
-- Run in Supabase: Dashboard → SQL Editor → New query → paste → Run.
-- ============================================================================
--
-- WHY: schema.sql already revoked direct anon SELECT on public.digital_sends
-- specifically because sender_phone/sender_name must never be readable via
-- the public anon key (see the "SECURITY:" comment block in schema.sql).
-- But track_order() is SECURITY DEFINER — it runs as the function owner and
-- bypasses RLS entirely — and its second version (added when digital_sends
-- was folded into the response) does `jsonb_agg(ds)`, i.e. every column,
-- including sender_phone and sender_name. That's the exact same leak the
-- direct-SELECT fix was meant to close, reopened through a different path,
-- and it's reachable by anyone with an order_number + the phone used at
-- checkout — both are guessable/knowable by someone other than the buyer
-- in some flows (e.g. a recipient who receives the order_number).
--
-- FIX: return an explicit allowlist of digital_sends columns instead of the
-- whole row. Nothing in this function's actual purpose (letting the buyer
-- see their own gift's delivery status) needs sender_phone, sender_name, or
-- the internal reply_token/provider_message_id fields.

create or replace function public.track_order(p_order_number text, p_phone text)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql security definer set search_path = public as $$
declare
  v_order public.orders%rowtype;
  v_items jsonb;
  v_history jsonb;
  v_digital_sends jsonb;
begin
  select * into v_order from public.orders
    where order_number = p_order_number and contact_phone = p_phone;
  if not found then return null; end if;

  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(oi), '[]'::jsonb) into v_items
    from public.order_items oi where oi.order_id = v_order.id;

  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(h order by h.changed_at), '[]'::jsonb) into v_history
    from public.order_status_history h where h.order_id = v_order.id;

  -- Explicit allowlist — deliberately excludes sender_phone, sender_name,
  -- reply_token, and provider_message_id.
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
    'id', ds.id,
    'recipient_name', ds.recipient_name,
    'occasion', ds.occasion,
    'card_image_url', ds.card_image_url,
    'channel', ds.channel,
    'scheduled_at', ds.scheduled_at,
    'sent_at', ds.sent_at,
    'status', ds.status,
    'gift_type', ds.gift_type,
    'media_type', ds.media_type,
    'opened_at', ds.opened_at
  ) order by ds.scheduled_at), '[]'::jsonb) into v_digital_sends
    from public.digital_sends ds where ds.order_id = v_order.id;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'order', to_jsonb(v_order),
    'items', v_items,
    'history', v_history,
    'digital_sends', v_digital_sends
  );
end;
$$;

-- Grant is idempotent — CREATE OR REPLACE keeps prior grants, but stating it
-- explicitly here means this file is a complete, standalone fix on its own.
grant execute on function public.track_order(text, text) to anon, authenticated;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SOURCE: schema-admin-order-delete.sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- ============================================================================
-- ZIVOGIFT — Admin: allow deleting orders from the admin dashboard
-- Run in Supabase: Dashboard → SQL Editor → New query → paste → Run.
-- Safe to re-run (DROP POLICY IF EXISTS guard).
-- ============================================================================
--
-- WHY THIS IS NEEDED
-- ------------------
-- schema.sql enables RLS on public.orders and defines exactly two policies:
--   orders_owner_select  (SELECT)
--   orders_admin_update  (UPDATE)
-- There is deliberately NO INSERT policy (orders are created only by the
-- create-cashfree-order Netlify function via the service-role key), and there
-- was NO DELETE policy at all.
--
-- With RLS on and no DELETE policy, a browser DELETE through the anon key
-- (which is what /admin.html uses) matches zero rows and returns SUCCESS with
-- an empty result — a silent no-op. The admin "Delete selected" button would
-- therefore appear to work while deleting nothing.
--
-- This adds a DELETE policy that mirrors the existing orders_admin_update
-- policy exactly: only a logged-in admin (public.is_admin() → profiles.is_admin
-- for auth.uid()) may delete. A random anon visitor is not an admin, so this
-- does not widen public access.
--
-- CHILD ROWS ARE HANDLED BY THE DATABASE, NOT THE BROWSER
-- -------------------------------------------------------
-- Every foreign key pointing at orders(id) already specifies its own delete
-- behaviour, so one DELETE on orders cleans everything up and can never be
-- blocked by a foreign key:
--   order_items.order_id          ON DELETE CASCADE
--   order_status_history.order_id ON DELETE CASCADE
--   digital_sends.order_id        ON DELETE CASCADE
--        └─ reply_tokens.gift_id        ON DELETE CASCADE
--        └─ gift_reactions.gift_id      ON DELETE CASCADE
--        └─ share_clip_jobs.digital_send_id ON DELETE CASCADE
--   care_package_orders.order_id  ON DELETE SET NULL
--   subscriptions.order_id        ON DELETE SET NULL   (a paid Zivo Pass is
--                                                        kept alive on purpose)
-- FK cascade actions run at the system level and are NOT filtered by the child
-- tables' own RLS policies, so no extra per-child DELETE policy is required.
-- ============================================================================

drop policy if exists "orders_admin_delete" on public.orders;
create policy "orders_admin_delete" on public.orders for delete
  using (public.is_admin());

-- Optional: make PostgREST pick the change up immediately instead of waiting
-- for its periodic schema refresh.
NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SOURCE: 02_functions.sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- ============================================================================
-- ZIVOGIFT · 02_functions.sql  —  ALL RPC functions for Runs 1–2 (consolidated)
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Run this SECOND (after 01_columns.sql). Idempotent (CREATE OR REPLACE).
-- Contains:
--   • zg_phone_last10()  helper (tolerant phone matching)
--   • get_my_memories()  — Run 1 Memory Vault (sent + received, redacted)
--   • record_gift_open() — Run 2 atomic open/complete analytics recorder
-- ============================================================================

-- ── helper: last 10 digits of any phone string ──────────────────────────────
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.zg_phone_last10(p text)
RETURNS text LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$
  SELECT right(regexp_replace(coalesce(p,''), '\D', '', 'g'), 10);
$$;

-- ── Run 1: Memory Vault ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Returns the caller's SENT (orders.user_id = auth.uid()) and RECEIVED
-- (digital_sends.recipient_phone last-10 matches the caller's profile phone)
-- gifts. SECURITY DEFINER but every query is scoped to auth.uid(). Never
-- returns phone numbers; redacts sender_name for the anonymous character_drop.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.get_my_memories()
RETURNS jsonb LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$
DECLARE
  v_uid uuid := auth.uid();
  v_phone text;
  v_sent jsonb;
  v_received jsonb;
BEGIN
  IF v_uid IS NULL THEN
    RETURN jsonb_build_object('error', 'not_authenticated');
  END IF;

  SELECT public.zg_phone_last10(phone) INTO v_phone FROM public.profiles WHERE id = v_uid;

  SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(row ORDER BY row->>'created_at' DESC), '[]'::jsonb) INTO v_sent
  FROM (
    SELECT jsonb_build_object(
      'id', ds.id, 'direction', 'sent',
      'recipient_name', ds.recipient_name, 'occasion', ds.occasion, 'gift_type', ds.gift_type,
      'channel', ds.channel, 'card_image_url', ds.card_image_url, 'teaser_image_url', ds.teaser_image_url,
      'gift_url', ds.gift_url, 'status', ds.status, 'scheduled_at', ds.scheduled_at,
      'sent_at', ds.sent_at, 'opened_at', ds.opened_at, 'reveal_completed_at', ds.reveal_completed_at,
      'reaction', ds.reaction, 'reacted_at', ds.reacted_at, 'is_time_capsule', ds.is_time_capsule,
      'order_number', o.order_number, 'created_at', ds.created_at,
      'open_delay_seconds', CASE WHEN ds.opened_at IS NOT NULL AND ds.sent_at IS NOT NULL
                                 THEN extract(epoch FROM (ds.opened_at - ds.sent_at))::int END,
      'reaction_count', (SELECT count(*) FROM public.gift_reactions gr WHERE gr.gift_id = ds.id AND gr.submitted_at IS NOT NULL)
    ) AS row
    FROM public.digital_sends ds
    JOIN public.orders o ON o.id = ds.order_id
    WHERE o.user_id = v_uid
  ) s;

  SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(row ORDER BY row->>'sort_at' DESC), '[]'::jsonb) INTO v_received
  FROM (
    SELECT jsonb_build_object(
      'id', ds.id, 'direction', 'received',
      'sender_name', CASE WHEN ds.gift_type = 'character_drop' THEN NULL ELSE ds.sender_name END,
      'occasion', ds.occasion, 'gift_type', ds.gift_type, 'channel', ds.channel,
      'card_image_url', ds.card_image_url, 'gift_url', ds.gift_url, 'status', ds.status,
      'sent_at', ds.sent_at, 'opened_at', ds.opened_at, 'is_time_capsule', ds.is_time_capsule,
      'sort_at', coalesce(ds.sent_at, ds.scheduled_at, ds.created_at)
    ) AS row
    FROM public.digital_sends ds
    WHERE v_phone IS NOT NULL AND length(v_phone) = 10
      AND public.zg_phone_last10(ds.recipient_phone) = v_phone
      AND ds.status = 'sent'
  ) r;

  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'sent', v_sent, 'received', v_received,
    'sent_count', jsonb_array_length(v_sent), 'received_count', jsonb_array_length(v_received)
  );
END;
$$;

REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.get_my_memories() FROM anon;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.get_my_memories() TO authenticated;

-- ── Run 2: atomic open/complete recorder ────────────────────────────────────
-- mark-gift-opened.js calls this instead of a read-modify-write, so two rapid
-- taps can't race or double-count. SECURITY DEFINER because the recipient is
-- anonymous; the gift_id in the URL is the capability (as get-gift.js treats it).
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.record_gift_open(
  p_gift_id uuid, p_stage text, p_mode text DEFAULT NULL
) RETURNS jsonb LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$
DECLARE r public.digital_sends%ROWTYPE;
BEGIN
  SELECT * INTO r FROM public.digital_sends WHERE id = p_gift_id;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN RETURN jsonb_build_object('ok', false, 'error', 'not_found'); END IF;

  IF p_stage = 'opened' THEN
    UPDATE public.digital_sends
       SET view_count = view_count + 1,
           opened_at  = COALESCE(opened_at, now()),
           first_open_delay_seconds = COALESCE(first_open_delay_seconds,
             CASE WHEN sent_at IS NOT NULL THEN GREATEST(0, extract(epoch FROM (now() - sent_at))::int) END)
     WHERE id = p_gift_id;
  ELSIF p_stage = 'completed' THEN
    UPDATE public.digital_sends
       SET reveal_completed_at = COALESCE(reveal_completed_at, now()),
           reveal_mode         = COALESCE(reveal_mode, p_mode)
     WHERE id = p_gift_id;
  END IF;

  RETURN jsonb_build_object('ok', true);
END;
$$;

REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.record_gift_open(uuid, text, text) FROM public;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.record_gift_open(uuid, text, text) TO anon, authenticated, service_role;

NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';

FILE: supabase\consolidated\50_whatsapp_delivery.sql

-- =====================================================================
-- ZIVOGIFT consolidated migration: 50_whatsapp_delivery.sql
--
-- Run order for a FRESH database: 10 -> 20 -> 30 -> 40 -> 50.
-- On an EXISTING live database: RUN THIS ONE. It is purely additive
-- (new nullable columns + indexes + one view) and is safe to re-run.
--
-- WHY THIS EXISTS
-- ---------------
-- digital_sends.status only ever recorded whether ZivoGift managed to hand a
-- message to a provider. For email that is close enough to the truth. For
-- WhatsApp it is not: Meta's /messages endpoint returns 200 and a message id
-- almost immediately, long before it knows whether the number is reachable,
-- whether the template is still in good standing, or whether the user has
-- blocked the business. The real outcome arrives seconds-to-minutes later as
-- a delivery receipt on the webhook, under `value.statuses[]`.
--
-- netlify/functions/whatsapp-webhook.js ignored that array completely. So a
-- WhatsApp gift that Meta failed to deliver still sat in the database marked
-- 'sent', the admin delivery-health panel counted it as a success, and nobody
-- -- not the buyer, not you -- ever found out the recipient's phone never
-- buzzed at midnight.
--
-- These columns close that gap, and give the scheduler somewhere to record
-- when a gift had to be rescued onto a different channel.
-- =====================================================================

-- ── 1. WhatsApp delivery receipt columns ─────────────────────────────
--
-- wa_status mirrors Meta's own lifecycle so the values are greppable
-- against Meta's docs and logs, rather than being a private vocabulary:
--   sent      -- Meta accepted it and queued it
--   delivered -- it reached the recipient's device
--   read      -- the recipient opened the chat
--   failed    -- terminal; wa_error_code says why
--
-- NULL means "no receipt seen yet", which is different from 'failed' and
-- must stay distinguishable, hence nullable with no default.

ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS wa_status text;

ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS wa_status_at timestamptz;

ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS wa_error_code int;

-- Set when a send was delivered on a channel OTHER than the one the buyer
-- chose -- currently only WhatsApp -> email. Keeping the reason as free text
-- rather than a boolean means the admin view can show the actual Meta error
-- that forced the fallback.
ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS fallback_reason text;

-- Guardrail: only the four values Meta actually sends, plus NULL.
-- Added as NOT VALID so an existing row with unexpected data cannot block the
-- migration; new writes are still checked.
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.table_constraints
    WHERE table_name = 'digital_sends' AND constraint_name = 'digital_sends_wa_status_chk'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends
      ADD CONSTRAINT digital_sends_wa_status_chk
      CHECK (wa_status IS NULL OR wa_status IN ('sent','delivered','read','failed'))
      NOT VALID;
  END IF;
END $$;

-- ── 2. Indexes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- The webhook's hot path is a lookup by provider_message_id on every single
-- receipt -- and Meta sends up to three per message (sent, delivered, read).
-- Without this index that is a sequential scan of the whole table per receipt,
-- which is the one query guaranteed to get slower as you grow.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_digital_sends_provider_msg
  ON public.digital_sends (provider_message_id)
  WHERE provider_message_id IS NOT NULL;

-- Supports the admin delivery-health panel and any "what failed last night"
-- query without scanning delivered rows.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_digital_sends_wa_status
  ON public.digital_sends (wa_status, sent_at DESC)
  WHERE channel = 'whatsapp';

-- ── 3. Delivery health view ──────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- Read this after a midnight batch to see what ACTUALLY landed. The
-- distinction that matters is `accepted_by_meta` vs `confirmed_delivered`:
-- if those two numbers diverge, your gifts are not arriving even though
-- digital_sends.status says 'sent' for all of them.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.whatsapp_delivery_health AS
SELECT
  date_trunc('day', COALESCE(sent_at, created_at)) AS day,
  gift_type,
  count(*)                                              AS total,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'sent')               AS accepted_by_meta,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE wa_status = 'delivered')       AS confirmed_delivered,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE wa_status = 'read')            AS confirmed_read,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE wa_status = 'failed')          AS confirmed_failed,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE wa_status IS NULL
                     AND status = 'sent')               AS no_receipt_yet,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE fallback_reason IS NOT NULL)   AS fell_back_to_email
FROM public.digital_sends
WHERE channel = 'whatsapp' OR fallback_reason IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, 2;

-- The view inherits digital_sends' RLS via security_invoker, so it cannot be
-- used to read around the policies that protect sender_phone/sender_name.
-- (Postgres 15+ / current Supabase. Harmless to attempt on older versions.)
DO $$ BEGIN
  EXECUTE 'ALTER VIEW public.whatsapp_delivery_health SET (security_invoker = on)';
EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN
  RAISE NOTICE 'security_invoker not supported on this Postgres version -- view uses definer rights; restrict access via GRANTs instead.';
END $$;

REVOKE ALL ON public.whatsapp_delivery_health FROM anon;

-- ── 4. Verify ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns
--   WHERE table_name = 'digital_sends'
--     AND column_name IN ('wa_status','wa_status_at','wa_error_code','fallback_reason');
--
-- SELECT * FROM public.whatsapp_delivery_health LIMIT 20;

FILE: supabase\consolidated\60_campaigns_and_admin_ops.sql
=====================================================

-- =====================================================================
-- ZIVOGIFT consolidated migration: 60_campaigns_and_admin_ops.sql
--
-- Run order for a FRESH database: 10 -> 20 -> 30 -> 40 -> 50 -> 60.
-- On an EXISTING live database: RUN THIS ONE. It is purely additive
-- (new tables + one view + seed rows) and is safe to re-run.
--
-- WHAT THIS ADDS
-- --------------
--   1. public.v_customers        -- the customer list, derived from orders
--   2. public.marketing_optouts  -- the compliance gate (did not exist at all)
--   3. public.campaigns          -- one row per broadcast
--   4. public.campaign_recipients-- one row per individual send + receipt
--   5. public.admin_settings     -- DB-backed kill switches (no redeploy)
--   6. public.festival_schedules -- recurring yearly campaigns
--
-- WHY v_customers IS A VIEW OVER orders, NOT A TABLE
-- --------------------------------------------------
-- public.profiles has columns: id, full_name, phone, is_admin, created_at.
-- There is NO email column on profiles -- Supabase keeps the email in
-- auth.users, which is not reachable from the browser under RLS. The only
-- place a reachable customer email exists in this schema is
-- orders.contact_email / orders.guest_email.
--
-- So "all my existing customers" can only honestly mean "everyone who has
-- placed an order". A view means there is no second copy of customer data to
-- drift out of sync, and no migration to re-run when a new order lands.
--
-- WHY marketing_optouts IS NOT OPTIONAL
-- -------------------------------------
-- Before this migration the codebase had no unsubscribe concept anywhere
-- (grep: unsubscribe / opt_out / consent -- zero hits). Sending bulk
-- marketing with no opt-out path gets a Resend sending domain blocked and a
-- WhatsApp Business number quality-rated down to the point where the
-- TRANSACTIONAL gift templates stop being delivered. That would break the
-- actual product, not just the marketing. Every audience query in
-- _lib/audience.js filters through this table.
-- =====================================================================


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. MARKETING OPT-OUTS
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Stored by lowercased email AND/OR 10-digit phone, because the same human
-- can unsubscribe by clicking a link in an email or by replying STOP on
-- WhatsApp, and we must honour either one across both channels.
--
-- phone is stored as the last 10 digits, deliberately NOT E.164. The
-- codebase writes phones inconsistently (orders.contact_phone is raw user
-- input; digital_sends.recipient_phone is '91'-prefixed). Normalising to the
-- last 10 digits is the only comparison that matches every existing row.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.marketing_optouts (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email       text,
  phone10     text,
  source      text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'link',   -- 'link' | 'whatsapp_stop' | 'manual' | 'bounce'
  campaign_id uuid,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT marketing_optouts_has_identifier CHECK (email IS NOT NULL OR phone10 IS NOT NULL)
);

-- Partial unique indexes rather than a composite unique: a row may carry an
-- email, a phone, or both, and NULLs do not collide usefully in a composite.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_marketing_optouts_email
  ON public.marketing_optouts (lower(email)) WHERE email IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_marketing_optouts_phone
  ON public.marketing_optouts (phone10) WHERE phone10 IS NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE public.marketing_optouts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "marketing_optouts_admin_all" ON public.marketing_optouts;
CREATE POLICY "marketing_optouts_admin_all" ON public.marketing_optouts FOR ALL
  USING (public.is_admin()) WITH CHECK (public.is_admin());
-- Public unsubscribe writes happen through the service-role key in
-- netlify/functions/unsubscribe.js, which bypasses RLS by design.


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. THE CUSTOMER VIEW
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- One row per unique person. Identity key is the lowercased email when we
-- have one, else the 10-digit phone -- matching how a human would dedupe.
--
-- PAID definition matches js/admin.js's PAID_STATES exactly
-- ('paid','processing','packed','out_for_delivery','delivered') so the
-- numbers in the Campaigns tab agree with the numbers in Overview. If those
-- two ever disagree you will not trust either, so they are kept identical.

DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.v_customers;
CREATE VIEW public.v_customers AS
WITH order_rows AS (
  SELECT
    o.id                                                    AS order_id,
    o.user_id,
    lower(nullif(btrim(coalesce(o.contact_email, o.guest_email)), '')) AS email,
    right(regexp_replace(coalesce(o.contact_phone, o.guest_phone, ''), '\D', '', 'g'), 10) AS phone10,
    nullif(btrim(o.contact_name), '')                       AS full_name,
    o.status,
    o.total,
    o.created_at,
    (o.status IN ('paid','processing','packed','out_for_delivery','delivered')) AS is_paid,
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.order_items oi
      JOIN public.products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
      WHERE oi.order_id = o.id AND p.type = 'digital'
    ) AS has_digital,
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.order_items oi
      JOIN public.products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
      WHERE oi.order_id = o.id AND p.type <> 'digital'
    ) AS has_physical
  FROM public.orders o
),
keyed AS (
  SELECT *, coalesce(email, phone10) AS customer_key
  FROM order_rows
  WHERE coalesce(email, phone10) IS NOT NULL
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT
    k.customer_key,
    (array_agg(k.email     ORDER BY k.created_at DESC) FILTER (WHERE k.email     IS NOT NULL))[1] AS email,
    (array_agg(k.phone10   ORDER BY k.created_at DESC) FILTER (WHERE k.phone10  <> ''))[1]        AS phone10,
    (array_agg(k.full_name ORDER BY k.created_at DESC) FILTER (WHERE k.full_name IS NOT NULL))[1] AS full_name,
    (array_agg(k.user_id   ORDER BY k.created_at DESC) FILTER (WHERE k.user_id   IS NOT NULL))[1] AS user_id,
    count(*)                                           AS orders_count,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE k.is_paid)                  AS paid_orders_count,
    coalesce(sum(k.total) FILTER (WHERE k.is_paid), 0) AS lifetime_value,
    min(k.created_at)                                  AS first_order_at,
    max(k.created_at)                                  AS last_order_at,
    max(k.created_at) FILTER (WHERE k.is_paid)         AS last_paid_order_at,
    bool_or(k.has_digital)                             AS has_digital,
    bool_or(k.has_physical)                            AS has_physical
  FROM keyed k
  GROUP BY k.customer_key
)
-- Opt-out is resolved HERE, in the view itself, so that no caller anywhere
-- can forget to join it. Done as a LATERAL against the already-grouped rows
-- rather than inside the aggregate select list, which is where an earlier
-- draft of this view was subtly wrong.
SELECT
  g.*,
  (oo.hit IS NOT NULL) AS opted_out
FROM grouped g
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT 1 AS hit
  FROM public.marketing_optouts mo
  WHERE (g.email   IS NOT NULL AND mo.email   = g.email)
     OR (g.phone10 IS NOT NULL AND mo.phone10 = g.phone10)
  LIMIT 1
) oo ON true;

COMMENT ON VIEW public.v_customers IS
  'Deduped customer list derived from orders. profiles has no email column, so orders is the only reachable source of customer contact details.';

-- The view runs with the privileges of the querying role. The browser never
-- reads it directly (RLS on orders would filter it to the caller's own
-- orders); all campaign reads go through the service-role key in
-- netlify/functions/_lib/audience.js.


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. CAMPAIGNS
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.campaigns (
  id               uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name             text NOT NULL,
  channel          text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'email',   -- 'email' | 'whatsapp' | 'both'
  segment          text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'all',     -- see _lib/audience.js SEGMENTS
  subject          text,                            -- email only
  body             text NOT NULL,                   -- plain text; the email shell wraps it
  cta_url          text,
  cta_label        text,
  wa_template      text,                            -- approved Meta MARKETING template name
  status           text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',   -- draft|scheduled|sending|paused|completed|cancelled
  scheduled_at     timestamptz,
  started_at       timestamptz,
  completed_at     timestamptz,
  total_recipients int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  sent_count       int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  failed_count     int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_by       uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  is_automated     boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,  -- true = created by festival-scheduler
  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_campaigns_status ON public.campaigns(status, scheduled_at);

ALTER TABLE public.campaigns ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "campaigns_admin_all" ON public.campaigns;
CREATE POLICY "campaigns_admin_all" ON public.campaigns FOR ALL
  USING (public.is_admin()) WITH CHECK (public.is_admin());


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 4. CAMPAIGN RECIPIENTS
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Column names deliberately mirror digital_sends (status, provider_message_id,
-- wa_status, wa_status_at, wa_error_code, error_message, attempts) so that
-- whatsapp-webhook.js's existing receipt logic can be pointed at this table
-- with the same field handling rather than a parallel vocabulary.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.campaign_recipients (
  id                  uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  campaign_id         uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.campaigns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  customer_key        text NOT NULL,
  full_name           text,
  email               text,
  phone10             text,
  channel             text NOT NULL,                -- 'email' | 'whatsapp'
  status              text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued', -- queued|sent|failed|skipped
  attempts            int  NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  provider_message_id text,
  wa_status           text,
  wa_status_at        timestamptz,
  wa_error_code       int,
  error_message       text,
  sent_at             timestamptz,
  created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- The scheduler's hot query. Partial index keeps it cheap even as the table
-- grows, which matters because campaign-sender runs on a cron every 5 min
-- and must early-exit without burning Netlify credits.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_campaign_recipients_queued
  ON public.campaign_recipients(campaign_id) WHERE status = 'queued';
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_campaign_recipients_msgid
  ON public.campaign_recipients(provider_message_id) WHERE provider_message_id IS NOT NULL;

-- One send per person per campaign per channel. This is the guard that makes
-- a retried or double-clicked launch idempotent instead of double-messaging
-- your whole customer list.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_campaign_recipient
  ON public.campaign_recipients(campaign_id, customer_key, channel);

ALTER TABLE public.campaign_recipients ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "campaign_recipients_admin_all" ON public.campaign_recipients;
CREATE POLICY "campaign_recipients_admin_all" ON public.campaign_recipients FOR ALL
  USING (public.is_admin()) WITH CHECK (public.is_admin());


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 5. ADMIN SETTINGS (kill switches)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- These live in the DATABASE, not in Netlify env vars, for one specific
-- reason: changing an env var requires a redeploy, a redeploy requires a
-- laptop, and it burns build credits. A row in this table can be flipped
-- from the admin panel on a phone, and every scheduler reads it on entry.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.admin_settings (
  key        text PRIMARY KEY,
  value      jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT 'false'::jsonb,
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_by uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
);

ALTER TABLE public.admin_settings ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

  USING (public.is_admin()) WITH CHECK (public.is_admin());

INSERT INTO public.admin_settings (key, value) VALUES
  ('pause_campaigns',      'false'::jsonb),
  ('pause_all_schedulers', 'false'::jsonb),
  ('pause_festivals',      'false'::jsonb)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING;


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 6. FESTIVAL SCHEDULES
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- month/day rather than a full date, because these recur every year and a
-- stored date would silently stop firing after the first year -- exactly the
-- failure mode this feature exists to avoid while you are away from a laptop.
--
-- send_hour_utc defaults to 04:00 UTC = 09:30 IST, a deliberate choice: the
-- existing reminder-scheduler fires at 02:00 UTC and occasion-scheduler at
-- 02:30 UTC, so festivals land after both and cannot collide with them.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.festival_schedules (
  id             uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name           text NOT NULL,
  month          int  NOT NULL CHECK (month BETWEEN 1 AND 12),
  day            int  NOT NULL CHECK (day BETWEEN 1 AND 31),
  lead_days      int  NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,      -- fire this many days BEFORE the date
  channel        text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'email',
  segment        text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'paid',
  subject        text,
  body           text NOT NULL,
  cta_url        text DEFAULT 'https://zivogift.com',
  cta_label      text DEFAULT 'Send a gift',
  wa_template    text,
  active         boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- OFF by default; you switch each one on
  last_fired_year int,                           -- the once-per-year idempotency guard
  created_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_festival_name ON public.festival_schedules(lower(name));

ALTER TABLE public.festival_schedules ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "festival_schedules_admin_all" ON public.festival_schedules;
CREATE POLICY "festival_schedules_admin_all" ON public.festival_schedules FOR ALL
  USING (public.is_admin()) WITH CHECK (public.is_admin());

-- Seeded INACTIVE on purpose. Nothing auto-sends to your customer list until
-- you read the copy and tick Active yourself.
--
-- Dates: fixed-date festivals carry their real date. Holi, Raksha Bandhan and
-- Diwali follow the Hindu lunar calendar and MOVE every year -- the dates
-- below are placeholders you must correct annually from the admin panel. They
-- are seeded anyway so the row, the copy and the schedule already exist and
-- you only ever have to change two number fields from your phone.
INSERT INTO public.festival_schedules (name, month, day, lead_days, channel, segment, subject, body, active) VALUES
  ('New Year',        1,  1,  4, 'email', 'all',  'Start their year with something they will keep',
   'A new year is the best excuse to tell someone they mattered in the last one. Send a personalised Zivogift note that lands on New Year''s Day.', false),
  ('Valentine''s Day',2, 14, 5, 'email', 'all',  'Valentine''s gifts that are not another teddy bear',

FILE: supabase\consolidated\70_pipeline_fixes.sql

-- =====================================================================
-- ZIVOGIFT consolidated migration: 70_pipeline_fixes.sql
--
-- Run order for a FRESH database: 10 -> 20 -> 30 -> 40 -> 50 -> 60 -> 70.
-- On an EXISTING live database: RUN THIS ONE. Purely additive (new nullable
-- columns + indexes + one view). Safe to re-run.
--
-- WHAT THIS ADDS, AND WHICH AUDIT FINDING EACH ONE CLOSES
-- -------------------------------------------------------
--   1. digital_sends.buyer_notified_at   -- #3  buyer told when a gift fails
--   2. orders.tracking_number/courier    -- #6  physical orders were untrackable
--   3. orders.recovery_email_sent_at     -- #8  abandoned checkout recovery
--   4. products.stock_qty                -- #10 nothing prevented overselling
--   5. v_abandoned_checkouts (view)      -- #8  the recovery queue
-- =====================================================================


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. BUYER FAILURE NOTIFICATION STAMP  (audit finding #3)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- gift-scheduler.js gave up after MAX_ATTEMPTS and emailed ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL
-- only -- and if that env var was unset, the failure went nowhere but a log
-- line. The buyer was never told their gift had not arrived.
--
-- This column makes the new buyer notification idempotent: a re-queued or
-- manually retried send that fails again must not email the same person a
-- second time. NULL means "not yet told", which is the correct default for
-- every existing row -- those buyers were never told either, and back-filling
-- a timestamp would wrongly suppress a notification they still deserve if the
-- row is retried.

ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS buyer_notified_at timestamptz;

COMMENT ON COLUMN public.digital_sends.buyer_notified_at IS
  'When the BUYER was emailed about a permanent delivery failure. Guards against duplicate notifications on retry.';


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. COURIER TRACKING  (audit finding #6)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- There was no tracking field anywhere in the schema. The status email told a
-- customer their gift was "Out for delivery" and then gave them no way to
-- actually track it -- so every one of those emails generated a "where is my
-- order?" reply you had to answer by hand.
--
-- tracking_url is stored rather than derived from courier_name, because
-- courier URL formats change and a hardcoded template would rot silently.
-- Admin pastes whatever the courier gives them.

ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS tracking_number text;
ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS courier_name    text;
ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS tracking_url    text;

-- Partial index: only a small fraction of orders ever carry a tracking number,
-- and this supports "find the order for this AWB" lookups from support.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_tracking
  ON public.orders(tracking_number) WHERE tracking_number IS NOT NULL;


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. ABANDONED CHECKOUT RECOVERY  (audit finding #8)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Orders were created with status 'pending_payment' before the customer was
-- sent to Cashfree, and nothing ever followed up on the ones that never came
-- back. These are the highest-intent visitors the site gets -- they chose a
-- gift, typed a delivery address, and reached the payment page.
--
-- One column, not a table: the order row already holds everything needed.
-- NOT NULL means "already contacted", which is what makes the scheduler
-- idempotent and stops a cron restart from re-mailing everybody.

ALTER TABLE public.orders
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS recovery_email_sent_at timestamptz;

COMMENT ON COLUMN public.orders.recovery_email_sent_at IS
  'When an abandoned-checkout recovery email was sent. NULL = not yet contacted. Exactly one is ever sent per order.';

-- The recovery scheduler's hot query.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_abandoned
  ON public.orders(status, created_at)
  WHERE status = 'pending_payment' AND recovery_email_sent_at IS NULL;


-- The recovery queue, with the timing rules expressed ONCE, here, rather than
-- duplicated in the scheduler.
--
-- WHY THE 1-HOUR FLOOR
-- --------------------
-- A customer who is mid-payment right now, or who is on a slow bank OTP page,
-- must never receive a "you did not finish" email while they are still
-- finishing. An hour is comfortably longer than any real payment flow,
-- including the worst UPI/3DS timeouts.
--
-- WHY THE 7-DAY CEILING
-- ---------------------
-- Past a week the email reads as strange rather than helpful, and the person
-- has usually either bought elsewhere or forgotten. It also stops a first
-- deploy of this feature from mailing years of historical abandoned rows in
-- one burst -- which would look exactly like a spam run to every mailbox
-- provider at once.
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.v_abandoned_checkouts;
CREATE VIEW public.v_abandoned_checkouts AS
SELECT
  o.id,
  o.order_number,
  o.contact_name,
  o.contact_email,
  o.contact_phone,
  o.total,
  o.created_at,
  right(regexp_replace(coalesce(o.contact_phone, o.guest_phone, ''), '\D', '', 'g'), 10) AS phone10
FROM public.orders o
WHERE o.status = 'pending_payment'
  AND o.recovery_email_sent_at IS NULL
  AND o.contact_email IS NOT NULL
  AND btrim(o.contact_email) <> ''
  AND o.created_at < now() - interval '1 hour'
  AND o.created_at > now() - interval '7 days';

COMMENT ON VIEW public.v_abandoned_checkouts IS
  'Orders stranded at pending_payment for 1h-7d that have not yet had a recovery email.';


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 4. STOCK TRACKING  (audit finding #10)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Nothing in the schema or the order path prevented selling a denomination
-- that had run out. For serial-number currency notes that is a real
-- constraint: a ₹500 note carrying a specific birth date either exists in
-- your drawer or it does not, and the customer has already paid before anyone
-- finds out.
--
-- DESIGN: stock_qty IS NULLABLE, AND NULL MEANS "UNLIMITED".
-- That is deliberate and is what makes this migration safe to apply to a live
-- site: every existing product stays unlimited until YOU set a number on it.
-- A default of 0 would take the entire catalogue offline the moment this runs.
--
-- Digital products (type='digital') should simply be left NULL forever -- they
-- have no physical scarcity.

ALTER TABLE public.products
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS stock_qty int;

COMMENT ON COLUMN public.products.stock_qty IS
  'Units available. NULL = unlimited (the default, and correct for all digital products). 0 = sold out.';

-- Guard against a negative value arriving from a bad admin edit or a race.
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'products_stock_qty_non_negative'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.products
      ADD CONSTRAINT products_stock_qty_non_negative
      CHECK (stock_qty IS NULL OR stock_qty >= 0) NOT VALID;
  END IF;
END $$;


-- Atomic stock decrement.
--
-- WHY AN RPC AND NOT A PLAIN UPDATE FROM THE FUNCTION
-- ---------------------------------------------------
-- Two customers buying the last ₹500 note at the same instant would both read
-- stock_qty = 1, both pass a JS check, and both be charged. The single
-- statement below decrements only WHERE stock_qty >= p_qty, so exactly one of
-- those two transactions can succeed; the loser gets FALSE and is told the
-- item just sold out, before payment.
--
-- Returns TRUE when the decrement happened (or when the product is unlimited),
-- FALSE when there was not enough stock.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.decrement_stock(p_product_id text, p_qty int)
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_updated int;
  v_stock   int;
BEGIN
  SELECT stock_qty INTO v_stock FROM public.products WHERE id = p_product_id;

  -- Unknown product: not this function's job to reject. create-cashfree-order
  -- already validates the product exists; returning true keeps the two
  -- concerns separate rather than failing with a confusing "out of stock".
  IF NOT FOUND THEN RETURN true; END IF;

  -- NULL = unlimited.
  IF v_stock IS NULL THEN RETURN true; END IF;

  UPDATE public.products
     SET stock_qty = stock_qty - p_qty
   WHERE id = p_product_id
     AND stock_qty >= p_qty;

  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_updated = ROW_COUNT;
  RETURN v_updated > 0;
END;
$$;

-- Restock / manual correction helper, so the admin panel never has to hold
-- the service-role key to adjust a number.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.set_stock(p_product_id text, p_qty int)
RETURNS void
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT public.is_admin() THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Only an admin can set stock levels';
  END IF;
  UPDATE public.products SET stock_qty = p_qty WHERE id = p_product_id;
END;
$$;

FILE: supabase\consolidated\80_whatsapp_inbox.sql

-- ============================================================================
-- ZIVOGIFT · 80_whatsapp_inbox.sql
--
-- CUSTOMER MESSAGES (WhatsApp Inbox) — schema.
--
-- Run this AFTER 70_pipeline_fixes.sql. It is additive and idempotent: it
-- creates new tables only and does NOT alter public.whatsapp_inbound_log,
-- which stays exactly as it is because Condition-Based Delivery (#23) and
-- Care-Package pause/resume both depend on its UNIQUE(wa_message_id) dedupe.
--
-- WHY THESE TABLES EXIST
-- ----------------------
-- whatsapp_inbound_log is an EVENT log: flat, inbound-only, upper-cased,
-- text-only, with no thread and no outbound side. It was built to answer
-- "did this person text the keyword?" and it answers that well.
--
-- It cannot answer "show me my conversation with this customer", because:
--   • it stores no outbound messages
--   • it stores no media (photos of bulk-order requirement lists, voice notes)
--   • it upper-cases the body, destroying it as a readable transcript
--   • it has no unread / open / closed state to work a queue from
--
-- So: new tables, new purpose. Both writers run through the service-role key
-- from Netlify Functions, so RLS is admin-only across the board.
--
-- ZERO-MESSAGE-LOSS DESIGN
-- ------------------------
-- The webhook writes wa_messages BEFORE it interprets anything. Three things
-- make loss structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely:
--   1. raw_payload jsonb holds Meta's original object verbatim. Even a message
--      type this code has never seen is fully recoverable.
--   2. msg_type 'unsupported' is a valid, stored state — not a reason to drop.
--   3. wa_webhook_failures spools any payload that threw before it could be
--      stored, so the worst case is "stored but unprocessed", never "gone".
-- ============================================================================

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- CONTACTS — one row per customer phone number (the conversation header)
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.wa_contacts (
  id                uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

  -- phone10 is THE join key across this codebase (campaign_recipients.phone10,
  -- marketing_optouts.phone10, the ...slice(-10) normalisation in the webhook).
  -- Keeping the same convention means no translation layer anywhere.
  phone10           text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  wa_phone          text,                       -- full E.164 without '+', e.g. 919876543210
  profile_name      text,                       -- Meta-supplied WhatsApp display name

  -- ── 24-HOUR CUSTOMER SERVICE WINDOW ───────────────────────────────────────
  -- Meta permits free-text replies only within 24h of the customer's last
  -- inbound message. Outside it, a free-text send is REJECTED and an approved
  -- template is required. The admin UI reads this to decide whether to show a
  -- free-text composer or the template composer — without it the dashboard
  -- would appear to send and silently fail.
  last_inbound_at   timestamptz,
  window_expires_at timestamptz,

  last_outbound_at  timestamptz,
  last_message_at   timestamptz,                -- either direction; drives list sort
  last_message_preview text,

  unread_count      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  status            text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',   -- open | closed
  admin_note        text,

  -- Soft links for context. Deliberately NOT foreign keys: a bulk-order
  -- enquiry can arrive from someone who has never ordered, and a FK would
  -- either reject the row or force a placeholder.
  user_id           uuid,
  last_order_number text,

  -- Throttles the free email alert to once per contact per hour.
  last_alert_at     timestamptz,

  created_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_contacts_last_message
  ON public.wa_contacts (last_message_at DESC NULLS LAST);

-- Partial index: the inbox default view is "open conversations with unread
-- messages", which is almost always a tiny slice of the table.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_contacts_unread
  ON public.wa_contacts (unread_count DESC, last_message_at DESC)
  WHERE unread_count > 0;

ALTER TABLE public.wa_contacts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "wa_contacts_admin_all" ON public.wa_contacts;
CREATE POLICY "wa_contacts_admin_all" ON public.wa_contacts
  FOR ALL USING (public.is_admin()) WITH CHECK (public.is_admin());

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- MESSAGES — every message, both directions, every type
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.wa_messages (
  id              uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  contact_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.wa_contacts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  phone10         text NOT NULL,

  direction       text NOT NULL CHECK (direction IN ('in', 'out')),

  -- Meta's message id. UNIQUE is the dedupe guarantee: Meta retries a webhook
  -- delivery whenever we fail to return 200, and without this a retry storm
  -- would duplicate every message in the transcript.
  --
  -- NULLable on purpose — an outbound send that FAILED at Meta has no id, and
  -- we still want the attempt visible in the thread. Postgres treats NULLs as
  -- distinct in a UNIQUE index, so any number of failed sends coexist.
  wa_message_id   text UNIQUE,

  -- text | image | audio | video | document | sticker | location | contacts
  -- | button | interactive | reaction | system | unsupported
  msg_type        text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'text',
  body            text,                    -- ORIGINAL casing. Never upper-cased.
  caption         text,

  -- Media is stored by REFERENCE first. Meta's own media URLs expire within
  -- minutes and require the bearer token, but the media_id stays valid ~30
  -- days — long enough to fetch lazily when an admin actually opens the
  -- thread. Eagerly downloading every inbound image inside the webhook would
  -- risk Netlify's 10s function limit and pay R2 egress for spam.
  media_id        text,
  media_mime      text,
  media_sha256    text,
  media_size      bigint,
  media_url       text,                    -- populated on first view (R2)
  media_fetched_at timestamptz,
  media_error     text,

  -- Quoted/replied-to message. This is what makes replying from a personal
  -- phone unambiguous (Run D relay): Meta puts the quoted message id in
  -- context.id, which resolves to exactly one conversation.
  context_wa_id   text,

  -- Outbound bookkeeping
  status          text,                    -- queued|sent|delivered|read|failed
  status_at       timestamptz,
  error_code      text,
  error_message   text,
  sent_by_admin   text,                    -- admin email, or NULL for automation
  template_name   text,                    -- set when sent as a template

  -- Why this outbound row exists. 'reply' = typed in the dashboard.
  -- 'automation' = mirrored from gift/campaign/order sends.
  -- 'relay' = sent from the personal-number relay.
  source          text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'reply',

  -- Meta's original object, verbatim. The last line of defence: if this code
  -- misreads a payload shape, the truth is still on disk.
  raw_payload     jsonb,

  created_at      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_messages_contact
  ON public.wa_messages (contact_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_messages_phone
  ON public.wa_messages (phone10, created_at DESC);
-- Used by the delivery-receipt handler to resolve a status update to a row.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_messages_waid
  ON public.wa_messages (wa_message_id)
  WHERE wa_message_id IS NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE public.wa_messages ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "wa_messages_admin_all" ON public.wa_messages;
CREATE POLICY "wa_messages_admin_all" ON public.wa_messages
  FOR ALL USING (public.is_admin()) WITH CHECK (public.is_admin());

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- FAILURE SPOOL — the reason "lost message" is not a possible outcome
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The webhook must always return 200 to Meta (a non-200 triggers retries that
-- can flood the function). That means a bug inside our own processing would
-- otherwise swallow a real customer message silently. Anything that throws
-- lands here with the raw body attached, and the Emergency tab surfaces the
-- count so you can see it happened.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.wa_webhook_failures (
  id           uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  stage        text,          -- where it broke: 'parse' | 'message' | 'status'
  wa_message_id text,
  from_phone   text,
  error        text,
  raw_payload  jsonb,
  resolved     boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_failures_unresolved
  ON public.wa_webhook_failures (created_at DESC)
  WHERE resolved = false;

ALTER TABLE public.wa_webhook_failures ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "wa_webhook_failures_admin_all" ON public.wa_webhook_failures;
CREATE POLICY "wa_webhook_failures_admin_all" ON public.wa_webhook_failures
  FOR ALL USING (public.is_admin()) WITH CHECK (public.is_admin());

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- RELAY MAP — makes a quoted reply from your personal phone unambiguous
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- When the relay forwards a customer message to ADMIN_WHATSAPP_NUMBER, Meta
-- gives that forwarded message its own id. If you long-press it and hit Reply,
-- Meta returns that id in context.id on the inbound webhook.
--
-- This table is what turns that id back into "the reply is for THIS customer".
-- Without it, replying from your phone would depend entirely on typing the
-- number prefix — workable, but not what anyone actually does when three
-- conversations are live at once.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.wa_relay_map (
  id            uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  -- The id of the message WE sent to the admin's personal number.
  relay_wa_id   text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  contact_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.wa_contacts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  phone10       text NOT NULL,
  -- The customer message being forwarded, so a reply can quote it back.
  source_wa_id  text,
  created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wa_relay_map_contact
  ON public.wa_relay_map (contact_id, created_at DESC);

ALTER TABLE public.wa_relay_map ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "wa_relay_map_admin_all" ON public.wa_relay_map;
CREATE POLICY "wa_relay_map_admin_all" ON public.wa_relay_map
  FOR ALL USING (public.is_admin()) WITH CHECK (public.is_admin());

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- KILL SWITCHES
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- admin_settings is created by 60_campaigns_and_admin_ops.sql. These rows are
-- read on every webhook tick, so they take effect with no redeploy — which is
-- the entire point (a Netlify env change costs build credits and a laptop).
--
--   pause_wa_alerts : stop the free email alert on new customer messages
--   pause_wa_relay  : stop the personal-number WhatsApp relay (Run D).
--                     Ships as TRUE = relay OFF, because the relay is the only
--                     part of this feature that costs money per message.
INSERT INTO public.admin_settings (key, value)
VALUES ('pause_wa_alerts', false)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING;

INSERT INTO public.admin_settings (key, value)
VALUES ('pause_wa_relay', true)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING;

-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- BACKFILL — carry existing inbound history into the new inbox
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Everything already captured in whatsapp_inbound_log becomes a real thread,
-- so the Messages tab is not empty on day one. Bodies are upper-cased (that
-- damage predates this migration and cannot be undone), which is why the
-- backfilled rows are tagged msg_type 'text' with source-of-truth intact in
-- the original table.
INSERT INTO public.wa_contacts (phone10, wa_phone, last_inbound_at, last_message_at, window_expires_at, last_message_preview)
SELECT
  RIGHT(REGEXP_REPLACE(l.from_phone, '\D', '', 'g'), 10)  AS phone10,
  REGEXP_REPLACE(l.from_phone, '\D', '', 'g')             AS wa_phone,
  MAX(l.created_at),
  MAX(l.created_at),
  MAX(l.created_at) + INTERVAL '24 hours',
  NULL
FROM public.whatsapp_inbound_log l
WHERE LENGTH(REGEXP_REPLACE(l.from_phone, '\D', '', 'g')) >= 10
GROUP BY 1, 2
ON CONFLICT (phone10) DO NOTHING;

INSERT INTO public.wa_messages (contact_id, phone10, direction, wa_message_id, msg_type, body, created_at, source)
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.phone10,
  'in',
  l.wa_message_id,
  'text',
  l.body,
  l.created_at,
  'backfill'
FROM public.whatsapp_inbound_log l
JOIN public.wa_contacts c
  ON c.phone10 = RIGHT(REGEXP_REPLACE(l.from_phone, '\D', '', 'g'), 10)
WHERE l.wa_message_id IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (wa_message_id) DO NOTHING;

-- Backfilled threads are history, not a to-do list — do not light up the
-- unread badge with messages you have already dealt with.
UPDATE public.wa_contacts SET unread_count = 0 WHERE unread_count <> 0;

-- ============================================================================
-- ZIVOGIFT — ₹1 live-test promo (ZIVOSURI01) + birthday-note add-ons safety seed
-- Run once in Supabase: Dashboard → SQL Editor → New query → paste → Run.
-- Safe to re-run (idempotent).
-- ============================================================================

-- ── 1) ₹1 SMOKE-TEST PROMO ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Uses a NEW promo type 'fixed_total'. create-cashfree-order.js reads this type
-- and forces the FINAL payable amount to `value` (₹1 here), regardless of what
-- is in the cart. Cashfree's minimum order amount is ₹1, so keep value >= 1.
-- This lets you push one real payment through the LIVE gateway for a token sum.
--
-- SECURITY NOTE: because this makes ANY cart cost ₹1, treat ZIVOSURI01 as a
-- secret. Deactivate it the moment your live test passes:
--     update public.promo_codes set active = false where code = 'ZIVOSURI01';
insert into public.promo_codes (code, type, value, active)
values ('ZIVOSURI01', 'fixed_total', 1, true)
on conflict (code) do update
  set type = excluded.type,
      value = excluded.value,
      active = excluded.active;

-- ── 2) BIRTHDAY-NOTE ADD-ONS (safety seed) ──────────────────────────────────
-- These 6 rows already ship in schema.sql. This block only guarantees they
-- exist in your DB so the new Admin → Add-ons panel has something to manage.
-- 'on conflict do nothing' means it will NOT overwrite any prices/active flags
-- you have already customised.
insert into public.addons (id, name, description, emoji, price, active, sort_order) values
  ('addon_box',        'Premium Keepsake Box',   'Kraft or velvet keepsake box.',                     '📦', 149, true, 10),

-- ---------- EXTENSIONS ----------
create extension if not exists "pgcrypto"; -- for gen_random_uuid()

-- ---------- PROFILES (1 row per auth.users row) ----------
create table if not exists public.profiles (
  id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  full_name text,
  phone text,
  is_admin boolean not null default false,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- Auto-create a profile row whenever someone signs up
create or replace function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer set search_path = public
as $$
begin
  insert into public.profiles (id, full_name, phone)
  values (new.id, new.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name', new.raw_user_meta_data->>'phone')
  on conflict (id) do nothing;
  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists on_auth_user_created on auth.users;
create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute procedure public.handle_new_user();

-- ---------- ADDRESSES ----------
create table if not exists public.addresses (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  label text default 'Home',
  recipient_name text not null,
  phone text not null,
  line1 text not null,
  line2 text,
  city text not null default 'Bengaluru',
  state text not null default 'Karnataka',
  pincode text not null,
  is_default boolean not null default false,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- ---------- PRODUCTS ----------
-- type: 'note' | 'bundle' | 'kit' | 'digital' | 'squad'
create table if not exists public.products (
  id text primary key,               -- short slug, e.g. 'note_100'
  type text not null,
  name text not null,
  description text,
  emoji text,
  face_value numeric,                 -- for currency notes, e.g. 100
  price numeric not null,
  compare_at_price numeric,           -- optional "value framing" price, nullable
  image_url text,
  options jsonb default '[]'::jsonb,  -- [{label, values:[]}]
  active boolean not null default true,
  sort_order int not null default 0,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- ---------- ADD-ONS ----------
create table if not exists public.addons (
  id text primary key,
  name text not null,
  description text,
  emoji text,
  price numeric not null default 0,
  active boolean not null default true,
  sort_order int not null default 0
);

-- ---------- PROMO CODES ----------
create table if not exists public.promo_codes (
  code text primary key,
  type text not null default 'percent', -- 'percent' | 'flat'
  value numeric not null,
  max_discount numeric,
  active boolean not null default true,
  expires_at timestamptz
);

-- ---------- ORDERS ----------
-- status flow: pending_payment -> paid -> processing -> packed -> out_for_delivery -> delivered
--              (or) -> cancelled / refunded / payment_failed
create table if not exists public.orders (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  order_number text unique not null default ('ZG' || to_char(now(),'YYMMDD') || lpad(floor(random()*100000)::text,5,'0')),
  user_id uuid references auth.users(id) on delete set null, -- null = guest order
  guest_email text,
  guest_phone text,
  status text not null default 'pending_payment',
  contact_name text not null,
  contact_phone text not null,
  contact_email text not null,
  delivery_type text not null default 'standard', -- 'standard' | 'campus' | 'express'
  address_line text not null,
  city text not null default 'Bengaluru',
  pincode text,
  delivery_notes text,
  subtotal numeric not null default 0,
  discount numeric not null default 0,
  delivery_fee numeric not null default 0,
  total numeric not null default 0,
  promo_code text,
  payment_method text default 'cashfree',
  cashfree_order_id text,
  cashfree_payment_session_id text,
  cashfree_payment_id text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table if not exists public.order_items (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  order_id uuid not null references public.orders(id) on delete cascade,
  product_id text references public.products(id),
  name_snapshot text not null,
  unit_price numeric not null,
  qty int not null default 1,
  recipient_name text,
  recipient_dob date,
  personalization_message text,
  selected_options jsonb default '{}'::jsonb,
  addons jsonb default '[]'::jsonb,    -- [{id,name,price}]
  addon_total numeric not null default 0,
  line_total numeric not null default 0
);

create table if not exists public.order_status_history (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  order_id uuid not null references public.orders(id) on delete cascade,
  status text not null,
  note text,
  changed_by uuid references auth.users(id),
  changed_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create index if not exists idx_orders_user on public.orders(user_id);
create index if not exists idx_order_items_order on public.order_items(order_id);
create index if not exists idx_status_history_order on public.order_status_history(order_id);

-- updated_at maintenance

returns trigger language plpgsql as $$
begin new.updated_at = now(); return new; end; $$;

drop trigger if exists trg_orders_touch on public.orders;
create trigger trg_orders_touch before update on public.orders
  for each row execute procedure public.touch_updated_at();

-- helper: is the current user an admin?
create or replace function public.is_admin()
returns boolean language sql stable security definer set search_path = public as $$
  select coalesce((select is_admin from public.profiles where id = auth.uid()), false);
$$;

-- profiles: a user can read/update their own row; admins can read all
drop policy if exists "profiles_self_select" on public.profiles;
create policy "profiles_self_select" on public.profiles for select
  using (auth.uid() = id or public.is_admin());
drop policy if exists "profiles_self_update" on public.profiles;
create policy "profiles_self_update" on public.profiles for update
  using (auth.uid() = id);

-- addresses: owner only (+ admin read)
drop policy if exists "addresses_owner_all" on public.addresses;
create policy "addresses_owner_all" on public.addresses for all
  using (auth.uid() = user_id or public.is_admin())
  with check (auth.uid() = user_id);

-- products/addons/promo_codes: public read of active items; admin full access
drop policy if exists "products_public_read" on public.products;
create policy "products_public_read" on public.products for select using (active = true or public.is_admin());
drop policy if exists "products_admin_write" on public.products;
create policy "products_admin_write" on public.products for all using (public.is_admin()) with check (public.is_admin());

drop policy if exists "addons_public_read" on public.addons;
create policy "addons_public_read" on public.addons for select using (active = true or public.is_admin());
drop policy if exists "addons_admin_write" on public.addons;
create policy "addons_admin_write" on public.addons for all using (public.is_admin()) with check (public.is_admin());

drop policy if exists "promo_public_read" on public.promo_codes;
create policy "promo_public_read" on public.promo_codes for select using (active = true or public.is_admin());
drop policy if exists "promo_admin_write" on public.promo_codes;
create policy "promo_admin_write" on public.promo_codes for all using (public.is_admin()) with check (public.is_admin());

-- orders: owner can read their own; admin can read/update all.
-- INSERT is intentionally NOT allowed from the browser — orders are created
-- only by the create-cashfree-order Netlify Function using the service-role key,
-- so totals can never be tampered with client-side.
drop policy if exists "orders_owner_select" on public.orders;
create policy "orders_owner_select" on public.orders for select
  using (auth.uid() = user_id or public.is_admin());
drop policy if exists "orders_admin_update" on public.orders;
create policy "orders_admin_update" on public.orders for update
  using (public.is_admin()) with check (public.is_admin());

drop policy if exists "order_items_owner_select" on public.order_items;
create policy "order_items_owner_select" on public.order_items for select
  using (
    public.is_admin() or
    exists (select 1 from public.orders o where o.id = order_id and o.user_id = auth.uid())
  );

drop policy if exists "status_history_owner_select" on public.order_status_history;
create policy "status_history_owner_select" on public.order_status_history for select
  using (
    public.is_admin() or
    exists (select 1 from public.orders o where o.id = order_id and o.user_id = auth.uid())
  );
drop policy if exists "status_history_admin_insert" on public.order_status_history;
create policy "status_history_admin_insert" on public.order_status_history for insert
  with check (public.is_admin());

-- ============================================================================
-- GUEST ORDER TRACKING
-- Lets anyone look up an order by order_number + the phone number used at
-- checkout, without needing to be logged in or bypassing RLS for everyone.
-- ============================================================================
create or replace function public.track_order(p_order_number text, p_phone text)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql security definer set search_path = public as $$
declare
  v_order public.orders%rowtype;
  v_items jsonb;
  v_history jsonb;
begin
  select * into v_order from public.orders
    where order_number = p_order_number and contact_phone = p_phone;
  if not found then
    return null;
  end if;
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(oi), '[]'::jsonb) into v_items
    from public.order_items oi where oi.order_id = v_order.id;
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(h order by h.changed_at), '[]'::jsonb) into v_history
    from public.order_status_history h where h.order_id = v_order.id;
  return jsonb_build_object('order', to_jsonb(v_order), 'items', v_items, 'history', v_history);
end;
$$;

grant execute on function public.track_order(text, text) to anon, authenticated;

-- ADMIN SETUP — run this manually AFTER your first signup, replacing the email:

-- ============================================================================
-- DIGITAL GIFT SENDS — Phase 2 addition
-- Tracks every scheduled WhatsApp/email delivery for digital products.
-- The gift-scheduler Netlify Function polls this table every 2 minutes.
-- ============================================================================

-- Add recipient contact + scheduled time onto order_items (safe to run after
-- the table already exists — uses IF NOT EXISTS guards).
do $$ begin
  if not exists (select 1 from information_schema.columns where table_name='order_items' and column_name='recipient_phone') then
    alter table public.order_items add column recipient_phone text;
  end if;
  if not exists (select 1 from information_schema.columns where table_name='order_items' and column_name='scheduled_send_at') then
    alter table public.order_items add column scheduled_send_at timestamptz;
  end if;
end $$;

create table if not exists public.digital_sends (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  order_id uuid not null references public.orders(id) on delete cascade,
  order_item_id uuid not null references public.order_items(id) on delete cascade,
  recipient_name text not null,
  recipient_phone text not null,           -- WhatsApp number in E.164 format: 919876543210
  sender_name text not null,               -- buyer's name, shown in the message
  personal_message text,
  occasion text default 'Birthday',
  card_image_url text,                     -- URL of the card image to attach
  channel text not null default 'whatsapp', -- 'whatsapp' | 'email' (future)
  scheduled_at timestamptz not null,       -- when to send
  sent_at timestamptz,
  status text not null default 'pending',  -- 'pending' | 'sent' | 'failed' | 'cancelled'
  provider_message_id text,               -- Interakt/provider's message ID for tracking
  error_message text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create index if not exists idx_digital_sends_scheduled on public.digital_sends(scheduled_at, status);
create index if not exists idx_digital_sends_order on public.digital_sends(order_id);

-- RLS: admin full access; buyer can see their own sends.
alter table public.digital_sends enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "digital_sends_owner_select" on public.digital_sends;
create policy "digital_sends_owner_select" on public.digital_sends for select
  using (
    public.is_admin() or
    exists (select 1 from public.orders o where o.id = order_id and o.user_id = auth.uid())
  );

drop policy if exists "digital_sends_admin_all" on public.digital_sends;
create policy "digital_sends_admin_all" on public.digital_sends for all
  using (public.is_admin()) with check (public.is_admin());

-- Update track_order RPC to also return digital sends for the buyer.
create or replace function public.track_order(p_order_number text, p_phone text)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql security definer set search_path = public as $$
declare
  v_order public.orders%rowtype;
  v_items jsonb;
  v_history jsonb;
  v_digital_sends jsonb;
begin
  select * into v_order from public.orders
    where order_number = p_order_number and contact_phone = p_phone;
  if not found then return null; end if;
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(oi), '[]'::jsonb) into v_items
    from public.order_items oi where oi.order_id = v_order.id;
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(h order by h.changed_at), '[]'::jsonb) into v_history
    from public.order_status_history h where h.order_id = v_order.id;
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(ds order by ds.scheduled_at), '[]'::jsonb) into v_digital_sends
    from public.digital_sends ds where ds.order_id = v_order.id;
  return jsonb_build_object(
    'order', to_jsonb(v_order),
    'items', v_items,
    'history', v_history,
    'digital_sends', v_digital_sends
  );
end;
$$;

-- ============================================================================
-- SCHEMA ADDITIONS — Group 1 features (run after the base schema above)
-- Safe to re-run: all wrapped in IF NOT EXISTS checks.
-- ============================================================================

-- Feature 1: store vibe_key on digital_sends for personalised card generation
-- Feature 4: store sender_phone, opened_at, gift_url, reaction fields
-- Feature 3: store ref (gift_reply source tracking) on orders

DO $$ BEGIN
  -- digital_sends additions
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='digital_sends' AND column_name='vibe_key') THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends ADD COLUMN vibe_key text;
  END IF;
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='digital_sends' AND column_name='sender_phone') THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends ADD COLUMN sender_phone text;
  END IF;
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='digital_sends' AND column_name='opened_at') THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends ADD COLUMN opened_at timestamptz;
  END IF;
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='digital_sends' AND column_name='gift_url') THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends ADD COLUMN gift_url text;
  END IF;
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='digital_sends' AND column_name='reaction') THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends ADD COLUMN reaction text;
  END IF;
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='digital_sends' AND column_name='reacted_at') THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.digital_sends ADD COLUMN reacted_at timestamptz;
  END IF;

  -- orders additions (reply gift tracking)
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='orders' AND column_name='reply_token') THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD COLUMN reply_token uuid;
  END IF;
  -- BUGFIX: create-cashfree-order.js has inserted a `ref` value on every
  -- order for a while now (gift_reply source tracking, Feature 3 above),
  -- but the ALTER TABLE for it was never actually written here — only the
  -- comment. That's what caused "Could not find the 'ref' column of
  -- 'orders' in the schema cache" at checkout.
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='orders' AND column_name='ref') THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD COLUMN ref text;
  END IF;
END $$;

-- SECURITY: digital_sends no longer allows direct anon SELECT — sender_phone
-- and sender_name must never be queryable by the public anon key, since that
-- key is embedded in client-side JS and would let anyone with a gift UUID
-- pull the real sender's phone number directly via Supabase REST, bypassing
-- the get-gift.js redaction function entirely.
--
-- gift.html now fetches gift data exclusively through the get-gift Netlify
-- function (service-role key, server-side redaction for character_drop).
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "digital_sends_anon_by_id" ON public.digital_sends;
-- No anon SELECT policy is created — anon access to this table is fully revoked.
-- All reads happen server-side via Netlify functions using the service role key.

FILE: supabase\_archive\schema-fix-orders-ref-column.sql

-- FIX: orders.ref column was never created in the database.
--
-- netlify/functions/create-cashfree-order.js has been inserting a `ref`
-- value into every order (source-tracking for gift-reply orders), but the
-- ALTER TABLE statement for that column was accidentally never written —
-- schema.sql only had the comment, not the actual column. Every checkout
-- has been failing with:
--   "Could not find the 'ref' column of 'orders' in the schema cache"
--
-- Run this once against your production Supabase project (SQL Editor),
-- then hit "Reload schema" under Settings → API (or just wait ~60s — Supabase
-- usually picks up new columns automatically via the pg_notify DDL hook,
-- but a manual reload is instant and free).

DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='orders' AND column_name='ref') THEN
    ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD COLUMN ref text;
  END IF;
END $$;

-- Force PostgREST to pick up the new column immediately instead of
-- waiting for its own periodic schema refresh.
NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
